## Prioritized research backlog

This backlog selects twenty-one high-leverage topics from three passes of candidates. The second pass added source discovery and provenance, user simulation, context and memory stress, MCP/tool conformance, provider drift, cost budgets, human trust, multilingual behavior, metamorphic generation, and data governance. A third pass against the best-practice guidance kept the deferred product questions but added four missing validity areas: eval integrity, ecosystem drift, concurrent operations, and offline-to-production validity.

- [ ] **1. Inventory eval data sources and define provenance rules.** Find authoritative troubleshooting guides, executable failure scenarios, realistic applications, incident examples, deterministic analyzers, and security/best-practice rules. Record licenses, revisions, Kubernetes compatibility, extraction method, review status, and permitted use. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **2. Build an AI Assistant failure taxonomy from real incidents.** Separate model-quality failures, Headlamp/runtime defects, provider/tool failures, safety incidents, and invalid eval runs. Mine bug regressions first, then privacy-reviewed support cases and production traces. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **3. Construct a Kubernetes scenario coverage model.** Define incident families, severities, resource relationships, telemetry needs, permissions, cluster scale, operators, and user skill levels; map every source and fixture to it and identify blind spots. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **4. Create an expert-labeled RCA gold set.** Record causal facts, required and contradictory evidence, acceptable alternative diagnoses, safe repairs, abstention conditions, and prohibited actions. Measure expert agreement before calibrating automated graders. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **5. Validate and calibrate the grader stack.** Compare deterministic checks, rubric judges, pairwise judges, and expert labels. Quantify false passes, false failures, agreement, position/style bias, prompt-injection resistance, and sensitivity to judge changes. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **6. Define evidence-grounding and causal-quality measures.** Score whether the assistant retrieved authoritative evidence, linked cause to symptom, ruled out alternatives, cited fresh observations, and distinguished root cause from visible status. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **7. Evaluate safety, cluster-analysis policy, and data handling end to end.** Cover destructive actions, approval scope, RBAC, prompt injection, secret exposure, image and manifest hygiene, security posture, excessive mutation, rollback, and refusal quality. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **8. Choose a realistic, maintainable fixture strategy.** Benchmark recorded APIs, scripted sessions, KWOK, Kind, vCluster, realistic demo applications, and chaos injection for fidelity, isolation, setup validity, cleanup reliability, telemetry, and cost. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **9. Evaluate multi-turn, tool/MCP, and provider behavior.** Test clarification, context degradation, malformed tool results, argument/schema fidelity, approval continuation, provider-specific message constraints, fallback behavior, and model snapshot drift. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **10. Design the production feedback loop and statistical release policy.** Research privacy-preserving trace sampling, user feedback, incident promotion, paired baselines, trial counts, uncertainty, minimum practical regressions, severity-weighted gates, and rollback criteria. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **11. Identify existing benchmarks for Kubernetes AI and SRE agents.** Find public benchmarks, eval suites, and leaderboards for Kubernetes troubleshooting, diagnosis, remediation, preventive analysis, and SRE/DevOps agents operating on Kubernetes. Compare their task sources, cluster or simulator fidelity, supported tools and agents, reference labels and graders, safety coverage, holdout and contamination controls, metrics, reproducibility, licensing, maintenance, and published results; identify reusable cases and uncovered requirements. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **12. Model user personas and multi-turn interaction at scale.** Define realistic novice, expert, hurried, mistaken, underspecified, and adversarial operator behaviors; compare scripted, model-simulated, and human users; validate simulators against real interaction traces; and measure clarification quality, recovery from bad assumptions, escalation, and task completion without treating a simulator's preferences as user truth. This extends Research 9 with a reusable interaction-test method rather than a separate answer-quality score. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **13. Evaluate speed, cost, energy, capacity, and correctness tradeoffs.** Measure time to first useful evidence, time to diagnosis and recovery, p50/p95 end-to-end latency, tool and model concurrency, token and infrastructure cost, timeout/censoring behavior, cache effects, and correctness under realistic cluster sizes and provider limits. Report Pareto frontiers rather than one blended score: faster or cheaper is useful only at an explicit change in RCA, safety, and recovery quality. Measure local power and hardware utilization where possible; for hosted models, label provider-reported or model-based energy and carbon figures as estimates, record their assumptions and uncertainty, and avoid false per-request precision. Define budgets by task severity and workflow, including energy and cost per successful safe task, instead of optimizing one global average. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **14. Study operator trust, reliance, and handoff.** Run controlled studies of calibrated confidence, evidence presentation, approval wording, uncertainty, correction, and escalation. Measure appropriate reliance, error detection, time to safe decision, automation bias, trust repair after failure, and whether operators can reconstruct what the agent observed and changed; do not use satisfaction alone as evidence of correctness or safety. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **15. Add multilingual, localization, and accessibility slices.** Test equivalent incidents across supported languages, locale-specific terminology, right-to-left presentation, screen-reader and keyboard workflows, cognitive load, color-independent status communication, and language switching during a session. Treat these as stratified slices over the same gold facts and hard outcomes, with native-speaker and accessibility review, rather than isolated benchmark programs. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **16. Develop metamorphic and compositional scenario generation.** Define semantics-preserving transformations such as resource renaming, namespace relocation, irrelevant-object injection, message paraphrase, telemetry reordering, and equivalent API representations, plus controlled fault composition. Verify invariants with Kubernetes oracles and expert review, then use paired results to detect shortcut learning, brittle prompts, positional bias, and failures that emerge only from interacting faults. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **17. Design portable eval-platform and observability integration.** Map the canonical scenario, trajectory, grader, and result schemas to OpenTelemetry and optional sinks such as Braintrust, LangSmith, MLflow, or cloud eval services. Evaluate round-trip fidelity, redaction, artifact retention, offline/local execution, cost, rate limits, schema evolution, and vendor exit. Keep execution truth and release gates in repository-owned artifacts rather than a hosted dashboard. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **18. Secure the eval system against leakage and gaming.** Threat-model candidate access to labels, setup scripts, fixture names, grader prompts, expert trajectories, shared caches, network sources, and prior-run artifacts. Add canaries, unavailable-agent and known-bad controls, contamination records, judge-injection tests, reward-hacking probes, least-privilege execution, and auditable invalidation rules so benchmark success cannot be manufactured by reading or steering the measurement system. **Status: started below.**
- [ ] **19. - [ ] **20. - [ ] **21. Validate offline evals against deployment outcomes.** Research whether benchmark and shadow-mode results predict expert judgments, support resolution, safe escalation, incident duration, rollback, and production failure classes. Use privacy-reviewed observational studies and staged experiments, monitor distribution shift and missing populations, and revise or retire metrics that improve offline without improving operator or system outcomes. **Status: started below.**

Treat Research 18, 19, and 21 as the highest-priority validity programs after the initial framework: they determine whether results are trustworthy, remain meaningful as the ecosystem changes, and predict deployment outcomes. Research 12, 13, 14, and 20 are product and operational studies that reuse the core scenario and trajectory contracts. Research 15 is a required slice across representative scenarios, Research 16 is a scenario-generation and robustness method, and Research 17 is infrastructure integration after the repository-owned formats stabilize. This structure avoids ten disconnected scorecards while keeping each research question and owner explicit.

#### Citation convention

Topic-scoped citations such as [R7-1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14470v2) appear at the point of the claim. The prefix identifies the research topic, not a global bibliography order. Each completed topic's **source and evidence ledger** then states what the cited source supports and, equally importantly, what it does not establish for Headlamp. Clickable source names in tables are also citations; uncited normative language such as “should,” “recommend,” or “proposed” is Headlamp-specific synthesis unless the sentence says otherwise.

### Research 1: data sources, scenario guidance, and provenance

#### Research method and scope

The primary hypothesis is: **a source-derived eval case is admissible only when an independent reviewer can reconstruct the exact source material and reuse basis, reproduce the intended healthy/fault behavior and oracle on a declared environment, and verify that the candidate cannot observe hidden derivation or gold artifacts; source reputation or a high heuristic score cannot substitute for those checks**. The cheapest falsification is to give a second reviewer only the acquisition record for one documentation-derived case and one executable upstream case. If either reviewer cannot recover the same bytes and license evidence, reproduce the declared state transition, or reach the same admission decision without the upstream answer wording, the current provenance protocol is insufficient.

The source search was refreshed on September 6, 2026. Search families included `Kubernetes troubleshooting documentation examples`, `Kubernetes test failure regression`, `Kubernetes AI benchmark fixture`, `Kubernetes operator analyzer`, `Kubernetes postmortem incident`, `cloud native demo fault injection`, `dataset provenance metadata`, `research software licensing provenance`, `scoping review search reporting`, and backward citation chaining from included methods. Searches covered official Kubernetes and tool documentation, GitHub repositories/issues/releases, Crossref/DOI metadata, standards bodies, and references from included sources. This is a structured scoping and source-qualification study, not an exhaustive systematic review of every repository or private incident corpus.

PRISMA-ScR motivates transparent objectives, eligibility, source selection, charting, and result flow for scoping reviews [R1-2](https://doi.org/10.7326/M18-0850), while PRISMA-S makes search sources, dates, queries, limits, deduplication, and reproducibility explicit [R1-3](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13643-020-01542-z). They are healthcare-oriented reporting guidelines, so Topic 1 uses their auditable practices by analogy and does not claim PRISMA compliance. Wohlin's software-engineering guidance supports iterative backward/forward snowballing with recorded start sets and stopping decisions [R1-4](https://doi.org/10.1145/2601248.2601268); citation chaining supplements rather than proves search completeness.

Include a source when it supplies at least one inspectable contribution: authoritative Kubernetes behavior, an executable setup/fault/cleanup lifecycle, operator-observable evidence, an independent assertion or regression test, a realistic application graph, a security/policy rule, or a concrete incident causal chain. Exclude or quarantine sources that are inaccessible, mutable without a retrievable snapshot, promotional without methods, answer-only without evidence, irreducibly unsafe/private, duplicate without added evidence, or unusable under the intended reuse basis. Record every screened source and one primary exclusion reason; absence from the final inventory means “not qualified in this search,” not “does not exist.”

Future refreshes must publish `discovered → deduplicated → retrieved → screened → rights-reviewed → behavior-reviewed → admitted` counts and stable exclusion codes. The earlier scouting that produced the current inventory did not retain a complete machine-readable query/result and exclusion log, so this revision cannot reconstruct those historical flow counts. Treat the present list as a qualified start set and run the recorded protocol prospectively before claiming search yield, saturation, or comparative source coverage.

Research questions:

1. Which source classes contribute scenario seeds, healthy baselines, faults, observations, causal gold, deterministic outcomes, policies, or counterexamples without one source silently supplying every layer?
2. Can another reviewer recover the exact source fragment, its revision, retrieval path, license evidence, notices, and transformation lineage after links or branches move?
3. Does the intended reuse copy expressive material, transform code/configuration, or retain only independently verified facts, and who approved that classification?
4. Does the derived case reproduce on every declared Kubernetes, operator, CRD, architecture, and dependency combination, including setup, readiness, fault manifestation, recovery, and cleanup?
5. Is the oracle independent of the candidate and upstream answer wording, and does it reject healthy, insufficient-evidence, wrong-cause, and lucky-repair controls?
6. Which source or environment changes trigger revalidation, migration, claim narrowing, quarantine, or retirement?
7. How much coverage and unique failure information does each admitted source add after family deduplication, rather than how many files or repositories were collected?

#### Evidence classes and claim limits

No source class is automatically authoritative for every claim:

| Evidence class                       | Appropriate contribution                                                                                        | Claim limit                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Normative standard or project policy | Licensing terms, API/deprecation/version policy, metadata vocabulary, or required process                       | Establishes the document's rule and scope, not that a fixture complies or behaves correctly                                                        |
| Pinned source and accepted test      | Exact implementation, assertion, regression condition, or license/notice state at one revision                  | A test can encode a bug or narrow environment; repository-root terms may not cover vendored, linked, generated, or separately licensed material    |
| Reproduced live behavior             | Healthy/fault transition, observations, outcome, recovery, cleanup, and compatibility on a captured environment | One environment/run does not establish portability, realism, causal explanation, or future behavior                                                |
| Analyzer, benchmark, or chaos case   | Candidate seed, fault mechanism, expected finding, verifier, or taxonomy                                        | Its own output is not an independent gold standard, and public identifiers/answers can leak                                                        |
| Documentation or runbook             | Intended semantics, investigation order, known alternatives, and human-readable remediation                     | Examples may be simplified, stale, non-executable, or incomplete for a target cluster                                                              |
| Issue, postmortem, or support report | Product intent, incident hypothesis, symptom/evidence vocabulary, and realistic contributing conditions         | Report state, popularity, or asserted root cause is not accepted behavior, reuse permission, reproducibility, or proof that a reduced fixture fits |

W3C PROV-DM distinguishes entities, activities, agents, derivations, generations, and invalidations [R1-5](https://www.w3.org/TR/2013/REC-prov-dm-20130430/). Apply that graph in the evaluator-owned registry rather than storing one `source_url`: source snapshot → selected fragment → extraction activity → healthy baseline/fault transformation → candidate-view and evaluator-view artifacts, with responsible agents and timestamps at every activity. The candidate receives only the compiled candidate-view artifact and declared tools, never the provenance graph or evaluator-side identities. FAIR makes findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reuse separate properties [R1-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18), and DataCite 4.6 provides versioned metadata and related-identifier patterns for research outputs [R1-7](https://schema.datacite.org/meta/kernel-4.6/). Neither FAIRness nor a persistent identifier establishes correctness, permission, privacy, or availability forever.

Datasheets for Datasets motivates recording motivation, composition, collection, preprocessing, uses, distribution, and maintenance [R1-8](https://doi.org/10.1145/3458723). Use those questions for the corpus card, but keep executable per-case provenance: documentation alone cannot recover missing bytes or prove a case's behavior.

#### Headlamp issue #1374 as design input

[R1-1: Headlamp #1374, “Cluster Analysis Information and best practices”](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/headlamp/issues/1374), describes the operator job more broadly than incident RCA: analyze a running cluster for image currency, security policy, container and Helm-chart security, Kubernetes and container best practices, troubleshooting signals, and operational health. It points to server-side dry-run validation, K8sGPT, KubeLinter, kube-score, Kubeconform, chart-testing, klint, Kubevious, and kube-hunter as possible analysis ingredients.

The issue suggests two eval tracks:

1. **Incident troubleshooting:** explain why a workload is unhealthy, collect distinguishing evidence, and recommend or perform a scoped repair.
2. **Preventive cluster analysis:** find material risks in otherwise functioning resources, explain their impact and confidence, prioritize actionable findings, and avoid presenting every opinionated linter warning as an incident.

This distinction matters for grading. A schema violation or failed server-side dry run can be a deterministic error. A missing resource limit, `latest` image tag, or absent NetworkPolicy is usually a policy finding whose severity depends on workload context and organizational policy. Preventive findings should therefore record the rule source, version, applicability, severity, evidence, exception policy, and remediation rather than being folded into the RCA pass rate.

The issue was opened in September 2023, moved onto a Headlamp roadmap in 2024, auto-closed as `not planned` after inactivity on May 31, 2025, and then added to the Kubernetes SIGs Headlamp release-plan project and queued in June 2025. There is no assignee, milestone, linked implementation, or maintainer discussion accepting a design. Treat it as valuable product intent and source discovery, not a committed roadmap or completed feature.

#### Source-selection rule

Do not scrape repositories into prompts and call the result an eval dataset. Build each case from independently reviewable layers:

- **Scenario seed:** an incident, task, test, guide, analyzer case, or controlled fault.
- **Healthy baseline:** pinned deployable resources and explicit readiness checks.
- **Fault transformation:** the smallest intentional change that creates the symptom.
- **Gold evidence:** Kubernetes/API facts that distinguish the cause from alternatives.
- **Oracle:** deterministic postconditions plus expert-reviewed semantic criteria.
- **Provenance:** source URL, immutable revision, source and derived-artifact licenses, attribution, transformation notes, Kubernetes/operator versions, reviewer, and review date.

Whenever practical, derive the fault from one source and validate its expected behavior against another. This reduces circular evaluation, such as using a linter's own fixture and output as both the generated task and unquestioned gold answer.

Apply hard gates before heuristic ranking:

| Gate                      | Required evidence                                                                                                                                                     | Failure disposition                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Identity and retrieval    | Canonical source, immutable revision/release, exact paths, source-fragment digest, retrieval method/tool, timestamp, and retained or approved archival path           | `source_unresolvable`; discovery only until exact material is recoverable                        |
| Rights and permitted use  | File/scope-specific license evidence, copyright/attribution and notice files, intended use, copied-versus-factual classification, restrictions, and qualified review  | `rights_unresolved`; do not copy or distribute; independently re-author facts only when approved |
| Reproducible behavior     | Pinned setup, readiness, fault, evidence, recovery, cleanup, dependencies, declared repetitions, and observed failure rate on every supported environment             | `behavior_unconfirmed`; taxonomy/authoring seed only                                             |
| Independent oracle        | Cause/outcomes established from Kubernetes/application semantics, live observations, or separately authored expert evidence; positive, negative, and healthy controls | `oracle_circular`; never use the candidate's or seed source's assertion as unquestioned truth    |
| Safety and isolation      | Bounded permissions/targets, synthetic data/secrets, cleanup/rollback, escaped-effect checks, and no dependence on uncontrolled destructive infrastructure            | `unsafe_fixture`; quarantine                                                                     |
| Candidate-view separation | Generated-view inventory and scan proving source names, setup/fault code, answers, rubrics, verifiers, hidden objects, and provenance graph are inaccessible          | `candidate_leakage`; invalidate affected cases and results                                       |
| Compatibility             | Exact Kubernetes/client/operator/CRD versions, feature gates, architecture, images, registries, network/telemetry dependencies, and tested/supported matrix           | `compatibility_unqualified`; restrict the claim or requalify                                     |
| Independent review        | Distinct author plus behavior and rights reviewers, conflicts, evidence-linked decision, review date, expiry, and revalidation triggers                               | `review_incomplete`; cannot enter a scored split                                                 |

“Public on GitHub” is not a reuse classification. GitHub notes that without a license default copyright applies and public users receive only the platform rights to view and fork [R1-10](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/licensing-a-repository). Record machine-readable SPDX license expressions where possible [R1-9](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/), but inspect the exact file, path scope, notices, dependencies, embedded assets, and intended use. CC BY 4.0 requires retained attribution/license information and modification indication when licensed material is shared [R1-11](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode.en); Apache-2.0 redistribution requires the license, modified-file notices, retained applicable notices, and NOTICE handling when present [R1-12](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). These are source texts, not project-specific legal advice; unresolved cases require qualified review.

#### Source qualification and acquisition record

Score a candidate before importing it. Use five dimensions, each from 0 to 2:

- **Reproducibility:** narrative only; partial setup; or pinned setup, readiness, fault, and cleanup.
- **Evidence quality:** asserted cause only; useful observations; or structured observations that distinguish alternatives.
- **Oracle independence:** source supplies its own answer; answer can be cross-checked; or separate authoritative behavior and expert review are available.
- **Maintenance:** abandoned or highly environment-specific; maintainable with manual work; or actively versioned with stable automation.
- **Reuse clarity:** missing or source-by-source terms; identified license with unresolved embedded material; or verified license and attribution path for the exact imported artifacts.

The total ranks only sources that pass the hard gates; it cannot compensate for a failed gate. The current `7/10` boundary is a provisional work-queue heuristic, not a validated admission threshold. Before retaining it, have independent reviewers score a stratified sample, report item-level disagreement and adjudication, and compare review workload and useful-case yield at adjacent thresholds. A case scoring at least `7/10` remains a candidate until its complete case contract passes; lower-scoring sources remain eligible for taxonomy or scenario discovery when rights and privacy permit.

| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------: | -------: | -----------------: | ----------: | ----: | ------------: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Kubernetes English docs plus examples             |               2 |        2 |                  2 |           2 |     2 |         10/10 | Candidate for selected manifests and factual claims. The inspected snapshot's root license is CC BY 4.0 [R1-17](https://github.com/kubernetes/website/tree/079ac780d512ab01d905e65dc622bfe38b94e6da); still inspect file scope/embedded material and satisfy attribution/change requirements. |

The inspected root license is Apache-2.0 [R1-18](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/b2ec8b6fefac451a2dedafc4dd71f2f16c7a6abe); record exact test path/commit and applicable notices.                         |

Apache-2.0 was verified at the inspected snapshot [R1-20](https://github.com/gke-labs/k8s-ai-bench/tree/ac9ac9c4c4d975a4737f2f55b8d3e363320d3f52); inspect each task's dependencies/notices.                                   |

Create one append-only acquisition record for every screened source fragment. A decision may be superseded, but the old record and reason remain addressable:

```yaml
schema_version: <version>
record_id: <stable-id>
status: <discovered|screened|qualified|discovery-only|quarantined|retired>
source:
  kind: <documentation|test|fixture|incident|analyzer|policy>
  title: <title>
  owner_or_authors: [<identity>]
  repository: kubernetes/website
  revision: <40-character-commit>
  paths:
    - content/en/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/assign-cpu-resource.md
    - content/en/examples/pods/resource/cpu-request-limit-2.yaml
  upstream_url: <canonical-page-or-issue>
  retrieved_at: <ISO-8601>
  retrieval: { tool: <name>, version: <version>, command_digest: <sha256> }
  fragment_digests: { <path>: <sha256> }
rights:
  source_license_expression: CC-BY-4.0
  license_evidence: { url: <immutable-url>, digest: <sha256>, scope: <paths> }
  notices: [<path-and-digest>]
  attribution: <required-attribution>
  intended_uses: [evaluation, redistribution]
  copied_or_factual: <copied|transformed|facts-only>
  restrictions_or_exceptions: [<item>]
  reviewer: <identity>
derivation:
  use: scenario-seed
  copied_content: [manifest]
  parent_fragment_digests: [<sha256>]
  tool: { name: <name>, version: <version>, config_digest: <sha256> }
  transformations: [neutral-names, pinned-image-digest, deterministic-cpu-request]
  excluded_content: [upstream-explanation, expected-answer-wording]
  derived_artifact_digests: { <path>: <sha256> }
compatibility:
  kubernetes_server: [<tested-versions>]
  kubectl: <version>
  platform_architecture: [kind-amd64]
  operators_crds_feature_gates: [<identity>]
  images_charts_registries: [<digest-or-version>]
validation:
  healthy_readiness: <check-digest>
  fault_manifestation: <check-digest>
  oracle: <check-or-rubric-digest>
  recovery_cleanup: <check-digest>
  repetitions_and_results: <artifact-digest>
visibility:
  candidate_view_digest: <sha256>
  evaluator_view_digest: <sha256>
  leakage_scan: <tool-version-and-result>
review:
  author: <identity>
  behavior_reviewer: <identity>
  rights_reviewer: <identity>
  decision: <qualified|discovery-only|quarantined|retired>
  reasons: [<evidence-linked-reason>]
  reviewed_at: <ISO-8601>
  revalidate_on: [date, upstream-release, dependency-change, failed-sentinel]
```

The registry should separately hash copied fragments, generated files, candidate/evaluator views, and the final derived fixture. A moving branch URL is useful for discovery but is not provenance. Dependency images, Helm charts, vulnerability databases, CRDs, extraction tools, and configuration also need immutable identities even when the top-level repository is pinned. SLSA's verification pattern checks artifact subject digest, signature, trusted builder, canonical source, build type, and external parameters [R1-16](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/verifying-artifacts); adapt those checks where attestations exist, but do not treat provenance as proof of correctness, benign behavior, complete dependencies, or valid licensing.

Compatibility is a claim over a matrix, not a `minimum` string. Record actual server, client, kubelet, operator, API, feature-gate, architecture, and dependency cells tested. Kubernetes publishes component skew constraints [R1-13](https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/) and separate API deprecation guarantees by stability level [R1-14](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/); neither guarantees third-party CRD, webhook, image, or application compatibility. A failed unsupported cell is `not_applicable` only if excluded before execution; an undeclared or unexpectedly failing supported cell invalidates that case result. Topic 1 qualifies a source/case only for its declared cells; Topic 19 owns the cross-version support matrix, migration policy, and candidate-versus-environment attribution.

#### Concrete Kubernetes starter cases

The four documentation-derived cases in the first tranche can now be made specific:

| Case                             | Seed and fault                                                                                                                                                                    | Candidate-visible evidence                                                                                                          | Hidden verifier and semantic gold                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Main distractors and portability                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pod requests impossible CPU      | Start from `content/en/examples/pods/resource/cpu-request-limit-2.yaml`; set the request above the largest node's allocatable CPU rather than relying on incidental cluster load. | Pod remains unbound; `PodScheduled=False`; scheduler event has reason `FailedScheduling`; node allocatable values and Pod requests. | Assert no `spec.nodeName`, `PodScheduled=False`, reason `Unschedulable`, and a message containing insufficient CPU. The RCA must compare request with allocatable capacity and not merely say “Pending”; `test/integration/util/util.go` supplies the structured condition pattern.     | Include irrelevant image and readiness details. Run on a cluster whose largest allocatable CPU is measured during setup; derive the request from it.  |
| Nonexistent image                | Use a tiny Pod with an intentionally nonexistent tag under a controlled registry namespace; keep credentials absent by design and pin all other images by digest.                 | Container waiting reason transitions through `ErrImagePull` or `ImagePullBackOff`; pull events contain the failed image reference.  | Accept either documented transient waiting reason, then require `ImagePullBackOff` within the timeout. The RCA must identify the bad image reference and distinguish it from missing pull credentials; `test/e2e/common/node/runtime.go` demonstrates the accepted reason set.          | Add an unrelated Secret and healthy sibling Pod. Avoid depending on a public registry outage or an architecture-specific image.                       |
| Service selector selects no Pods | Deploy healthy serving Pods and a Service, then alter one selector value so no Pod labels match. Keep Service DNS and ports valid.                                                | Pods are Ready and directly reachable; Service exists and resolves; its EndpointSlice has no endpoints; selector and labels differ. | Assert zero ready EndpointSlice endpoints before repair and the expected count after the selector is restored. The RCA must name the mismatched key/value and rule out DNS, Pod health, and `targetPort`; the service-debugging guide defines this diagnostic ordering.                 | Include a valid named `targetPort` and a second unrelated Service. Requires EndpointSlice-based checks because the older Endpoints API is deprecated. |
| Required ConfigMap volume absent | Deploy a Pod that references a nonexistent, non-optional ConfigMap volume; use an image already preloaded into the test cluster so image pulling cannot become the cause.         | Pod is scheduled but does not start; volume setup events identify the missing ConfigMap; expected Pod conditions remain incomplete. | Assert the Pod is scheduled, no app container has started, and the referenced ConfigMap is absent. The RCA must identify the exact volume reference and avoid recommending image or scheduler changes; `test/e2e_node/pod_conditions_test.go` provides independent condition semantics. | Add an existing unrelated ConfigMap with a similar name. This needs a real kubelet, so it is suitable for Kind but not an API-only recorded fixture.  |

For every case, create a healthy twin with the same prompt and irrelevant resources. Healthy twins catch assistants that diagnose from scenario shape or fixture names instead of current evidence. The fault overlay, hidden cause, semantic rubric, and repair patch must never be delivered through the candidate's tool surface.

This pass inspected artifacts at the following branch tips. These revisions are a reproducible research snapshot, not automatic approval to import every referenced file:

The four `k8s-ai-bench` repair candidates are sufficiently concrete to prototype. Import the setup intent, not the answer-bearing directory or resource names, and require an RCA before exposing mutation tools:

| Derived case           | Upstream task and evidence                                        | Headlamp hard verifier                                                                                                                                                   | Admission notes                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Pending Pod and PVC    | `tasks/fix-pending-pod/{task.yaml,setup.sh,verify.sh,cleanup.sh}` | PVC becomes `Bound`, Pod becomes `Ready`, the original Pod/PVC identities remain, and no unrelated StorageClass, PV, or namespace changes occur.                         | Admit after replacing `homepage-*` names. The upstream verifier establishes recovery; add a rubric requiring the storage binding cause before repair.                    |
| Crash-looping workload | `tasks/fix-crashloop/{task.yaml,setup.sh,verify.sh,cleanup.sh}`   | Deployment reaches observed generation and available replicas; replacement Pods stay Ready through a stability window; only the faulty container command/config changes. | Admit provisionally. Re-run setup and verifier on the pinned Kind version because the cleanup script is less defensive and the generic prompt leaks the target identity. |
| Image pull failure     | `tasks/fix-image-pull/{task.yaml,setup.sh,verify.sh,cleanup.sh}`  | Correct image digest is deployed, observed generation catches up, all replicas are Ready, and image-pull Secrets and unrelated workloads are unchanged.                  | Admit after pinning a reachable replacement digest and preloading it. The semantic rubric must distinguish a bad reference from registry credentials or outage.          |
| Broken health probes   | `tasks/fix-probes/{task.yaml,setup.sh,verify.sh,cleanup.sh}`      | Deployment is available, readiness and liveness endpoints succeed repeatedly, probe timing stays inside an allowlist, and no probe is merely removed.                    | Admit after reconciling the prompt's `orders` namespace with cleanup's `health-check` namespace. A setup smoke check must prove the intended mismatch before the run.    |

Do not use the generated Gatekeeper tasks as substitutes for these runtime repairs. Their `alpha-*` and `beta-*` artifacts, `constraint.yaml`, `template.yaml`, `suite.yaml`, and `gator verify` flow are valuable for the six preventive-analysis cases, but they inherit the policy library's opinionated semantics. The `container-image-must-have-digest`, `required-probes`, `pod-disruption-budget`, and narrowly scoped resource/RBAC constraints are candidate seeds only after a human reviews both compliant and violating examples.

K8sGPT provides four strong edge-case definitions for paired controls. Recreate each pair as ordinary Kubernetes resources and use live API behavior as the oracle; do not run K8sGPT during grading or copy its expected message into the candidate-visible fixture:

| Pair                        | Upstream test cases                                               | Broken and healthy forms                                                                                                                           | Independent oracle and false-positive control                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pod readiness evidence      | `pkg/analyzer/pod_test.go`                                        | A Running but unready Pod with an `Unhealthy` warning event versus the same transient state without an event.                                      | The broken case requires repeated failed readiness probes plus a current event; the no-event form must not be called a proven probe failure. This directly tests evidence-sensitive abstention. |
| Service endpoint selection  | `pkg/analyzer/service_test.go`                                    | A selector-backed Service with an empty EndpointSlice versus leader-election endpoints or a Service whose selected Pods become Ready.              | Query EndpointSlices and selected Pod labels directly. Suppress leader-election records and do not infer a broken Service merely from an empty legacy Endpoints object.                         |
| PVC provisioning            | `pkg/analyzer/pvc_test.go`                                        | A Pending PVC with a current `ProvisioningFailed` event versus Bound, eventless Pending, and Pending with a different event reason.                | Require the claim phase, involved object, reason, and latest relevant event to agree. The eventless case should produce uncertainty, not a fabricated storage-class cause.                      |
| Deployment rollout progress | `pkg/analyzer/deployment_test.go` plus issues `#1742` and `#1743` | A stalled rollout whose observed generation has caught up versus an unreconciled or progressing rollout with temporarily fewer available replicas. | Gate failure on observed generation, progress conditions, and a deadline/stability window. Raw desired-versus-ready inequality is explicitly insufficient and is a known false-positive risk.   |

The OpenTelemetry cases also need one terminology correction and an explicit scheduled-suite contract:

| Case                        | Exact mechanism and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Deterministic checks and recovery                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cart failed readiness       | Set `failedReadinessProbe=on` in `src/flagd/demo.flagd.json`. `src/cart/src/services/HealthCheckService.cs` returns `Unhealthy("connection failed")`; Kubernetes readiness removes endpoints.                                   | Drive steady cart traffic, require cart containers to remain Running while readiness fails and ready endpoints fall, and require traces to localize failures to cart. Reset the flag and prove endpoints and requests recover.                                                           |
| Recommendation cache growth | Set `recommendationCacheFailure=on`. `src/recommendation/recommendation_server.py` repeatedly appends catalog IDs and another quarter of the accumulated cache on misses, while spans expose cache hit/miss and product counts. | Rename the proposed case from “memory leak” to “recommendation cache growth” unless process-memory growth is independently measured. Use deterministic recommendation traffic, assert monotonic cache/product-count evidence plus bounded RSS growth, reset/restart, and prove recovery. |

The second case is not merely a generic cache failure: the inspected implementation does retain and amplify `cached_ids`, so it is a valid memory-growth seed. However, random cache hits make wall-clock detection flaky. Use a fixed random seed or a minimum number of observed misses, and grade the causal chain from flag evaluation to cache miss, list amplification, process memory pressure, and downstream symptom. The demo's telemetry-test pattern is reusable here: drive explicit traffic, then poll Jaeger, Prometheus, and OpenSearch rather than waiting for the load generator's weighted task mix.

HolmesGPT fixture inspection produced useful authoring rules but not four immediately importable cases. `24_misconfigured_pvc` has deterministic `ProvisioningFailed` setup and cleanup, but its expected output only says that the PVC is misconfigured and its source description points to `80_pvc_storage_class_mismatch` for the actual answer. `28_permissions_error` is valuable for partial-evidence and RBAC-denial behavior, while `124_checkout_latency_prometheus` has a strong PromQL setup assertion, but both need a complete independent rubric and Kind portability run. Keep all three in the candidate queue and leave the fourth slot open; admitting weak cases to satisfy the planned count would make the corpus less credible.

The two chaos slots remain gated as well. Select them only after one pinned target application has a healthy baseline and application-level recovery probes. Prefer one Pod/container fault and one network or DNS fault with disjoint evidence. Admission requires target-selector review, proof that the fault became observable, proof that the agent could infer it without seeing the chaos object, rollback completion, restoration of application SLOs, and deletion of every chaos custom resource. Until those checks exist, the tranche has **14 mapped source cases, six category-level preventive cases, three HolmesGPT candidates, and three open slots** (one HolmesGPT and two chaos), not 26 implementation-ready cases.

#### Error and troubleshooting information sources

Repository contents are only one channel. The source registry should support:

- **Upstream issue → fix → regression-test chains:** stronger than an isolated issue because the accepted patch and test clarify the actual cause. Require a reproducible public case and avoid inferring truth from unconfirmed reports.
- **Kubernetes and operator events, conditions, controller logs, and API status:** authoritative observations for a running fixture, but event text is version-sensitive and often describes symptoms rather than causes.
- **Release notes, deprecation guides, and upgrade tests:** useful for version-skew and removed-API cases. Pin both source and target versions.
- **Official troubleshooting guides and runbooks:** useful for investigation steps and alternative hypotheses. Convert procedural advice into evidence criteria rather than requiring one exact trajectory.
- **Security advisories and policy frameworks:** useful for impact and remediation context, but dangerous as static gold because databases and accepted controls change.
- **Headlamp bug regressions, opt-in traces, support reports, and failed manual tests:** closest to the shipped assistant and user distribution. Redact first, record consent and retention, deduplicate, and keep production-derived cases out of candidate-visible development sets.

Public incident collections need a strict holding area. [`hjacobs/kubernetes-failure-stories`](https://github.com/hjacobs/kubernetes-failure-stories) is Kubernetes-specific but its GitHub copy is archived and points to Codeberg; it aggregates stories rather than granting rights to the linked articles. [`danluu/post-mortems`](https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems) is actively curated and includes valuable Kubernetes incidents, but the checked repository page exposes no license and most underlying reports have separate terms. Etsy Morgue and Netflix Dispatch are incident-management software, not public incident datasets; both are archived. Postmortem-template collections are useful for gold-record fields, not causal labels.

An incident may advance from discovery only when all of these are true:

1. The original report is public and permits the intended extraction or only uncopyrightable facts are retained after review.
2. The report provides a concrete causal chain, timestamps, observations, and ruled-out alternatives rather than a single asserted “root cause.”
3. A public fix, regression test, documented invariant, or independent expert can verify the behavior.
4. The incident can be reduced to a safe fixture without proprietary infrastructure, personal data, real secrets, or destructive scale.
5. The resulting case does not expose source-specific names or phrasing that let a model recall the report instead of investigating the cluster.

The most promising narratives are version-skew, service-routing, DNS, admission, resource-exhaustion, and rollout incidents that map to ordinary Kubernetes resources. Large provider control-plane outages, hardware failures, and organization-specific cascading failures are better used to expand the taxonomy and distractor design than as executable first-tranche cases.

#### Recommended first source tranche

Start with a deliberately small, reviewable import rather than bulk generation:

1. Derive four read-only RCA cases from Kubernetes documentation plus matching upstream status/controller tests.
2. Adapt four HolmesGPT investigation cases and four k8s-ai-bench repair cases, with independent Headlamp rubrics and verifiers.
3. Add four K8sGPT positive/negative analyzer pairs as healthy-versus-broken controls.
4. Build two OpenTelemetry Demo scheduled cases: failed readiness and recommendation-cache growth with measured memory impact.
5. Add two Chaos Mesh or Litmus faults against one pinned demo application, proving setup, observation, recovery, and cleanup.
6. Add six #1374 preventive cases: schema-invalid, failed server-side dry run, unpinned image, excessive privilege, missing resilience control, and one policy finding that should be suppressed due to documented context.

This targets **26 executable case variants**, not 22 and not 26 independent causal families, with different provenance and oracle types: $4+4+4+4+2+2+6=26$. Topic 3 owns family/variant/trial identities and the coverage denominator. The fixture-qualification pass above does not yet admit all 26: the count must remain a target until the final HolmesGPT and chaos cases pass setup, oracle, cleanup, compatibility, and license review, and the six preventive categories become complete case contracts. Before implementation, verify each repository and copied artifact's license at the pinned revision; preserve notices and attribution; record whether the derived case copies expressive content, transforms code/configuration, or only uses factual behavior. A public GitHub repository is not automatically unrestricted training or benchmark data.

#### Failure ownership and invalidity

Preserve the first invalidating layer rather than reporting a candidate failure:

- `search_record_incomplete`: source, query/date, screening decision, duplicate relation, or exclusion reason is missing;
- `source_unresolvable`: immutable source fragment or recorded digest cannot be retrieved or matched;
- `rights_unresolved`: license scope, notice, attribution, intended use, embedded material, privacy, or review is incomplete;
- `extraction_unreproducible`: recorded tool/configuration cannot regenerate the derived bytes and lineage;
- `behavior_unconfirmed`: healthy, fault, observation, recovery, or cleanup contract does not reproduce within declared bounds;
- `oracle_circular`: expected facts/outcomes depend on the seed source's answer or the candidate under evaluation;
- `compatibility_unqualified`: environment identity is incomplete or a claimed supported cell has not passed;
- `unsafe_fixture`: setup, fault, agent, verifier, or cleanup can exceed the approved target or data boundary;
- `candidate_leakage`: candidate-visible material exposes hidden source identity, transformation, cause, rubric, verifier, or gold;
- `review_conflict`: independent reviewers disagree on a hard gate and adjudication remains open;
- `stale_source`: an expiry or change trigger fired without a completed bridge/revalidation.

These are pre-execution case-admission states. They map to Topic 2's `excluded-invalid-run` if discovered after a run begins and take precedence over candidate-quality attribution; Topic 2 owns later runtime/product/model failure classification, while Topics 18–20 add integrity, compatibility, and concurrency invalidators without erasing the first cause.

Invalid cases produce no candidate score. Keep source-discovery value and failed qualification evidence, but do not repair an invalid case after seeing candidate output and count the same run.

#### Focused pilot

1. Freeze the search log, eligibility rules, extraction form, hard gates, rubric anchors, reviewer roles, supported environment cells, repetition/information target, and practical setup/oracle/cleanup error margins before qualification results.
2. Select two heterogeneous seeds already specified above: impossible CPU request from Kubernetes documentation plus independent scheduler semantics, and one `k8s-ai-bench` PVC/probe lifecycle. Qualify causal gold and reviewer independence through Topic 4's reference-standard process rather than letting the source adopter self-certify it. Keep a rejected/no-license narrative source as a negative rights control.
3. Have a second reviewer reconstruct each exact source fragment, license evidence, notices, and derived artifact using only the acquisition record and an empty cache. Compare digests and record every undocumented manual step.
4. Run healthy twin, faulty case, repair, and cleanup for the declared repetitions on each claimed Kubernetes/environment cell. Preserve setup timeouts, retries, transient failures, logs, and unsupported cells rather than rerunning to a clean result.
5. Challenge oracle independence with a wrong-cause/lucky-repair trajectory, an insufficient-evidence trajectory, and source-answer wording removed or paraphrased. The deterministic and expert layers must distinguish outcome recovery from causal/evidence quality.
6. Generate candidate and evaluator views from the same provenance graph. Scan the candidate packet, mounted files, tool responses, logs, environment, and network permissions for source identifiers, fault code, rubric/gold phrases, and verifier artifacts.
7. Have behavior and rights reviewers decide hard gates independently, then adjudicate with evidence links. Report item-level agreement, unresolved conflicts, review time, and threshold sensitivity for the ordinal prioritization score.
8. Mutate one digest, revision, license scope, compatibility cell, oracle dependency, and hidden-file rule. Require each control to produce the correct invalidity state before any candidate model runs.
9. Admit only cases that reconstruct, reproduce, clean up, preserve oracle independence, satisfy the reviewed reuse basis, and reject all injected invalid controls. Keep the original two cases as provenance sentinels for future schema/tool changes.

The pilot validates the protocol, not the realism, family coverage, or ecosystem breadth of a 26-variant corpus. Topic 3 evaluates family coverage and Topic 19 evaluates the support matrix after admission. The Topic 1 pilot succeeds only if both reviewers can reproduce exact lineage and the same evidence-linked gate decision; declared behavior stays within prewritten margins; every supported cell and cleanup is accounted for; candidate/evaluator separation holds; and all invalid controls fail closed. If one case fails, narrow or revise that case/protocol and rerun on a fresh qualification record before scaling acquisition.

#### Counterevidence and limitations

- An official document or accepted upstream test can still be stale, narrowly scoped, or wrong for a third-party distribution; authority and observed behavior remain separate evidence.
- A perfectly reproducible injected fault may be unlike incidents operators actually face. Topic 2 incident evidence and Topic 3 coverage must test realism and population relevance.
- Root repository licenses do not necessarily cover submodules, vendored files, generated artifacts, linked articles, container images, chart dependencies, trademarks, privacy, or database rights. Machine-readable license detection reduces clerical errors but is not legal approval.
- Pinning a commit and hashing bytes gives identity, not durable availability. Retain approved archives where policy permits and test restoration without silently creating a new source of record.
- Public benchmark and fixture exposure raises contamination risk even when names are neutralized. Topic 18 controls determine whether a source can enter development, regression, or holdout splits.
- Independent review is costly and reviewers share assumptions. Preserve disagreement and require domain, legal, or security specialists for claims outside the fixture author's competence rather than treating two signatures as truth.
- Source diversity and case count do not establish incident-family, severity, permission, provider, language, accessibility, or cluster-scale coverage. Topic 3 owns the coverage denominator.
- Deterministic recovery can reward a lucky mutation; causal/evidence gold and prohibited-action checks remain necessary. Conversely, a correct RCA can fail because the environment or verifier is invalid.
- Revalidation cannot guarantee timeless compatibility. Kubernetes, operators, registries, policies, vulnerability databases, and upstream histories change; expiry and sentinel failures must narrow claims until requalified.

| [R1-4](https://doi.org/10.1145/2601248.2601268): Guidelines for snowballing in systematic literature studies                                                                   | Software-engineering guidance for start sets, backward/forward citation chaining, iterations, decisions, and replication                                        | One methodology and replication; snowballing inherits start-set/citation bias and cannot prove complete coverage                                  |
| [R1-5](https://www.w3.org/TR/2013/REC-prov-dm-20130430/): W3C PROV-DM Recommendation                                                                                           | Formal entities, activities, agents, derivation, generation, association, attribution, specialization, and invalidation concepts                                | Generic provenance model; does not choose Headlamp fields, storage, trust roots, licensing decisions, or validity gates                           |
| [R1-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18): FAIR Guiding Principles                                                                                                         | Distinguishes findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable data/metadata with persistent identity and provenance                                           | Principles are aspirational and do not prove correctness, openness, permission, privacy, or durable hosting                                       |
| [R1-7](https://schema.datacite.org/meta/kernel-4.6/): DataCite Metadata Schema 4.6                                                                                             | Versioned schema/documentation for identifiers, creators, publisher, dates, versions, rights, descriptions, funding, and related resources                      | Publication/discovery metadata is not a complete executable case manifest and a DOI does not guarantee behavior or perpetual access               |
| [R1-8](https://doi.org/10.1145/3458723): Datasheets for Datasets                                                                                                               | Documentation questions for motivation, composition, collection, preprocessing, uses, distribution, and maintenance                                             | A datasheet can be incomplete or wrong and cannot replace per-artifact hashes, executable validation, rights review, or hidden-view separation    |
| [R1-9](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/): SPDX Specification 3.0.1                                                                                                     | Versioned machine-readable software/supply-chain model including license expressions, listed licenses, relationships, packages, files, snippets, and provenance | SPDX expression/detection does not decide legal scope, intended-use permission, embedded rights, attribution sufficiency, or compatibility        |
| [R1-10](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/licensing-a-repository): GitHub licensing guidance | States that default copyright applies without a license and public repository platform rights to view/fork do not grant general reproduction/derivative rights  | General platform guidance with an explicit legal-information disclaimer; qualified review remains necessary                                       |
| [R1-11](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode.en): Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International                                                              | Primary license text for sharing/adaptation, attribution, source/license link, retained notices, modification indication, downstream terms, and exclusions      | Applies only to material/licensed rights within scope; does not grant patent/trademark/privacy rights or prove the licensor controls all material |
| [R1-12](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0): Apache License 2.0                                                                                                       | Primary license text for copyright/patent grants and redistribution duties including license copy, modification notices, retained notices, and NOTICE handling  | Scope and third-party/vendored material still require inspection; license compliance does not validate behavior or security                       |
| [R1-13](https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/): Kubernetes version-skew policy                                                                                   | Current supported minor releases and allowed skew among API server, kubelet, kube-proxy, controllers, and kubectl                                               | Moving policy for Kubernetes components; does not establish operator/CRD/application/image compatibility or support old eval cells                |
| [R1-14](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/): Kubernetes deprecation policy                                                                     | Stability-specific API, CLI, feature/behavior, feature-gate, and metric deprecation/removal rules plus warning mechanisms                                       | Policy permits pre-GA churn and exceptions and does not cover every third-party API or arbitrary development commit                               |
| [R1-15](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/api-concepts/#dry-run): Kubernetes API dry-run                                                                          | Server dry-run executes authorization/admission/defaulting/validation/merge without persistence; documents webhook and generated-value constraints              | Does not execute persisted-state/controller/runtime consequences and cannot alone establish deployability, recovery, cleanup, or causal truth     |
| [R1-16](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/verifying-artifacts): SLSA artifact verification                                                                                            | Verification of signature, subject digest, builder trust, canonical source, build type, external parameters, and optional dependencies                          | Provenance depends on trust roots/completeness and does not prove source correctness, benign behavior, licensing, or intended package selection   |
| [R1-17](https://github.com/kubernetes/website/tree/079ac780d512ab01d905e65dc622bfe38b94e6da): Kubernetes website snapshot                                                      | Immutable documentation/example snapshot inspected on 2026-09-06; root license is CC BY 4.0 and paths provide versioned teaching/troubleshooting material       | Root license and commit do not prove each example is executable, current, independently authored, or free of separately scoped material           |
| [R1-18](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/b2ec8b6fefac451a2dedafc4dd71f2f16c7a6abe): Kubernetes source snapshot                                                    | Immutable source/test/API snapshot inspected on 2026-09-06; root license is Apache-2.0 and tests expose machine-checkable behavior                              | Master snapshot is not a supported release; tests may be narrow, privileged, flaky, or unsuitable as user-facing cases                            |
| [R1-19](https://github.com/HolmesGPT/holmesgpt/tree/5e983c17f30e93099c7d775167266d4cd1d586c4): HolmesGPT snapshot                                                              | Pinned investigation-fixture source with setup/cleanup, expected facts, tool requirements, canaries, and multi-source cases; root license verified Apache-2.0   | Public, Holmes-specific cases can leak answers and their expected output is not an independent Headlamp oracle                                    |
