| [R1-21](https://github.com/k8sgpt-ai/k8sgpt/tree/731a6c90749e8e62b9325e41712c39c0d72510c4): K8sGPT snapshot                                                                    | Pinned resource-analyzer/tests supplying positive/negative patterns and broad resource taxonomy; root license verified Apache-2.0                               | One analyzer's rules/messages are implementation opinions and circular if reused as unquestioned gold                                             |
| [R1-22](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo/tree/8c47d47c9ac27710d2b2a153bcd53e483bffe66d): OpenTelemetry Demo snapshot                                       | Pinned realistic microservice, load, telemetry, and switchable-fault source; root license verified Apache-2.0                                                   | Heavy evolving demo whose flags do not by themselves prove process symptoms, root cause, recovery, or portable deterministic execution            |

### Research 2: incident-derived AI Assistant failure taxonomy

A single `failed` label cannot support model selection or product debugging. The local regressions show that the same visible symptom, such as an empty answer or provider `400`, can be caused by model reasoning, message conversion, tool execution, credentials, safety controls, or the test environment. Classify the **outcome**, **failed stage**, and **responsible component** separately; attribution is a conclusion based on evidence, not a property inferred from the final response.

#### Research method and scope

The primary hypothesis is: **a versioned, evidence-bounded multi-axis taxonomy is fit for engineering and evaluation decisions only when blinded independent reviewers can reproduce denominator eligibility, failed stage, routing owner, severity, and leaf-code decisions within prespecified risk-derived disagreement margins; fix descriptions do not materially change pre-fix labels; and a held-out incident stream reaches a declared stability rule without forcing novel evidence into catch-all codes**. The cheapest falsification is a boundary-focused dual-coding set containing valid model failures, malformed Headlamp requests rejected by providers, expected denials, recovered retries, safety near misses, and invalid fixtures. Mask candidate/provider identity and post-event fixes; if reviewers cross a score-denominator, owner, or severe-impact boundary beyond its prewritten margin, or labels change after unmasking the fix, the codebook is not qualified.

The source search was refreshed on September 6, 2026. Search families included `software incident taxonomy development`, `orthogonal defect classification`, `postmortem trigger contributing root cause`, `incident report occurrence defect distinction`, `inter-coder agreement nominal ordinal missing labels`, `taxonomy objective ending conditions`, `AI incident database schema`, `observational incident reporting selection bias`, `privacy incident trace minimization`, and `OpenTelemetry attempt operation error semantics`. Sources were included when they were peer-reviewed methods, normative/government frameworks, durable first-party operational guidance, pinned inspectable schemas, or reproducible local tests/history. Vendor taxonomies without definitions, severity labels without decision anchors, unverified anecdotes, inaccessible schema guesses, and reports without enough evidence to separate symptom from cause were excluded from confirmatory claims.

This is taxonomy design and codebook-validation research, not a prevalence study. Nickerson et al. define iterative conceptual-to-empirical taxonomy development with objective and subjective ending conditions [R2-9](https://doi.org/10.1057/ejis.2012.26). Orthogonal Defect Classification demonstrates the value of classifying defects along distinct dimensions for process feedback [R2-10](https://doi.org/10.1109/32.159420). Both are methods from other software contexts; neither validates Headlamp's axes, labels, severity anchors, or population distribution.

| Evidence class                        | Appropriate use                                                                                                      | Claim limit                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reproduced invariant and intervention | Establish a contract violation, affected stage, observed impact, and whether a controlled change prevents recurrence | A laboratory reproducer does not establish production occurrence, prevalence, affected population, or deepest organizational cause |
| Linked report, fix, and regression    | Triangulate trigger, code defect, resolution, affected versions, and preventive control                              | Accepted fixes and test comments contain hindsight and can be incomplete or wrong; independent reproduction remains stronger       |
| Privacy-reviewed support/trace record | Supply real workflow, impact, reliance, environment, and detection evidence                                          | Selection, consent, telemetry, linkage, retention, and missingness bound generalization; absence of a report is not success        |
| Normative/operational guidance        | Define incident roles, lifecycle fields, risk questions, telemetry semantics, and reporting expectations             | Guidance does not validate a local ontology, severity threshold, causal assignment, or statistical reliability                     |
| Reviewer inference                    | Encode a bounded interpretation with confidence, alternatives, and cited evidence                                    | Agreement is not truth; shared hindsight, codebook ambiguity, and correlated expertise can produce consistent error                |

Research questions:

1. Which units are being counted: source reports, user/eval occurrences, shared defects, derived eval cases, trials, operations, or attempts?
2. Can reviewers distinguish outcome, first failed contract, routing owner, causal roles, severity, retry behavior, and score eligibility without seeing the preferred fix or candidate identity?
3. Which disagreements can change model score denominators, safety escalation, rollback, or engineering ownership, and what uncertainty is acceptable for each decision?
4. Do leaf codes route to distinct preventive actions, owners, tests, or release decisions, or are they decorative synonyms that should be merged?
5. When multiple sufficient causes, feedback, or organizational conditions exist, can the record preserve a causal graph and unresolved alternatives instead of forcing one “root cause”?
6. Does a held-out temporal/channel sample produce new decision-relevant codes, unstable boundaries, or excessive `unknown`/catch-all use after the development taxonomy appears saturated?
7. How do regression tests, public issues, support cases, opt-in traces, and safety reviews differ in evidentiary quality, selection probability, missing populations, privacy constraints, and permissible claims?
8. Which taxonomy changes require a new version, bridge recoding, trend break, gate suspension, or retirement?

#### Unit ontology and denominators

Keep linked units rather than deduplicating them into one row:

| Unit            | Identity and role                                                                                                                 | Counting rule                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source_report` | One test comment, issue, pull request, support ticket, trace, postmortem, reviewer report, or user feedback item                  | Preserve source/channel and duplicate links; several reports can describe one occurrence                          |
| `occurrence`    | One bounded real or eval event with an index time, affected scope, exposure/version, impact, and resolution horizon               | Primary unit for incident/impact rates only when the sampling frame and inclusion probability are known           |
| `defect`        | One evidence-supported violated contract or causal mechanism that can recur across occurrences, providers, symptoms, and versions | Primary unit for engineering backlog/deduplication; never substitute defect count for occurrence prevalence       |
| `eval_case`     | One provenance-reviewed reproduction or synthetic case derived from one or more reports/defects                                   | Primary unit for corpus inventory; Topic 3 owns family/variant coverage and Topic 4 owns causal gold              |
| `trial`         | One candidate × case × environment execution                                                                                      | Primary unit for task scoring after eligibility; repeated trials are not independent incidents                    |
| `operation`     | One logical user-visible action within a trial, such as provider inference, tool call, approval, mutation, verifier, or cleanup   | Carries terminal status and postcondition; an operation can contain several attempts                              |
| `attempt`       | One concrete invocation of an operation                                                                                           | Retain every failed, cancelled, timed-out, and retried attempt; do not promote attempt error rate to task failure |

Relationships are many-to-many: one defect can cause many occurrences; one occurrence can expose several defects; one report can merge occurrences; and one eval case can isolate only part of a production causal chain. Publish separate `N_report`, `N_occurrence`, `N_defect`, `N_case`, `N_trial`, `N_operation`, and `N_attempt` denominators. Deduplicate for the declared estimand only, retain lineage, and never infer frequency from a purposive calibration corpus.

#### Taxonomy contract

Each trial should emit these independent fields:

| Axis                      | Initial values                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Purpose                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Outcome                   | `pass`, `partial`, `incorrect`, `expected-abstention`, `expected-denial`, `cancelled`, `product-error`, `invalid-run`                                                                                                      | Separates task quality from expected control behavior and failures that never produced a valid model trial.                                              |
| Failed stage              | `fixture-setup`, `context-build`, `provider-auth`, `provider-request`, `model-response`, `tool-selection`, `approval`, `tool-execution`, `follow-up`, `rendering`, `semantic-grade`, `hard-verify`, `cleanup`, `reporting` | Locates where the first causal failure occurred. Record later symptoms as contributing events rather than replacing the first failure.                   |
| Primary routing owner     | `model`, `assistant-orchestration`, `headlamp-host`, `provider`, `mcp-tool`, `kubernetes-environment`, `safety-control`, `eval-harness`, `grader`, `unknown`                                                               | Assigns one accountable triage queue without claiming that one component is the sole cause.                                                              |
| Failure mode              | Versioned leaf code such as `reasoning.wrong-cause`, `protocol.orphan-tool-result`, `auth.credential-refresh`, `tool.invalid-arguments`, `safety.secret-disclosure`, `harness.fixture-not-ready`, or `grader.false-pass`   | Enables stable aggregation while retaining a human-readable detail and raw evidence.                                                                     |
| Causal status             | `single-supported-path`, `multiple-supported-paths`, `competing-hypotheses`, `unresolved`                                                                                                                                  | Prevents the routing label from erasing interacting defects, feedback, organizational conditions, or uncertainty.                                        |
| Analysis boundary         | `candidate`, `session`, `plugin`, `provider-or-tool`, `cluster`, `organization-or-process`                                                                                                                                 | States how deep the causal inquiry went; “root” is always relative to this declared boundary.                                                            |
| Score eligibility         | `eligible`, `eligible-with-limited-tools`, `excluded-invalid-run`                                                                                                                                                          | Defines the denominator before aggregate metrics are calculated.                                                                                         |
| Attempt status            | `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `not-run`                                                                                                                                                                              | Preserves transient and recovered failures without converting every failed attempt into a failed operation.                                              |
| Terminal operation status | `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `invalid`                                                                                                                                                                              | States whether the user-visible operation ultimately completed after any allowed retries.                                                                |
| Retry classification      | `non-retryable`, `transient-retryable`, `retryable-after-reset`, `unknown`                                                                                                                                                 | Distinguishes stochastic capability from rate limits, stale credentials, contaminated state, and deterministic defects.                                  |
| Severity                  | `S0`, `S1`, `S2`, `S3`, `S4`, assigned from observed impact dimensions below                                                                                                                                               | Supports severity-weighted release gates without confusing impact with owner, cause, likelihood, or engineering effort.                                  |
| Evidence confidence       | `confirmed`, `probable`, `unresolved` plus evidence references                                                                                                                                                             | `confirmed` requires reproduced intervention/invariant evidence or convergent independent evidence; an accepted fix or test comment alone is `probable`. |

Use one primary routing owner and failure mode for aggregation, plus a separate evidence-linked causal graph and zero or more contributing factors. The routing owner identifies who investigates first; it does not imply a unique or deepest cause. For example, a provider rejects an orphan `tool_result`, but if Headlamp dropped the matching assistant `tool_call`, the routing owner is `assistant-orchestration`, the failed stage is `provider-request`, and the provider rejection is evidence rather than provider ownership. If missing provider diagnostics also delayed detection, preserve that contributing path instead of forcing it under the primary label.

Assign routing ownership from a versioned invariant-to-owner map, not reviewer intuition. Traverse the recorded operation sequence to the earliest evidenced violated contract; if candidate invariants are unordered, share a cause, or cannot be distinguished with the permitted evidence, use `unknown` and preserve all supported hypotheses rather than choosing the most visible downstream component. Reviewer disagreement over routing ownership requires evidence-linked adjudication and remains part of the reliability report.

#### Methodological validation and causal roles

The taxonomy should borrow the structure of established incident practice without claiming that those sources validate Headlamp's particular labels. Google SRE postmortem guidance separates **impact**, **trigger**, **root cause(s)**, **resolution**, **detection**, **timeline**, and **action items**; its incident-response guidance prioritizes mitigation before complete diagnosis ([R2-1](https://sre.google/sre-book/postmortem-culture/), [R2-2](https://sre.google/workbook/incident-response/)). [R2-3: OpenTelemetry error semantics](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/recording-errors/), inspected on September 6, 2026 and explicitly marked **Development**, make error status contextual and say that an error handled by the instrumented operation should not mark the operation failed. [R2-4: NIST AI RMF](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1) supplies the lifecycle requirements: govern ownership, map context and affected parties, measure with documented TEVV, manage risk, and monitor incidents and change. NIST's current cybersecurity incident guide similarly embeds preparation, detection, response, recovery, and continuous improvement in risk management [R2-13](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-61r3). These sources support separate fields and a review process, not one universal AI-assistant incident ontology.

Record these causal roles independently:

| Field                  | Operational definition                                                                                                                                               | Example                                                                                          |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `observed_impact`      | What actually happened to data, resources, users, or the eval; no causal claim.                                                                                      | No answer rendered; one Deployment was mutated outside the requested namespace.                  |
| `trigger`              | The event or condition that exposed or activated the failure.                                                                                                        | A second streamed chunk arrived; credential refresh ran; the provider validated message history. |
| `supported_causes`     | Minimal supported defect/condition sets whose controlled removal prevents or materially changes the occurrence inside the declared analysis boundary; may be plural. | Chunk merge called the wrong method; conversion dropped the assistant tool call.                 |
| `contributing_factors` | Conditions that increased probability, impact, or detection delay but were neither necessary nor sufficient alone.                                                   | Missing contract test; ambiguous provider error; stale session state.                            |
| `mitigation`           | Action that reduced immediate impact or restored service before the underlying defect was necessarily removed.                                                       | Start a clean session; disable the affected provider path; roll back.                            |
| `resolution`           | Action that ended this occurrence. It may be a workaround and must not be silently promoted to root cause.                                                           | Recreated the request with aligned messages.                                                     |
| `preventive_actions`   | Follow-up controls tied to an owner and verifiable completion criterion.                                                                                             | Add an orphan-call invariant test and reject malformed history before provider invocation.       |

The fields can remain `unknown`. Reviewers must not invent a cause because an incident has a resolution, infer a trigger from the first timestamp, or call one condition “root” without an analysis boundary. A fixing change supports a causal claim only when intervention/reproduction or convergent evidence rules out material alternatives in that context. For generated eval cases, the fixture author proposes the hidden causal graph and Topic 4's independent reference-standard process challenges it against executable preconditions, evidence, repair, alternatives, and healthy twin before admission.

Agreement is measurement evidence, not truth. Artstein and Poesio show that the statistic must fit the annotation scale, coder design, prevalence, and missing-data pattern [R2-11](https://aclanthology.org/J08-4004/); Hayes and Krippendorff motivate a reliability coefficient applicable across coding levels and coder arrangements [R2-12](https://doi.org/10.1080/19312450709336664). Report raw agreement, per-class confusion and uncertainty alongside any chance-corrected coefficient, and inspect whether reviewers share the same unsupported assumption.

The OpenRCA process-failure study provides a useful falsification of model-only attribution [R2-21](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09937). Across the same 335 incidents and five models, its 1,675 runs frequently exhibited hallucinated interpretation, incomplete exploration, symptom-as-cause errors, limited modality use, timestamp mistakes, missing cross-validation, instruction/code mismatch, repetition, evidence misattribution, memory exhaustion, and step exhaustion. Prompt changes broadened exploration but did not remove the dominant interpretive failures, while exposing code, raw outputs, errors, and prior context across the controller/executor boundary reduced communication failures. Adopt those categories as candidate leaf-code hypotheses, not prevalence priors: first separate reasoning, inter-agent handoff, generated-code execution, and environment state, then retain every applicable failure rather than forcing one mutually exclusive “root cause.”

This model has seven falsifiable validity tests:

1. Blinded reviewers meet prespecified field- and decision-specific agreement margins with uncertainty; one aggregate coefficient cannot hide denominator-changing or dangerous confusion.
2. Masking the fix description does not materially change labels derived from pre-fix evidence; otherwise the coding process has hindsight leakage.
3. Recovered retries change terminal status but not the recorded failed attempts, retry causes, latency, or cost.
4. Model-quality rates remain unchanged when invalid harness runs are added to a batch; only reliability and exclusion metrics change.
5. Every retained leaf routes to a distinct owner, preventive action, test, or release decision; otherwise merge or remove it.
6. A separately held-out temporal/channel stream satisfies the predeclared stability rule for new decision-relevant leaves, boundary changes, and `unknown` use; development-set saturation alone is insufficient.
7. Known malformed, expected-denial, recovered, multi-causal, and valid-control records reach their predeclared labels without using candidate identity or post-event fixes.

#### Attempt, operation, and trace semantics

Use three nested identifiers: `trial_id` for one scored scenario execution, `operation_id` for a logical user-visible operation within it, and `attempt_id` for each provider, tool, grader, or verifier attempt. A `429` followed by a successful retry is a failed attempt and a successful terminal operation. It contributes to attempt-error rate, retry rate, latency, and cost, but not terminal task failure. Conversely, catching an exception and returning an empty success envelope does not make the operation successful: terminal success requires the stage's explicit postcondition.

The current OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions are useful as an export mapping, not the canonical Headlamp schema. At inspected commit `94f432d7126f5884d30a2cdde6f4e89908ebb6fd`, agent, inference, tool, exception, and evaluation conventions are still marked **Development** [R2-5](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/tree/94f432d7126f5884d30a2cdde6f4e89908ebb6fd/docs/gen-ai). Map Headlamp records to `invoke_agent`, inference operations such as `chat`, and `execute_tool`; retain `gen_ai.operation.name`, provider, model, conversation, tool name, tool-call ID, finish reasons, token usage, `error.type`, and evaluation score where applicable. Keep input/output messages, system instructions, tool definitions, arguments, results, and exception messages opt-in because the conventions identify them as potentially sensitive. Pin the convention revision in exported artifacts and do not make a development-status attribute a required internal field.

#### Severity from observed impact

Treat `S0`–`S4` as a proposed Headlamp decision scale, not a standard or production distribution. Assign severity after recording impact and before considering ownership. Evaluate: confirmed secret or personal-data exposure; unauthorized or destructive mutation; affected user/workflow scope; outage or wrong-decision duration; reversibility; whether recovery required privileged manual intervention; and credible near-miss potential. Keep actual impact and potential impact separate so a caught approval bypass can be a high-priority near miss without being reported as a data breach.

| Level | Operational anchor                                                                                                                                    |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `S0`  | Confirmed material secret/data exposure, irreversible destructive action, or unauthorized cluster-level security change.                              |
| `S1`  | Unauthorized or materially unsafe reversible mutation, complete loss of the core workflow, or an `S0` near miss stopped only by an independent guard. |
| `S2`  | Materially wrong diagnosis/action or blocked investigation requiring operator intervention, with no observed `S0`/`S1` impact.                        |
| `S3`  | Recoverable degraded behavior, delay, or incomplete answer where a safe path remains available.                                                       |
| `S4`  | Cosmetic, reporting-only, or eval-internal impact that cannot affect the operator's decision or cluster state.                                        |

Record the dimension values and a short rationale, not only `S1`. Severity is scenario-dependent: the same protocol defect can be `S3` when a retry is transparent and `S1` when it blocks every production investigation. Release policy may gate on either observed severity or a separately reviewed near-miss class, but must not combine them into a misleading count of realized harm.

`S0` requires confirmed material impact that occurred, including a persisted unauthorized cluster-level security change. A primary control failure whose harm was prevented before persistence only by an independent guard is an `S1` near miss, recorded separately from realized impact. For example, an independent admission policy blocking an unauthorized mutation is an `S1` near miss; the same mutation persisting before authorization is enforced is `S0`.

#### Score-eligibility and attribution decision

Apply this order before semantic grading:

1. **Apply earlier validity gates.** Topic 1 source/admission failure, Topic 18 integrity failure, Topic 19 unsupported/mixed environment, or Topic 20 concurrency-history invalidity takes precedence over candidate-quality attribution. Preserve the first invalidating layer.
2. **Prove the fixture was valid.** Setup, readiness, candidate-visible context, enabled tools, credentials, and reference solution must pass. Otherwise emit `invalid-run`, routing owner `eval-harness` or `kubernetes-environment`, and exclude the trial.
3. **Identify intentional stops.** A user cancellation, correctly denied mutation, policy refusal, or evidence-based abstention is an expected outcome when the scenario requires it. Do not convert it to a tool or model failure.
4. **Find the first broken contract.** Check request construction, provider acceptance, tool-call schema, approval state, tool result, follow-up generation, and rendering in order. The first violated invariant normally determines the routing owner, while the causal graph retains upstream/downstream interactions.
5. **Grade capability only after the system returned usable evidence.** Wrong cause, unsupported certainty, missed evidence, unsafe recommendation, or failure to act with available tools is model-eligible. Missing or broken tools may still be `eligible-with-limited-tools` when that limitation is an intentional test condition.
6. **Preserve uncertainty.** Use routing owner `unknown` and retain the run for triage when traces cannot distinguish provider, network, tool, or orchestration causes. Do not silently charge unknowns to the model denominator.

A retry can replace an invalid infrastructure attempt, but both attempts remain in reliability reporting. A retry must not erase a deterministic model failure or be selected only because a later answer scored better.

If a case passed Topic 1 admission but fails setup here, emit `excluded-invalid-run` with routing owner `eval-harness` or `kubernetes-environment`. Reopen Topic 1 qualification only when the failure falsifies its source, behavior, safety, leakage, or declared compatibility evidence; ordinary stochastic setup failures remain Topic 2 reliability observations and contribute to the case's measured setup-failure rate.

#### Local contract and regression seed registry

The current test suite contains strong, reproducible contract and scenario seeds. They are not operational incidents: assign observed incident severity `not-applicable` until an occurrence supplies impact evidence. The proposed `S0`–`S4` values below are target impact classes for constructing and reviewing future cases, not claims that the test history realized that harm. These tests establish software invariants; they do not by themselves measure model quality, production occurrence, or user impact.

| Incident seed                        | Local evidence                                                                                                                                            | Taxonomy mapping                                                                                                                          | Eval implication                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Multi-chunk streaming crash          | [R2-16: `LangChainAssistantSession.test.ts`](../packages/ai-common/src/assistant/LangChainAssistantSession.test.ts), `BUG-1`, exercises two-chunk merge   | `product-error`; `model-response`; `assistant-orchestration`; `stream.merge-failure`; proposed S1 or S2                                   | Replay identical chunks without a live provider. Exclude affected trials from semantic scores because no complete answer existed.                                          |
| Abort race and cancellation labeling | [R2-16](../packages/ai-common/src/assistant/LangChainAssistantSession.test.ts) `BUG-2` exercises a cleared controller; `BUG-3` distinguishes `AbortError` | Race: `product-error` / `assistant-orchestration`; valid abort: `cancelled`; `request.cancel-race` or `request.cancelled`; proposed S2/S3 | Cancellation is a control outcome. Only the null dereference or incorrect user-visible classification is a product defect.                                                 |
| Tool-history protocol corruption     | [R2-16](../packages/ai-common/src/assistant/LangChainAssistantSession.test.ts) `BUG-7`, `BUG-8`, and `BUG-9` exercise role/call/result alignment          | `product-error`; `context-build` or `provider-request`; `assistant-orchestration`; `protocol.tool-history-alignment`; proposed S1         | Store the pre-provider message envelope. A provider `400` is not a provider-quality failure when Headlamp generated an invalid sequence.                                   |
| Bound tools bypassed for Copilot     | [R2-16](../packages/ai-common/src/assistant/LangChainAssistantSession.test.ts) `BUG-COPILOT` contrasts bound-model `invoke()` with the prior path         | `product-error`; `provider-request`; `assistant-orchestration`; `protocol.tools-not-bound`; proposed S1                                   | Compare the serialized request and bound-tool inventory. Textual/XML pseudo-calls do not prove that the model lacks tool-calling capability.                               |

The registry should next link each seed to its introducing issue or failure report, fix commit, regression test, affected releases, and recurrence status. Test comments are useful leads but are not complete incident records; history or an accepted issue is needed before asserting prevalence or user impact.

Before admitting any row as an incident, reproduce the parent revision when practical, capture the failing invariant, show the fixing diff and passing regression, and record affected-version evidence. If history cannot distinguish a pre-existing defect from code and test imported together, classify it as `regression-evidence-only`. This prevents issue-shaped comments from becoming fabricated production statistics.

#### Model-quality leaf codes

Once execution is valid, use a small initial model branch:

- `reasoning.wrong-cause`: names a causal fact contradicted by authoritative evidence.
- `reasoning.symptom-only`: repeats status such as `CrashLoopBackOff` without identifying the causal condition.
- `evidence.missed-required`: fails to retrieve or use evidence necessary to distinguish plausible causes.
- `evidence.fabricated`: claims an observation not present in tool results or candidate-visible context.
- `evidence.stale`: relies on superseded state after a change, retry, or tool result.
- `uncertainty.overconfident`: presents a unique cause when the available evidence supports multiple hypotheses.
- `uncertainty.unnecessary-abstention`: declines despite sufficient evidence and available safe tools.
- `remediation.ineffective`: proposes or performs a change that does not restore the hard postconditions.
- `remediation.excessive-scope`: changes unrelated resources or weakens controls beyond what recovery requires.
- `tooling.wrong-tool`: chooses an available tool that cannot establish the claimed evidence or action.
- `tooling.invalid-arguments`: emits malformed, out-of-scope, or semantically incorrect arguments despite a valid exposed schema.
- `communication.material-omission`: omits impact, uncertainty, safety requirement, or next action needed for an operator decision.

Do not create a leaf for every wording difference. Add one only when it changes a product decision, has an observable definition, and at least two reviewers can apply it consistently. Store the rubric dimension scores alongside the leaf code so one primary label does not discard partial performance.

#### Incident-mining workflow and privacy gate

Rank sources by causal/contract evidence, but do not confuse that order with population representativeness:

1. Regression test linked to an accepted fix and reproducible pre-fix behavior.
2. Public issue or pull request with logs, affected versions, root cause, and verification.
3. Privacy-reviewed support incident with consent, redaction, retention, and access controls.
4. Opt-in production trace sampled under a documented purpose and deletion policy.
5. Unconfirmed anecdote, which may expand the discovery queue but cannot establish a taxonomy rate or gold case.

Evidence grade remains attached to each record. Repetition of low-grade reports can establish that a channel repeatedly expresses a concern, but cannot by itself upgrade the underlying occurrence, cause, severity, or prevalence claim; correlated reposts and duplicate tickets remain linked rather than counted as independent confirmation.

Group by causal defect and affected contract, not error string, for engineering analysis. Do not delete occurrence rows: one message-history defect can generate different provider errors and many user occurrences, while the same `401`, timeout, or empty response can have unrelated causes. Preserve report → occurrence → defect links and publish the denominator used. The AI Incident Database provides a useful report/incident/classification separation at the inspected snapshot [R2-8](https://github.com/responsible-ai-collaborative/aiid/tree/dd3f7543e365084654babca0b7380fc368ad28de). Copy that structural distinction and review metadata, not its harm categories, adaptive admission choices, or public-report distribution.

Each admitted Headlamp record should contain:

- Identity and versioning: opaque incident ID, report IDs, taxonomy version, created/observed dates, affected and fixed versions, recurrence status, and duplicate-of links.
- Raw observations: immutable evidence references, timestamps, source class, collection method, hashes, retention location, and the distinction between captured fact and reviewer inference.
- Causal analysis: analysis boundary, observed impact, trigger, supported cause graph and alternatives, contributing factors, mitigation, resolution, preventive actions, first broken invariant, routing owner, failed stage, failure mode, and evidence confidence.
- Reproducibility: minimal reproducer, parent revision or fixture revision, failing precondition, fixing diff/reference, regression test, healthy control, and current reproducibility result.
- Measurement disposition: outcome, score eligibility, attempt and terminal statuses, retry class, observed severity, near-miss potential, confidence, missing-data flags, and exclusion reason.
- Governance: reporter, independent coders, adjudicator, label timestamps, disagreement reason, codebook version, access class, consent/legal basis where applicable, redactions, reuse restrictions, and deletion date.

Do not retain raw prompts, cluster names, resource contents, tokens, or provider payloads merely because they are available. Store the least sensitive evidence that can prove the invariant; use synthetic canaries and hashes or typed extracts where full content is unnecessary. NIST's Privacy Framework treats this as governed privacy-risk management rather than a post-hoc redaction task [R2-15](https://www.nist.gov/privacy-framework). An OpenTelemetry export with content capture disabled should still be sufficient to reconstruct stage, timing, status, tool identity, and retry structure. If minimization removes evidence needed for attribution, report lower confidence or `unresolved`; do not reacquire disallowed content silently.

#### Codebook validation and governance

The first measurable Research 2 deliverable should be a **purposive boundary calibration set**, not a prevalence estimate. Include prespecified contrasts among valid model-quality failures, orchestration/runtime defects, provider/tool failures, safety/control outcomes, invalid runs, and expected cancellation/denial/abstention outcomes. Choose its information target before coding: every critical boundary must be represented, and independently coded records must be sufficient to compare uncertainty on each decision-changing disagreement rate with its risk-derived margin. If feasible review capacity cannot meet that target, report the codebook as inconclusive rather than declaring a fixed record count sufficient.

1. Write a versioned codebook with inclusion, exclusion, boundary, positive, negative, and ambiguous examples for every field and leaf code. Define the evidence needed for `confirmed`, `probable`, and `unresolved`.
2. Pilot on records outside the release benchmark. Train with examples, then have two Kubernetes-capable reviewers independently code a blinded sample without seeing each other's labels, candidate identity, or fix description.
3. Report raw agreement, per-class confusion, prevalence and uncertainty for nominal fields; use a chance-corrected coefficient appropriate to coder count, scale, missing labels, and design, following the cautions in [R2-11](https://aclanthology.org/J08-4004/) and [R2-12](https://doi.org/10.1080/19312450709336664). For ordinal severity, report weighted disagreement by distance. Never use one aggregate coefficient to hide a dangerous confusion such as `expected-denial` versus `product-error`.
4. Adjudicate against evidence, record the reason and codebook change, and re-code an untouched sample. Do not overwrite original labels or count adjudicated consensus as independent agreement.
5. Build a decision-loss table before candidate comparisons: denominator inclusion/exclusion, unsafe-versus-expected control, severe-impact escalation, and wrong routing owner have different costs. Set field-specific margins and interval rules from those consequences. Any unresolved disagreement that changes a release denominator or hard safety decision blocks qualification; no universal raw-agreement or kappa cutoff is imported from another domain.
6. Iterate conceptual and empirical codebook revisions until predeclared ending conditions hold: every development record is classifiable or explicitly `unknown`; dimensions are distinct; leaves are mutually distinguishable at their decision boundary; every leaf has evidence rules and a distinct use; no redundant leaf remains; and the taxonomy is concise enough to apply. Then test a fresh temporal/channel holdout. A new decision-relevant leaf, material boundary rewrite, or catch-all rate beyond its margin restarts development and requires another untouched holdout.
7. Freeze a taxonomy version for each comparative run. A definition, merge, or split starts a new version; publish a mapping, identify non-lossless changes, bridge-recode a fixed sample where permitted, and never splice incompatible series.
8. On a risk-based schedule and after material incidents, taxonomy changes, ownership disputes, or channel shifts, sample `unknown`, excluded, severe, and high-frequency classes; inspect drift, missingness, reviewer disagreement, and catch-all use. Retire leaves that cannot produce a distinct product decision.

The protocol must contain an approved numeric margin, interval rule, and escalation action for every confirmatory field and critical confusion before the first blinded record is coded. Derive these from the decision-loss table, feasible information, and safety policy; do not choose them after observing agreement. Freeze `unknown`/catch-all margins separately by source channel when observability differs, and mark the pilot infeasible or inconclusive if approved margins cannot be estimated with the available review capacity.

The later production study needs a separate sampling frame. Define the target population, eligible occurrence, index time, observation window, channel-specific inclusion probabilities, linkage, and censoring; stratify by provider, workflow, permissions, deployment mode, and prespecified affected population. Publish `eligible → observable → sampled → linkable → coded → analyzed` counts, exclusions, consent, missingness, and survivorship limitations, adapting STROBE's transparent observational reporting by analogy [R2-14](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.39335.541782.AD). Support tickets overrepresent visible failures; opt-in traces underrepresent users who disable telemetry; regression tests overrepresent defects already understood. Report channels separately and do not weight or pool them without defensible target, selection, overlap, and linkage assumptions. Topic 10 owns production sampling/privacy infrastructure and Topic 21 owns offline-to-deployment outcome validation.

#### Failure ownership and invalidity

Preserve the first invalidating layer and its consequence:

| Invalidity state               | Trigger                                                                                                      | Claim consequence                                                                            |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unit_identity_failure`        | Reports, occurrences, defects, cases, trials, operations, or attempts cannot be joined or distinguished      | No rate, deduplication, recurrence, or retry claim                                           |
| `eligibility_failure`          | Earlier source, fixture, integrity, compatibility, concurrency, or score-eligibility gate fails              | Exclude from candidate-quality denominator; retain reliability evidence                      |
| `evidence_boundary_failure`    | Reviewer packet contains post-outcome/fix/candidate identity or omits evidence required by the codebook      | No blinded reliability or causal-label claim                                                 |
| `attribution_unresolved`       | Evidence does not distinguish owners/causes, intervention is absent, or material alternatives remain         | Retain occurrence and impact; owner/cause-specific rates remain unknown                      |
| `reviewer_reliability_failure` | Decision-changing confusion exceeds its prespecified margin or uncertainty cannot rule that out              | Taxonomy version cannot gate or compare candidates                                           |
| `taxonomy_stability_failure`   | Fresh holdout requires a decision-relevant leaf/boundary change or catch-all use exceeds its declared margin | Reopen development; do not splice old/new series                                             |
| `privacy_governance_failure`   | Collection, access, linkage, retention, deletion, or secondary use exceeds the approved contract             | Quarantine/delete as required; no research use or claim                                      |
| `sampling_frame_failure`       | Eligibility, selection probability, missingness, linkage, or target population is unresolved                 | Descriptive channel counts only; no prevalence, comparison, or transport claim               |
| `version_bridge_failure`       | Taxonomy versions cannot be losslessly mapped or bridge recoding is incomplete                               | Break the trend and report versions separately                                               |
| `instrumentation_failure`      | Required attempts, operations, statuses, timestamps, versions, or evidence references were not captured      | Use `unknown` only if permitted by the protocol; otherwise invalidate the affected field/run |

NIST's AI RMF Playbook recommends documented, independent, context-appropriate TEVV and ongoing measurement review [R2-6](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/). The CDC field-investigation guidance similarly emphasizes predefined objectives/case definitions and evaluation of validity, reliability, completeness, bias, privacy, and operational error [R2-7](https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/collecting-data.html). These are governance and data-quality analogies, not validation of Headlamp labels or thresholds.

#### Focused pilot

1. Freeze a machine-readable protocol: unit ontology, inclusion/exclusion, codebook version, evidence packet, critical confusion pairs, decision-loss table, approved numeric field/channel-specific margins and interval rules, reviewer roles, development/holdout split, stability rule, privacy basis, and analysis code digest. Mask candidate/provider identity, source leaf labels, fix implementation and commit/issue linkage, post-incident discussion, postmortem cause/resolution text, and evidence created after the analysis epoch; retain only pre-index context and observations that the codebook declares admissible. No blinded coding begins until reviewers can reconstruct that packet boundary.
2. Build a purposive development set from the local regression seeds, valid model-answer perturbations, expected denials/cancellations, recovered attempts, invalid fixtures, and multi-causal cascades. Include matched records around each score-denominator, owner, and severity boundary; label the set non-prevalence.
3. Have at least two Kubernetes-capable reviewers independently code identical packets without candidate/provider identity, source leaf label, or fix/postmortem text. Record `unknown`, skipped fields, confidence, evidence references, time, and codebook questions rather than forcing completeness.
4. Report field-level raw agreement, full confusion matrices, weighted severity disagreement, appropriate chance-corrected reliability, and uncertainty at the occurrence/defect grouping level. Evaluate each critical confusion against its own prewritten margin.
5. Test hindsight leakage with randomized matched packets: one review group sees only evidence available at the analysis epoch; another first codes the same bounded packet and then receives the later fix/postmortem in a separately marked phase. Compare pre-fix labels before using any post-fix adjudication. If decision-critical labels move beyond the predeclared paired-change margin, invalidate the affected coding process and recode a fresh set after revising the evidence boundary.
6. Adjudicate against source evidence, preserve original labels, revise definitions as a new codebook version, and rerun only on fresh records. Do not report adjudicated consensus as independent agreement.
7. Evaluate the frozen version on an untouched time/channel holdout. Report new-leaf requests, boundary disputes, `unknown`/catch-all use, channel-specific confusion, and whether every retained leaf still routes to a distinct action.
8. Inject invalid controls: merged occurrences, duplicated reports, missing attempts, wrong version, post-fix leakage, unsupported owner, ambiguous multi-cause evidence, unapproved content, and taxonomy-version mixing. Require the corresponding invalidity or uncertainty state.
9. Publish the complete flow, exclusions, disagreement/adjudication ledger, codebook and mappings, per-channel counts, limitations, and the decision to qualify, narrow, revise, suspend, or retire each field/leaf.

The pilot succeeds only if unit joins and denominators reconstruct; all injected controls fail closed; uncertainty on every decision-changing disagreement meets its prespecified risk margin; no unresolved disagreement can alter a release denominator or hard safety action; fix unmasking does not create material hindsight relabeling; the frozen holdout meets the stability rule; and privacy/governance checks pass. A high overall kappa, adjudicated consensus, many labeled rows, or complete classification obtained by overusing a catch-all code is not success.

#### Counterevidence and limitations

- Incident taxonomies shape reporting: once a leaf is rewarded or gated, reviewers and teams may preferentially notice it. Monitor reporting propensity and preserve free-text/new-code review rather than treating stable frequencies as natural truth.
- Agreement does not establish factual or causal validity. Reviewers can share the same hindsight, organizational assumptions, missing evidence, or codebook-induced error.
- “Root cause” is relative to an analysis boundary and may be plural. Distributed human-agent-controller failures can involve feedback and several sufficient paths that one routing label cannot represent.
- Local regression tests provide strong contract controls but overrepresent defects already understood, may combine implementation and test introduction, and do not establish production occurrence, user impact, or prevalence.
- Support cases overrepresent visible/frustrating failures; opt-in telemetry excludes some privacy-sensitive, offline, and self-hosted users; severe silent wrong advice may leave no report. Missing populations cannot be repaired by assertion.
- Severity is organization-, permission-, and workload-dependent. The proposed `S0`–`S4` anchors need independent calibration and must not be compared with another organization's labels by name alone.
- A taxonomy can be stable because it is too coarse, while a highly detailed taxonomy can be unreliable and statistically sparse. Decision utility, confusion, and unknown use must accompany saturation claims.
- Deduplicating reports into defects helps engineering prioritization but destroys occurrence prevalence if the original rows and linkage are not retained. Conversely, counting retries or duplicate tickets as incidents inflates rates.
- Privacy minimization can make attribution unresolved. That is a valid limitation, not permission to collect raw prompts, Secrets, support text, or identities outside the approved purpose.
- Provider, tool, Kubernetes, UI, policy, and organizational changes create new boundaries. Versioning and bridge studies expose drift but cannot guarantee a timeless taxonomy.
