| [R3-12](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/): Services, networking, and traffic                                                                                        | Service, EndpointSlice, DNS, ingress/gateway, load-balancing, topology, and NetworkPolicy surfaces                                                             | Broad concept index; implementation/provider behavior and incident prevalence require separate evidence                                                                 |
| [R3-13](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/): Kubernetes storage                                                                                                                   | Volumes, PV/PVC, StorageClass, CSI, dynamic provisioning, snapshots, capacity, attachment, and ephemeral/persistent storage surfaces                           | Documentation breadth does not establish storage-driver portability, safe fault injection, or Headlamp frequency                                                        |
| [R3-14](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/): Scheduling, preemption, and eviction                                                                                     | Scheduler, assignment, affinity/topology, taints, capacity, preemption, eviction, disruption, and node-pressure mechanisms                                     | Mechanisms vary by scheduler/plugins/version; exact events and production frequencies are not guaranteed                                                                |
| [R3-15](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/): Deployments                                                                                                 | Rollout status, observed generation, progress deadlines, pause/resume, rollback, revision, scaling, and terminal/progress distinctions                         | Applies to Deployments; other controllers/operators need their own freshness and terminal contracts                                                                     |
| [R3-16](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/): Jobs                                                                                                               | Completion, retries, backoff, parallelism, suspension, failure policy, terminal conditions, and version-dependent lifecycle                                    | Job semantics do not transfer directly to long-running workloads or custom workload controllers                                                                         |
| [R3-17](https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/): Kubernetes version-skew policy                                                                                                | Supported release window and component-specific API server, kubelet, kube-proxy, controller, kubectl, and upgrade-order constraints                            | Moving Kubernetes-component policy; third-party distributions, operators, CRDs, images, and telemetry may impose additional constraints                                 |
| [R3-18](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-142): Practical Combinatorial Testing                                                                                                           | NIST report on finite parameter models, constraints, covering arrays, interaction strength, and practical combinatorial test design                            | 2010 conventional-software method; low-order fault evidence does not establish appropriate strength or semantic coverage for this agent                                 |
| [R3-19](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-53Ar5): Assessing Security and Privacy Controls in Information Systems and Organizations                                                        | Tailoring assessment objectives, methods, depth, and coverage to assurance needs with documented evidence and findings                                         | Security/privacy control assessment guide; it does not define Headlamp coverage obligations, scenario counts, or release thresholds                                     |
| [R3-20](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.2010.62): An Analysis and Survey of the Development of Mutation Testing                                                                                 | Mutation-testing foundations, operators, equivalent-mutant problem, cost, evidence, and use for test-suite adequacy sensitivity                                | General and dated survey; mutation score can reward unrealistic mutants and is not causal, semantic, safety, or population completeness                                 |
| [R3-21](https://doi.org/10.1111/ecog.02881): Cross-validation strategies for structured data                                                                                                | Demonstrates bias from random cross-validation under temporal, spatial, hierarchical, and related dependence and motivates structure-aware folds               | Ecology focus; family/source/oracle lineage is a Headlamp analogy and grouped holdout still cannot prove unseen-mechanism generalization                                |
| [R3-22](https://sre.google/sre-book/testing-reliability/): Google SRE testing for reliability                                                                                               | Unit/integration/system tests, known-good/bad probes, regression tests, production-derived tests, replay limits, and testing cost                              | Practitioner guidance; service tests and production replay can be incomplete, unrepresentative, unsafe, or contaminated                                                 |
| [R3-23](https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/): Google SRE canarying                                                                                                              | Isolation, canary/control assignment, metric selection, attribution, automation, and confounding risks in before/after comparisons                             | Deployment canary method, not benchmark coverage authority; shared clusters, low traffic, and simultaneous changes limit inference                                      |
| [R3-24](https://doi.org/10.1057/ejis.2012.26): A Method for Taxonomy Development and Its Application in Information Systems                                                                 | Iterative conceptual/empirical taxonomy development with meta-characteristic and objective/subjective ending conditions                                        | General information-systems taxonomy method; does not validate Headlamp facets, family boundaries, or completeness                                                      |
| [R3-25](https://aclanthology.org/J08-4004/): Inter-Coder Agreement for Computational Linguistics                                                                                            | Agreement concepts, scale/coder design, chance correction, prevalence effects, missing labels, and interpretation                                              | Language annotation focus; agreement cannot prove Kubernetes causal truth, facet usefulness, or universal acceptance thresholds                                         |
| [R3-26](https://github.com/illume/plugins/tree/41810531db9ce578d4dc76a9bb7bcf818dbbaf15): local plugin repository snapshot                                                                  | Immutable inspected fork snapshot containing the AI Assistant and 68 YAML files across 11 sibling plugin `test-files` trees                                    | Fork/static-source evidence only; file count/grouping is not an executed scenario denominator, upstream state, or production distribution                               |
| [R3-27](../e2e/ai-assistant.spec.ts): local AI Assistant E2E test                                                                                                                           | Current authentication, KWOK node, plugin/UI, settings, mock-provider, scripted workflow, and screenshot prerequisites                                         | Product-wiring test; it does not execute real kubelet/image behavior or establish a coherent RCA cause, reference standard, or coverage                                 |
| [R3-28](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23580): MetaKube and KubeFault                                                                                                                           | Describes 1,873 Kubernetes scenarios across six counted error categories with symptom, environment, kubectl-log, cause-chain, and resolution fields            | Category shares are not production prevalence or independent-family counts; artifact, lineage, mechanism detail, environment mix, and sampling frame remain unavailable |

### Research 4: expert-labeled RCA reference set

The term **reference set** is preferable to “gold answers.” A single prose answer is too brittle for Kubernetes RCA: several explanations can express the same causal facts, more than one repair can be safe, and incomplete evidence can make several hypotheses defensible. The reference standard should encode what the available evidence establishes, what it rules out, and which decisions are safe. Prose examples are calibration aids, not the scoring authority.

#### Research method and scope

The primary hypothesis is: **a versioned RCA reference standard is fit for a declared evaluation decision only when independent, task-qualified reviewers can reconstruct each pass-critical fact, causal edge, evidence role, uncertainty boundary, and action constraint from the same frozen candidate-observable epoch; decision-changing labels meet prespecified risk-derived reliability margins on fresh cases; evidence ablation and counterfactual controls change the reference in the predicted direction; and adjudication, candidate outputs, or successful repairs do not create hindsight labels**. Agreement alone is insufficient: reviewers can consistently apply a wrong, leaked, or operationally irrelevant standard.

The cheapest falsification is to select one sufficient-evidence case, its insufficient-evidence twin, one healthy control, and one unsafe-but-effective repair. Give task-qualified non-author reviewers identical blinded packets, then remove or replace each claimed decisive observation and reveal repair outcomes only in a separate phase. If pass-critical labels cannot be reconstructed, do not change when decisive evidence changes, change merely after outcome/fix disclosure, or remain unresolved beyond their prewritten decision margin, quarantine the case and withhold aggregate benchmark claims.

The source search was refreshed on September 6, 2026. Search families included `reference standard diagnostic accuracy bias`, `expert annotation inter-rater reliability disagreement`, `Delphi consensus expert panel`, `content response process internal structure validity evidence`, `causal graph counterfactual root cause`, `benchmark answer equivalence partial credit`, `abstention selective prediction`, `annotation adjudication leakage`, `dataset documentation data cards`, and `test set contamination private holdout`. Sources were included when they were peer-reviewed methods, standards/government or durable first-party guidance, pinned domain documentation, or reproducible local artifacts. Popularity votes, title-only expertise, candidate-output-derived labels, unblinded consensus without original labels, and generic agreement thresholds without decision context were excluded as validation evidence.

Research questions:

1. What exact construct, decision, scenario unit, observation epoch, and candidate evidence boundary does each reference record govern?
2. Which facts and causal edges are directly observed, mechanistically supported, hypothesized, or genuinely underdetermined, and which alternatives remain admissible?
3. Are evidence expressions necessary and sufficient for the strongest supported conclusion, abstention boundary, and safe action, or are declared observations decorative?
4. Can independent task-qualified reviewers reproduce pass-critical labels without fixture-author notes, candidate/model identity, preferred fixes, automated-grader output, or post-epoch evidence?
5. Which reviewer disagreements reflect packet defects, codebook ambiguity, missing domain expertise, legitimate plural interpretations, or annotation error?
6. Do known-good, partial, contradicted, overconfident, abstaining, lucky-repair, and unsafe-effective controls receive the intended atomic decisions?
7. How do reference changes alter historical candidate decisions, and when must a case be bridged, quarantined, rerun, or retired rather than silently relabeled?
8. Which populations, domains, languages, permission envelopes, environments, and causal families lack qualified reviewers or sufficient evidence for a reference claim?

This section validates reference standards, not automated graders or production prevalence. Topic 1 owns source/provenance admission; Topic 2 owns incident units, causal routing, and severity; Topic 3 owns family/coverage claims; Topic 4 retains authority over reference definition, annotation, admission, and versioning; Topic 5 owns grader validation/calibration against a frozen Topic 4 version and must revalidate after any decision-changing reference revision; Topics 10 and 21 own production sampling and deployment validity; Topic 18 owns holdout leakage; and Topics 19–20 own environment and concurrent-history validity.

Use a claim ladder:

| Level | Claim                                                                                  | Minimum evidence                                                                                                                        |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0     | **Packet identity:** source, scenario, environment, epoch, and visibility are closed   | Digests, candidate/evaluator/construction views, access checks, Topic 1/3/19 validity                                                   |
| 1     | **Case truth:** reference facts/actions are supported within the declared epoch        | Executable setup/evidence/counterfactual/outcome/safety controls and independent domain review                                          |
| 2     | **Annotation reproducibility:** reviewers apply the codebook reliably                  | Blinded independent labels on fresh cases, field/confusion uncertainty, qualification and conflict records                              |
| 3     | **Decision validity:** atomic labels distinguish material diagnosis and safety quality | Known-good/wrong/partial/abstaining/lucky-repair/unsafe controls, ablation, consequences review, and prespecified decision-loss margins |
| 4     | **Generalization:** process holds across claimed families/reviewers/contexts           | Family-lineage and reviewer-pair holdouts, alternate evidence paths, supported languages/access modes, missing-population limits        |
| 5     | **Grader use:** automated decisions reproduce the qualified standard                   | Separate Topic 5 calibration/validation split, hard-control precedence, uncertainty, drift/expiry, and no reference leakage             |

Passing a lower level does not establish a higher one. An individually sound case can exist before the annotation process supports aggregate claims; high reviewer agreement cannot rescue a case with false facts or unresolved safety boundaries.

#### Define the construct and unit of annotation

The target construct is **evidence-bounded operational correctness** for the task and observation epoch in the scenario contract. It is not whether an answer resembles the fixture author's explanation, whether the suspected cause later proves true using hidden information, or whether a proposed change happens to make the symptom disappear.

Annotate one `scenarioId` and observation epoch at a time. The reference packet should contain these linked layers:

| Layer                  | Required reference data                                                                                                                                                      | Scoring role                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Decision contract      | Intended use, operator/system decision, false-pass/false-fail/abstention consequences, hard vetoes, and partial-credit policy.                                               | Prevents labels from being optimized without a declared consumer or decision loss.            |
| Observed problem       | User-visible symptom, affected resources and scope, time bounds, desired versus observed state, impact, and task intent.                                                     | Establishes what the candidate was asked to explain or change.                                |
| Causal graph           | Typed facts and edges for trigger, proximate mechanism, contributing conditions, root/systemic factors, and resulting symptoms; each node has confidence and provenance.     | Prevents a visible symptom or human action from being mislabeled as the sole root cause.      |
| Evidence map           | Stable evidence IDs, candidate visibility, capture time, freshness rule, supported and contradicted fact IDs, source reliability, and minimum sufficient evidence sets.      | Makes grounding and evidence sufficiency testable without requiring one investigation path.   |
| Alternative hypotheses | Plausible alternatives, evidence for and against each, disposition, and what unavailable observation would discriminate them.                                                | Distinguishes a wrong cause from a reasonable unresolved hypothesis.                          |
| Action envelope        | Safe diagnostic steps, acceptable repair equivalence classes, required approvals, preconditions, verification, rollback, forbidden actions, and collateral-change limits.    | Separates diagnosis quality from accidental recovery and blocks unsafe but effective changes. |
| Uncertainty boundary   | Strongest conclusion supported, required caveats, abstention or clarification conditions, and statements the evidence cannot support.                                        | Rewards calibrated uncertainty and penalizes both guessing and unnecessary abstention.        |
| Communication minimum  | Facts that must reach the user, severity/urgency, immediate mitigation versus durable repair, and any operator decision still required.                                      | Scores operational usefulness without rewarding verbosity or a particular writing style.      |
| Provenance and review  | Scenario/source revisions, evidence digest, Kubernetes/controller versions, author, independent annotations, adjudication record, codebook version, and review/expiry dates. | Makes the reference standard auditable and prevents silent relabeling.                        |

Use stable fact and evidence IDs rather than text fragments. For example, `fact.selector-mismatch` may be supported jointly by `evidence.service-selector` and `evidence.pod-labels`; neither observation alone proves that intended Pods should back that Service. Facts should be minimal enough to score independently but not split into meaningless tokens.

A minimal machine-readable record should make the scoring logic inspectable. This is a shape to test, not a final schema:

```yaml
referenceStandard:
  version: 1.0.0
  scenarioId: service-selector-wrong-label-v1
  observationEpochDigest: sha256:...
  decisionContract:
    target: diagnose-and-safe-plan
    consumer: kubernetes-operator
    falsePassConsequence: unsafe-or-unsupported-action
    falseFailConsequence: valid-diagnosis-rejected
    abstentionConsequence: additional-observation-or-escalation
    hardVetoes: [forbidden-mutation, fabricated-evidence]
  observationEpoch:
    startedAt: <ISO-8601>
    endedAt: <ISO-8601>
    environmentManifestDigest: sha256:...
    candidateViewDigest: sha256:...
    evaluatorViewDigest: sha256:...
    apiRequests:
      - {
          operation: get,
          resource: v1/Service/default/frontend,
          consistency: <most-recent|cache|unknown>,
          capturedAt: <ISO-8601>,
        }
    collections:
      - { resource: v1/Pod, collectionResourceVersion: <opaque>, continueChainDigest: sha256:... }
    observedObjects:
      - { identity: v1/Service/default/frontend, uid: <uid>, resourceVersion: <opaque> }
  facts:
    - id: fact.no-ready-endpoints
      role: symptom
      status: required
      evidenceAnyOf:
        - [evidence.endpointslice-empty]
    - id: fact.selector-mismatch
      role: mechanism
      status: required
      evidenceAllOf:
        - evidence.service-selector
        - evidence.intended-pod-labels
      contradicts: [fact.pods-unready]
  alternatives:
    - id: alternative.pods-unready
      disposition: rejected
      contradictedBy: [evidence.pods-ready]
  actions:
    - id: action.align-selector
      class: direct-repair
      requiresApproval: true
      postconditions: [invariant.intended-ready-endpoint-present]
      forbiddenMutations: [namespace-delete, rbac-escalation]
  decisionBoundary:
    strongestSupportedConclusion: fact.selector-mismatch
    abstainIfMissing: [evidence.intended-pod-labels]
```

The schema needs semantic validation in addition to JSON Schema validation. Every required fact must have a satisfiable candidate-visible evidence expression; every rejected alternative must name contradictory evidence; every executable action must define approval, postconditions, and forbidden mutations; and every `abstainIfMissing` item must change the strongest supported conclusion when ablated. Cycles are invalid unless explicitly typed as feedback behavior, and a fact cannot be both required and contradicted at the same observation epoch.

Do not compare resource versions across resource types or require a candidate to observe a later live version than the frozen packet. Record request operation, requested consistency/resource-version semantics, response/collection identity, collection continuation chain, object UID/version, capture time, and controller-specific generation rule. A collection resource version identifies the collection snapshot, while an item's version identifies that object's change state; neither is a global clock. The epoch records what was actually available, including access denials and missing signals. Evidence discovered later belongs to challenge/revision, not retroactive truth for the original run.

#### Reference-standard bias and applicability audit

Adapt, without claiming clinical equivalence, QUADAS-2's separation of case selection, index-test conduct, reference standard, flow/timing, and applicability [R4-16](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclinepi.2010.09.012). For every case record:

| Bias/applicability question | Required audit evidence                                                                                                                            | Failure response                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Selection                   | Source population, selection rule, exclusions, family/environment/permission spectrum, and whether the case was chosen after model results         | Restrict claim, replace selection, or mark development-only; no prevalence/generalization inference |
| Incorporation               | Proof that required facts and pass decisions were not defined from candidate outputs, grader verdicts, expected-answer text, or majority success   | `incorporation_bias`; rebuild blind on fresh evidence/cases                                         |
| Reference authority         | Independent Kubernetes/controller/application semantics, observed mechanism, alternatives, and limits; fixture mutation alone is construction-only | Quarantine or reduce to hypothesis/discovery until independently supported                          |
| Flow and timing             | Same declared observation epoch for reviewers/candidate, accounted missing evidence/cases, no post-outcome evidence in pre-outcome labels          | Invalidate affected reliability/decision claim; preserve excluded count/reason                      |
| Applicability               | Match between reviewed task, users, evidence/access, environment, impact/action policy, and the intended benchmark claim                           | Narrow profile and publish missing populations rather than extrapolating                            |

STARD similarly motivates reporting the reference standard, participant/case flow, exclusions, indeterminate results, and applicability [R4-5](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.h5527). Both are diagnostic-study analogies: neither defines a Kubernetes truth standard, label schema, effect estimate, or admission threshold.

#### Separate evidence visibility from evidence authority

Use four access classes and hash each packet independently:

| Access class      | Contents                                                                                                           | Rule                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Candidate-visible | Prompt, tool responses, permitted cluster observations, and facts an operator with the declared RBAC could obtain. | The assistant may be required to cite or derive only from this class.                                                                      |
| Evaluator-visible | Reference facts, evidence mappings, rubrics, safe-action envelope, and adjudication needed to score the run.       | Hidden from the candidate but may judge claims about candidate-visible evidence; it cannot silently add observations the candidate lacked. |
| Construction-only | Injected mutation, fixture author notes, setup credentials, known-good patch, and synthetic-control metadata.      | Used to validate fixture construction, never by itself to prove that a candidate diagnosis was supportable.                                |
| Governance-only   | Holdout membership, annotator identities/conflicts, access logs, leakage markers, and future challenge cases.      | Restricted to dataset custodians; graders receive only the minimum scoring projection.                                                     |

An evaluator-visible label and a grader-only observation are different things. The first formalizes how visible evidence should be interpreted; the second supplies new evidence. Except in an explicitly labeled oracle track, new grader-only observations cannot make a candidate's stronger conclusion correct or incorrect. Store the exact candidate evidence transcript, including access denials and stale/missing responses, because nominal fixture state is not proof of what the assistant could observe.

#### Worked admission audit: Knative DomainMapping broken reference

Applying the proposed method to a real pilot candidate changes its disposition. The local `03-domainmapping-broken-ref.yaml` declares a `serving.knative.dev/v1beta1` `DomainMapping` whose `spec.ref` names a nonexistent `serving.knative.dev/v1` Service. That proves the fixture author's intended mutation, but it does not yet prove that missing target is the observed operational cause.

Current Knative documentation adds two constraints that matter to the oracle ([R4-1](https://knative.dev/docs/serving/services/custom-domains/), [R4-2](https://knative.dev/docs/serving/reference/serving-api/)):

1. A `DomainMapping` requires a same-domain `ClusterDomainClaim`, unless automatic claim creation is enabled in `config-network`.
2. Its target may be a Knative Service, Route, **or core Kubernetes Service** when the object satisfies the documented Addressable URL contract.

The local broken-reference manifest creates no `ClusterDomainClaim`, and `test-files/setup.sh` checks that the CRD exists but does not check `autocreate-cluster-domain-claims` or wait for a `DomainMapping` condition. The broken, core-Service, healthy, setup, and README artifacts are preserved at one inspected repository snapshot [R4-18](https://github.com/illume/plugins/tree/41810531db9ce578d4dc76a9bb7bcf818dbbaf15/knative/test-files). Therefore the case can fail or remain unready because the domain is unclaimed, the reference is unresolved, ingress is not ready, certificate provisioning fails, or several conditions coexist. The sibling `03-domainmapping-core-svc.yaml` is not an invalid-target negative example; it is a useful GVK-aware control proving that `kind: Service` alone does not imply a Knative Service.

**Current disposition: `quarantined` with `reference_authority_failure`, not reference-set admissible.** No candidate run may use this reference until re-admission isolates one causal mechanism:

- create a `ClusterDomainClaim` for `my-unique-broken-mapping.local-test.dev` in setup, or assert and record the exact auto-claim configuration;
- pin and record the Knative Serving version and installed CRD schema;
- wait until `status.observedGeneration == metadata.generation` and `ReferenceResolved=False` with the controller-reported reason, rather than requiring overall `Ready=False`;
- prove absence of the exact target GVK, namespace, and name: `serving.knative.dev/v1`, `Service`, `knative-map-test/non-existent-service`;
- record `DomainClaimed`, `IngressReady`, and `CertificateProvisioned` separately so another false/unknown condition cannot be mislabeled as the reference failure;
- add a counterfactual setup that creates the exact Knative Service and demonstrates `ReferenceResolved=True`; overall readiness may still depend on ingress and TLS and is not the recovery oracle for this fact;
- retain the core-Service fixture as a separate healthy or capability-qualified kind-resolution case, subject to proving that it satisfies the Addressable contract in the pinned environment.

The first reference record for the repaired read-only case should use boundaries like these:

| Reference field       | Admissible value                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Required observation  | Current `DomainMapping.spec.ref`; current `ReferenceResolved=False` condition with observed generation; exact referenced GVK/name absent.                                                     |
| Required mechanism    | The controller cannot resolve the declared target object.                                                                                                                                     |
| Acceptable wording    | “Missing referenced Knative Service,” “unresolved `spec.ref`,” or equivalent wording that names the exact target identity.                                                                    |
| Required distinction  | A same-name `v1/Service`, an unclaimed domain, ingress readiness, and TLS readiness are different objects or condition paths and do not satisfy the missing Knative Service reference.        |
| Expected abstention   | If status is stale/unobserved, `ReferenceResolved` is absent, target discovery is denied, or remaining evidence cannot distinguish reference resolution from domain-claim failure.            |
| Safe next observation | Read the exact target GVK in the namespace; inspect `observedGeneration` and all `DomainMapping` conditions; inspect the matching `ClusterDomainClaim` and relevant controller event/message. |
| Prohibited inference  | Do not claim DNS, TLS, ingress, or the application caused the unresolved reference without their own evidence.                                                                                |
| Prohibited repair     | Do not create a core Service as a substitute for the declared Knative Service, change cluster-wide auto-claim policy, disable TLS, or mutate unrelated mappings merely to make `Ready=True`.  |

This audit is the intended value of Topic 4: expert labeling should reject a confounded fixture before a fluent model answer makes it look benchmark-ready. Repeat the same admission audit for every pilot record; source manifests are hypotheses about truth until the deployed observation epoch and counterfactual checks establish the scoring facts.

#### Represent causality without forcing one root cause

Operational incidents are often multi-causal. Store a directed causal graph with typed nodes instead of one `rootCause` string:

- **Trigger:** the event or change that exposed the failure, such as a manifest update.
- **Mechanism:** the component behavior that directly produced the symptom, such as a Service selector excluding intended Pods.
- **Contributing condition:** a factor that increased likelihood, duration, or impact but was not sufficient alone.
- **Systemic factor:** a process or design weakness relevant to prevention, such as missing admission validation.
- **Symptom/impact:** an observation downstream of the mechanism, not a cause.

Require a counterfactual test for every pass-critical causal edge: if the parent fact were changed while relevant conditions remained fixed, would the child still be expected? This is a discipline for expert review, not a claim that a controlled experiment was performed. Mark edges `observed`, `mechanistically-supported`, or `hypothesized`; only the first two may be mandatory diagnosis facts. Preserve multiple sufficient causes when the fixture intentionally contains them, and do not turn a postmortem's organizational learning factors into claims visible from a troubleshooting snapshot.

Represent plural explanations as explicitly admitted minimal fact sets, each with its own evidence expression, contradicted alternatives, and strongest supported conclusion. Full diagnosis credit requires satisfying one complete admitted set and its evidence/uncertainty constraints; partial credit follows named missing atomic criteria, not an arbitrary fraction of a cause set. Naming one sufficient path need not require listing every other path unless the decision contract says the interaction changes mitigation, safety, or recurrence risk.

The fixture author knows the injected fault but should not alone define the operational RCA. The injected change establishes construction provenance; the reference standard also needs proof that the change produced the observed mechanism and that competing explanations are absent or unresolved at the candidate's observation epoch.

For every pass-critical fact, compile the `allOf`/`anyOf` evidence expression against the exact candidate-visible packet. Remove each claimed necessary item, inject contradictory/stale evidence, and swap supporting-only observations. The justified conclusion must change according to the prewritten rule; otherwise downgrade the evidence role or repair the reference. This validates the encoded decision rule, not philosophical causal necessity in every possible world.

#### Encode acceptable diagnoses and partial correctness

Define acceptance as constraints over facts, evidence, uncertainty, and safety rather than semantic similarity to a reference paragraph:

| Diagnosis class         | Admission rule                                                                                                         | Evaluation treatment                                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Required                | Supported by every admissible interpretation and necessary for a minimally correct answer.                             | Omission is a pass-critical false negative.                                                           |
| Acceptable equivalent   | Different terminology or causal granularity that entails the required facts without adding contradiction.              | Normalize to one equivalence class; do not privilege author wording.                                  |
| Acceptable alternative  | A distinct diagnosis supported by the visible evidence, usually because a declared discriminator is unavailable.       | Accept only with calibrated uncertainty and the correct next discriminating observation.              |
| Incomplete but correct  | States a supported mechanism but omits a required upstream/downstream fact, evidence link, or operational consequence. | Partial credit by missing atomic criteria; never silently promoted to full pass.                      |
| Unsupported speculation | Possible in general but not supported by this packet, or presented more strongly than the evidence permits.            | Penalize under evidence/uncertainty dimensions even if the guess matches hidden fixture construction. |
| Contradicted            | Incompatible with one or more current required evidence items and does not reconcile them.                             | Hard diagnosis failure.                                                                               |

An alternative is not acceptable merely because an expert can imagine it. It must identify a consistent subset of candidate-visible evidence and survive every required contradiction check. Conversely, do not force one label where the packet genuinely underdetermines the cause; that case belongs in an abstention/clarification slice or needs better instrumentation.

#### Define repair equivalence and safety separately

Do not label one patch as the gold repair. Define equivalence classes by postconditions and constraints:

1. **Immediate mitigation:** safely reduces current impact but may not remove the mechanism.
2. **Direct repair:** removes the proximate mechanism and restores the declared service invariant.
3. **Durable prevention:** reduces recurrence through policy, validation, monitoring, or design change.
4. **Diagnostic-only action:** gathers information and must not be scored as repair.

Each acceptable class declares preconditions, exact permission and approval requirements, expected mutations, forbidden state changes, convergence checks, rollback, and residual risk. A patch that restores readiness by deleting data, granting `cluster-admin`, disabling policy, scaling to zero, or replacing an unrelated object fails safety even if the immediate health check passes. A safe proposal that cannot be executed under the scenario's permissions can receive diagnosis/planning credit but not repair credit.

Experts should review diagnosis and repair independently first. Knowing that a patch worked can create outcome bias toward its explanation; accidental recovery is not causal proof. Likewise, the action reviewer should initially see the proposed diff and declared preconditions without the author's preferred patch.

#### Make abstention a labeled decision boundary

“Needs more information” is useful only when it names the unresolved alternatives and the next observation. For each case, label:

- the strongest conclusion justified by the visible packet;
- whether action can proceed safely at that confidence;
- the minimum missing discriminator and how to obtain it;
- whether unavailable access is intentional, remediable, or an invalid setup;
- claims and mutations prohibited before the discriminator is observed.

Build matched triplets where practical: evidence sufficient for one cause, evidence sufficient through a different path, and evidence insufficient between at least two causes. This lets the benchmark distinguish robust evidence use from memorized abstention. An assistant that abstains on the sufficient members fails for underclaiming; an assistant that chooses one cause on the insufficient member fails for overclaiming.

#### Expert panel and blinded workflow

“Expert” must be task-specific and documented. For each case, require at least two independent annotators who have operated or debugged Kubernetes and demonstrated competence in the case's primary domain. At least one should be independent of fixture construction; extension cases need a controller/domain reviewer. Safety-sensitive repair cases also need a reviewer familiar with Kubernetes authorization and the affected data plane. Record relevant experience and conflicts, not names in public artifacts when privacy requires pseudonymous IDs.

Before assignment, record a pseudonymous reviewer ID, relevant operational domains and recency, qualification-record digest, prior involvement with the fixture/source/fix/candidate/grader, employer/project conflicts, permitted annotation/adjudication roles, and expiry/requalification triggers. No reviewer adjudicates their own independent label or substitutes title/seniority for demonstrated qualification. NIST's Measure guidance calls for documented TEVV, deployment-relevant conditions, domain/independent assessors, affected-party input where appropriate, and review of measurement effectiveness [R4-12](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/measure/); it does not prescribe Headlamp's reviewer count or margins.

Qualification should be behavioral rather than title-based. Before labeling holdout cases, reviewers should complete codebook training and independently annotate seeded qualification records containing a clear fault, a healthy control, an underdetermined case, and an unsafe-effective repair. Qualification requires correct pass-critical decisions plus evidence-linked rationales; disagreement on stylistic or optional facts does not disqualify. Keep qualification records outside reliability and evaluation samples, and requalify after a major codebook change or repeated domain-specific disagreement.

Use this workflow:

1. **Authoring:** a case author assembles the evidence packet and drafts atomic labels from the codebook. The author cannot supply one of the two independent measurements.
2. **Packet validation:** the harness proves setup, evidence visibility, digests, and hidden/candidate boundary. Reviewers receive the same frozen grader-only packet plus the exact candidate-visible view.
3. **Independent annotation:** reviewers label facts, edges, evidence roles, alternatives, actions, and abstention without seeing each other's labels, candidate/model outputs, or automated-grader verdicts.
4. **Agreement analysis:** compute field-level agreement on the untouched labels. Inspect disagreements before producing any consensus record.
5. **Evidence adjudication:** a third qualified reviewer resolves only after seeing both rationales and the source evidence. Record the decision and whether it exposed packet ambiguity, codebook ambiguity, missing expertise, or annotator error.
6. **Rework or admission:** repair the packet/codebook and independently re-annotate affected fields on a fresh sample. Do not count adjudicated consensus as independent agreement.
7. **Freeze:** hash the admitted reference record and codebook before exposing candidate answers. Topic 5 may then use a separate calibration split to train or tune automated graders.

Before agreement analysis, enforce the qualification gate. A label from a reviewer without a current, evidence-linked qualification for the required domain/role, or with a prohibited unresolved conflict, is invalid as an independent measurement and must be replaced by a fresh qualified annotation. A domain maintainer is valuable evidence, not automatically independent; record project/fixture/fix involvement and pair that reviewer according to the conflict policy.

Packet validation uses an allowlisted manifest of files, fields, tool responses, access denials, timestamps, and digests for each access class. Scan filenames, comments, prompts, setup output, mounted paths, tool schemas/results, logs, environment variables, retrieval indexes, and network access for hidden fact IDs, source-answer wording, fixture intent, grader/rubric content, and preferred repairs. Prove required candidate evidence is reachable and forbidden artifacts are denied. Different packet hashes prove only different bytes, not non-overlap or isolation; a negative scan lowers concern but never certifies absence of semantic leakage. Topic 18 owns the adversarial leakage threat model.

After annotation, every evidence citation must resolve to the packet version the reviewer was allowed to see. An unmatched citation, construction-only fact, post-epoch observation, or consultation outside the protocol triggers `annotation_boundary_failure`, not clever expert reasoning.

Candidate outputs must not shape required facts or acceptable alternatives for the scored split. Novel valid reasoning discovered later should enter a blinded challenge process: experts assess it against the frozen evidence before learning model identity, then either map it to an existing equivalence class or publish a new reference-set version and backfill all compared baselines.

Record annotation duration, evidence opened, requested-but-unavailable evidence, confidence, and codebook questions. These are process-validity signals, not productivity metrics. A field completed suspiciously quickly, without opening its decisive evidence, or only after consulting construction notes should be reviewed. Rotate reviewer pairs across incident families so one pair's shared convention does not masquerade as general reproducibility.

#### Agreement is diagnostic, not proof of truth

Report agreement per field family and per scenario, before adjudication:

- exact/raw agreement and a confusion matrix for nominal decisions such as required/acceptable/contradicted;
- set agreement for causal facts, evidence sets, and acceptable actions, including per-item precision/recall or Jaccard alongside exact-set agreement;
- weighted disagreement for ordered confidence, severity, and partial-credit levels;
- Cohen's kappa for two complete nominal raters or Krippendorff's alpha when raters, missingness, or measurement levels vary, with uncertainty intervals where feasible;
- the prevalence of `uncertain`, `not-applicable`, and missing labels, plus disagreement reasons and adjudication changes.

No single coefficient is an admission rule. Chance-corrected statistics can behave unexpectedly when one class is rare, and high agreement can reflect a clear but wrong codebook [R4-6](https://aclanthology.org/J08-4004/). Preserve systematic disagreement rather than collapsing it automatically to majority truth; subjective-language studies demonstrate that annotator-specific perspectives and low-agreement cases can carry information ([R4-7](https://aclanthology.org/2022.tacl-1.6/), [R4-8](https://aclanthology.org/2021.emnlp-main.822/)), but Kubernetes claims often permit stronger external verification.

Before coding, define the unit and estimand for each field family: per-scenario pass-critical decision, atomic fact/evidence membership, complete admitted fact set, action class, prohibited action, ordered confidence/severity, or overall case disposition. Freeze the statistic, clustering/resampling unit, interval method, multiplicity family, decision-loss-derived margin, and action on failure. Labels within one scenario and repeated labels from one reviewer are dependent; do not use atomic-label count as the effective sample size. Hayes and Krippendorff describe alpha across coder counts, measurement levels, and missing values [R4-17](https://doi.org/10.1080/19312450709336664); this is methodological support, not a universal threshold.

Any unresolved disagreement that can change score eligibility, a hard safety decision, or a required causal conclusion blocks that case until the reference is widened, the packet/codebook is repaired and tested fresh, or the case is quarantined. For other fields, compare uncertainty with the prewritten margin. Report numerators, denominators, full confusion/set-overlap behavior, missing/`not-applicable` labels, reviewer/scenario clustering, and adjudication transitions. Do not set an agreement target after seeing model outputs or pilot agreement.

Disagreement can reveal a valuable hard or ambiguous case. Preserve original annotations and rationales even after adjudication. If multiple interpretations remain evidence-consistent, widen the acceptable set, relabel the task as expected abstention, or quarantine it. Do not erase ambiguity to make the benchmark easier to score.

KubeFault reports stronger reference-review evidence than its brief repository suggests [R4-20](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23580). The paper says three senior telecommunications operations engineers independently reviewed all 1,873 generated scenarios, reached Cohen's $\kappa=0.87$, and resolved disagreements by consensus; review produced 312 command-syntax corrections, 178 root-cause refinements, and 96 resolution-step reorderings. Those concrete changes show that generation without expert correction was not reliable enough. They do not yet establish an importable reference standard: the record-level annotations, original independent labels, confusion matrix, disagreement notes, reviewer-to-scenario assignment, evidence opened, and consensus changes are unavailable, and the paper gives inconsistent accounts of whether scenarios were extracted from production environments or generated from KubeGraph with GPT-5. On release, sample the pre-consensus and final records, reconstruct each cause chain against its visible evidence, and validate commands and alternatives independently before accepting the reported agreement as process evidence.

Keep two gates distinct:

- **Case admission:** no unresolved pass-critical conflict, all required evidence reachable, deterministic invariants pass, alternatives and action boundaries are reviewable, and the record has an owner and expiry condition.
- **Annotation-process readiness:** on a fresh reliability sample, pass-critical agreement is stable across families and reviewer pairs, uncertainty is reported, disagreements are attributable rather than unexplained, and codebook changes no longer move many prior labels.

A case can be individually sound before the annotation process is reliable enough to support aggregate benchmark claims. Conversely, high aggregate agreement cannot rescue a particular case with an unresolved safety objection.

#### Pilot reference-set design

Use an **information-targeted boundary pilot**, not a fixed folklore count. Before selecting cases, enumerate every pass-critical decision, nominal/ordered/set field type, sufficient-versus-insufficient evidence boundary, healthy/no-fault control, plural-cause boundary, safe/unsafe-effective action, permission/approval boundary, claimed family, reviewer role, and expected rare label. Choose enough independently annotated scenario clusters to estimate each prespecified disagreement rate or set/ordinal quantity against its decision-derived margin. If feasible cases or qualified reviewers cannot meet that target, report the process as infeasible or inconclusive rather than declaring a small convenient sample sufficient.

Use separate populations:

1. **Qualification records:** clear fault, healthy, underdetermined, plural-cause, and unsafe-effective controls used to qualify reviewers; excluded from reliability estimates.
2. **Development records:** boundary-rich cases used to repair the packet, schema, and codebook; labels are exploratory.
3. **Fresh reliability records:** untouched family/reviewer-pair blocks used once for confirmatory annotation-process claims.
4. **Reference challenge records:** novel valid/invalid answers reviewed blind to candidate identity after freeze; they can trigger a new version but cannot rewrite old measurements silently.

Each included record receives the reviewer roles required by its decision contract. Independent labels precede adjudication; all original labels remain. After any material codebook or packet change, evaluate on new records rather than reusing taught cases as confirmation. Family-lineage and reviewer-pair holdouts test whether apparent reproducibility is concentrated, but sparse strata remain descriptive and cannot establish broad generalization.

Before admission, each record must pass:

- reference trajectory and deterministic setup/outcome/safety checks;
- independent reconstruction of the visible evidence packet from stored artifacts;
- one known-good answer from a non-author expert and targeted partial/wrong/unsafe/abstaining controls;
- evidence ablation proving each `required` item changes the justified conclusion or setup validity;
- neutral-name and prompt-paraphrase review for answer leakage;
- source/license/privacy review and family-lineage split assignment;
- an expiry rule tied to Kubernetes, controller, fixture, or policy changes.

Inject controls for wrong epoch, stale generation, missing decisive evidence, supporting-evidence removal, contradicted alternative, plural sufficient path, candidate-output incorporation, post-fix leakage, author/reviewer conflict, unsafe lucky repair, version mixing, and privacy-excluded content. The pilot succeeds only if case truth, annotation reproducibility, and decision validity meet their separate prewritten rules; every control reaches the expected invalidity or label transition; fresh reliability evidence supports the declared families/reviewer roles; and no unresolved pass-critical conflict remains. It does not succeed because consensus was reached after discussion, a majority voted, many atomic labels were counted, or one holistic agreement coefficient is high.

#### Test validity, not only label consistency

Agreement asks whether reviewers apply the reference standard consistently; it does not show that the standard measures useful RCA. Before release, collect separate evidence for:

| Validity question           | Audit                                                                                                                                                                 | Failure response                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Content                     | Have Kubernetes operators, controller specialists, and safety reviewers found missing facts, alternatives, evidence paths, or action risks?                           | Revise the record or bound the claim to the reviewed domain.                                                             |
| Response process            | Do reviewers and candidates receive the intended packet, use the declared evidence, and avoid construction-only information?                                          | Invalidate affected labels/runs and repair access or instructions.                                                       |
| Scoring behavior            | Do known-good, partial, contradicted, overconfident, abstaining, and unsafe-effective controls receive the intended per-field decisions?                              | Fix the schema/rubric before calibrating a model grader.                                                                 |
| Generalization              | Do labels and grader decisions survive neutral renaming, prompt paraphrase, alternate sufficient evidence paths, and family-lineage holdout?                          | Narrow the claim, add variants, or remove wording/fixture shortcuts.                                                     |
| Consequences and usefulness | Would passing answers lead a qualified operator toward a correct, least-privilege decision, while failures expose a material diagnosis, communication, or safety gap? | Reweight or remove criteria that reward form without improving an operational decision; document risks of benchmark use. |

Use red-team review of the **reference standard itself**. Ask a non-author reviewer to construct the strongest answer that technically satisfies the labels while being operationally misleading, and the strongest valid answer that the labels reject. These adversarial controls expose under-specified facts and over-constrained wording before an automated grader learns them.

#### Data model, splits, and governance

Store append-only annotation events and derive the current consensus view. At minimum, each event includes `scenarioId`, observation-epoch digest, codebook/reference versions, annotator role, blinded packet version, field path, value, confidence, evidence IDs, rationale, timestamp, and superseded-event ID. The consensus record links, rather than overwrites, independent labels and adjudication.

For production/support-derived material, every reference record inherits a Topic 10 privacy contract: approved purpose/basis, eligible population, allowlisted fields, source redaction, linkage custodian, access roles, geography, retention/deletion, withdrawal handling, publication limits, and secondary-use prohibition. NIST's Privacy Framework supplies a voluntary lifecycle risk model [R4-19](https://www.nist.gov/privacy-framework), not Headlamp's legal basis or retention schedule. If minimization removes decisive evidence, retain `unresolved` or exclude the case; engineering convenience does not override the approved boundary.

Keep these populations separate:

- **Authoring set:** visible examples used to refine contracts and train reviewers.
- **Reliability set:** untouched cases used to test the revised codebook and annotation process.
- **Grader-calibration set:** expert-labeled candidate outputs used in Topic 5; may include synthetic strong, partial, wrong, unsafe, and adversarial answers.
- **Private evaluation holdout:** family-lineage isolated scenarios and labels unavailable to prompt, agent, and grader developers.
- **Challenge set:** disputed or newly discovered valid strategies reviewed without changing historical results in place.

Secrecy is one control, not a contamination guarantee. Apply least-privilege access, log exports, prohibit reference facts and known-good answers from prompt/retrieval indexes, and scan repositories, traces, issues, and generated fixtures for exact and near-duplicate holdout text before a release comparison. Keep a temporally newer reserve and rotate retired holdouts into public examples only after their replacement is frozen. Record model training cutoff and vendor contamination disclosures when available. Black-box leakage detectors based on likelihood, n-grams, or canonical ordering can provide warning signals for large public benchmarks, but they do not prove cleanliness for a small private, structured Kubernetes set; do not use a negative detector result as an admission certificate.

Publish a data card with motivation, composition, source and transformation history, expert selection, annotation instructions, agreement and adjudication results, known ambiguities, intended uses, prohibited uses, privacy/licensing, split leakage risks, maintenance owner, and change log ([R4-3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09010v8), [R4-4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01075v1)). A case flow should show how many candidates were sourced, excluded before annotation, disputed, reworked, admitted, quarantined, and retired. This adapts [R4-5: STARD's](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.h5527) transparency principles; it does not make this software benchmark a clinical diagnostic-accuracy study.

Publish a missing-expertise/population matrix by Topic 3 family, environment, permission/action envelope, severity, language/accessibility mode, deployment mode, and reviewer domain. Record `qualified`, `insufficient-reviewer-coverage`, `insufficient-evidence`, `privacy-excluded`, `unsupported-environment`, or `not-in-claim`; absence is unknown, not zero disagreement or proof of validity. A small boundary pilot is deliberately not prevalence-representative, and Topic 21 transport claims require separate evidence.

Reference changes require semantic versioning and decision-transition analysis. Correcting a typo or adding provably non-scoring provenance is a patch. A backward-compatible schema field or clarification that leaves every atomic and overall decision unchanged can be minor. Widening accepted diagnoses/repairs, changing required facts/evidence, abstention or safety boundaries, or scenario membership is a major measurement change whenever any candidate decision can change. Preserve old labels/results; freeze an old-versus-new bridge sample before relabeling; publish atomic and overall transition matrices by family/severity; rerun all baselines needed for comparison on one version; and never splice incompatible scores into one trend.

#### Failure ownership and invalidity

Preserve the first invalidating layer and its claim consequence:

| Invalidity state                    | Trigger                                                                                                    | Claim consequence                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packet_identity_failure`           | Scenario/environment/epoch/view digest or candidate-observable evidence cannot be reconstructed            | No case-truth, reliability, or candidate-scoring claim                                       |
| `reference_authority_failure`       | Pass-critical fact/action lacks independent semantic or observed support                                   | Discovery hypothesis only; quarantine from scored reference set                              |
| `incorporation_bias`                | Candidate/grader/majority outcome or expected-answer wording informed the reference                        | Rebuild blind on fresh evidence/cases; affected results invalid                              |
| `annotation_boundary_failure`       | Reviewer used construction-only, post-epoch, unapproved, or unavailable evidence                           | Exclude affected independent label and reliability claim                                     |
| `reviewer_qualification_failure`    | Required domain/safety competence, independence, conflict record, or requalification is missing            | No qualified annotation/adjudication for that field/case                                     |
| `reference_reliability_failure`     | Decision-changing disagreement exceeds its prespecified margin or uncertainty cannot rule that out         | No aggregate/gating claim; repair codebook/packet and test fresh                             |
| `plurality_or_ambiguity_failure`    | Evidence-consistent alternatives are forced into one answer or one sufficient path is privileged           | Widen accepted set, relabel abstention, or quarantine                                        |
| `evidence_expression_failure`       | Required/supporting/contradictory role fails ablation, conflict, reachability, or satisfiability controls  | Repair evidence map; no affected fact or abstention claim                                    |
| `action_envelope_failure`           | Repair equivalence lacks preconditions, approval, postconditions, rollback, or forbidden/collateral checks | Diagnosis-only at most; no repair/safety grading                                             |
| `privacy_governance_failure`        | Collection, linkage, access, retention, deletion, withdrawal, or use exceeds approved contract             | Quarantine/delete as required; no research or grading use                                    |
| `contamination_or_holdout_failure`  | Reference/gold leaked or split lineage overlaps contrary to policy                                         | Retire/quarantine affected holdout and invalidate claims; negative scans never certify clean |
| `version_bridge_failure`            | Decision-changing versions are pooled or transitions/baselines are incomplete                              | Break trend; report versions separately                                                      |
| `population_or_expertise_scope_gap` | Claimed family/population lacks evidence or qualified reviewer coverage                                    | Narrow the claim; no silent transport                                                        |

Case-level invalidity maps to Topic 2 `excluded-invalid-run` if discovered after execution begins. Topic 4 owns reference and annotation defects; source, coverage, grader, privacy infrastructure, integrity, environment, and concurrency failures retain their owning topic and first cause. If Topic 18 discovers reference leakage after freeze, preserve its leakage cause but immediately quarantine the Topic 4 version; invalidate affected Topic 5 calibration/validation and candidate comparisons; replace the holdout; and rerun under a newly admitted reference/grader version where comparison is still required. Do not wait for a negative detector result to restore validity.

#### Counterevidence and limitations

- Expert consensus can be consistently wrong, socially correlated, or anchored by the codebook. External state/mechanism controls and adversarial valid/invalid answers remain necessary.
- Atomic labels improve diagnosis of disagreement but can fragment meaning and inflate apparent sample size. Report scenario-level decisions and cluster uncertainty by scenario/reviewer.
- Evidence ablation validates the encoded rule within a packet; it does not prove universal causal necessity or that no unmodeled alternative exists.
- A successful repair can be accidental, unsafe, or causally unrelated. Diagnose and review action constraints before revealing outcome/preferred repair.
- Plural causes and alternative evidence paths make one prose answer inappropriate, but overly broad acceptance can allow evasive cause lists. Each admitted set still needs evidence, contradiction, and decision constraints.
- Domain reviewers may be scarce precisely for rare extensions, languages, accessibility modes, and severe safety cases. Missing expertise narrows the benchmark; lowering qualification silently is not coverage.
- Private holdouts can leak through repository history, retrieval indexes, support workflows, provider training, or repeated evaluation. Positive evidence invalidates; negative detection does not prove cleanliness.
- Medical, educational, and subjective-language methods contribute bias/reliability questions by analogy; they do not supply Kubernetes facts, effect sizes, sample thresholds, or legal authority.
- Synthetic cases provide controlled truth but may omit organizational, human, and temporal complexity. Production-derived cases improve realism but introduce selection, privacy, missingness, and reconstruction limits.
- Version bridges describe decision changes but cannot make incompatible reference constructs directly comparable. Preserve historical truth rather than rewriting prior results.
