Release gates read only validated canonical results and their manifests. Hosted annotations can be imported as new provenance-bearing records and regraded, never edited into the original result.

#### OpenTelemetry projection profile

Map one **trial** to one root trace. Keep the root span name low-cardinality, for example `eval.trial`, and put stable run identifiers in attributes rather than the name. Use OpenTelemetry resource attributes only for process/deployment identity shared by many records: service name/version, runner build, deployment environment, and instrumentation scope. Scenario, candidate, trial, and dataset values belong on spans because they vary per run.

| Canonical concept             | OpenTelemetry projection                                                                                                                                                                           | Required caveat                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Trial                         | Root `eval.trial` span with opaque `headlamp.eval.run.id`, scenario revision/digest, candidate/config digest, trial ordinal, fixture backend, eligibility, and outcome                             | OpenTelemetry trace ID is correlation only; it is not the canonical run ID or idempotency key                                                                            |
| Setup and fault injection     | Child stage spans with setup/fault IDs, attempts, condition summaries, and artifact references                                                                                                     | Candidate-hidden setup and root cause must not be exported to candidate-visible destinations                                                                             |
| User/assistant turn           | Child turn/model spans and ordered message events when content policy allows                                                                                                                       | Full messages and system instructions are opt-in, sensitive GenAI attributes; keep role/order/digest and protected artifact reference when content is suppressed         |
| Model request                 | GenAI inference span with requested/returned provider and model, parameters, response ID, finish reason, token subsets, latency, retries, cache data, and error class                              | Pin the GenAI convention snapshot and retain raw provider accounting in canonical records; vendor normalization can merge provider/model names and token categories      |
| Tool discovery and execution  | Tool/MCP child spans with stable tool ID, schema digest, call ID, attempt, approval reference, arguments/result projection, duration, status, and error class                                      | Tool arguments and Kubernetes results are untrusted sensitive content; large values are artifacts, not attributes                                                        |
| Approval and policy decision  | Ordered span event or child span with request ID, policy version, scope digest, decision, actor class, timing, expiry, and continuation                                                            | Do not export user identity or displayed/requested payload unless the destination's policy explicitly permits it                                                         |
| Grader                        | `eval.grader` child span plus `gen_ai.evaluation.result` event with grader ID/version, score value/label, applicability, and error; evidence/rationale referenced separately                       | The development convention cannot represent full rubric, contradictory evidence, calibration, invalidity, or safety precedence, so canonical grader records remain truth |
| Verifier and cleanup          | Child spans with assertion-set digest, final-state/cleanup status, attempts, residue class, and artifact references                                                                                | A healthy HTTP span or completed cleanup call does not prove the Kubernetes final-state oracle                                                                           |
| Pair/composition relationship | Stable repository pair/group ID on roots plus span links where traces are available                                                                                                                | Links are optional telemetry and cannot define pairing or statistical independence                                                                                       |
| Artifact                      | URI or opaque object key, digest, media type, size, sensitivity and retention class                                                                                                                | Never embed manifests, logs, screenshots, archives, or base64 objects in span attributes                                                                                 |
| Aggregate metric              | Low-cardinality counters/histograms derived after canonical closure: eligible trials, hard pass, unsafe action, invalid owner/stage, latency/cost, export rejection/drop, and redaction violations | Do not use run, user, resource, prompt, or unbounded scenario IDs as metric dimensions; never reconstruct release decisions from sampled metrics                         |

OpenTelemetry spans provide one parent, links, timestamped events, status, and typed attributes, but event timestamps can be supplied out of order and a child can outlive its parent [R17-1](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/trace/api/). Preserve canonical `sequence` and `event_id` on every exported unit; wall-clock order and a vendor Gantt chart are not a substitute. Use span links for baseline/candidate, metamorphic, retried, and asynchronous relationships that are not ownership trees.

Keep three different statuses:

- `operation_status`: whether setup, model, tool, grader, verifier, cleanup, or export execution succeeded; this controls OpenTelemetry span status;
- `eval_outcome`: candidate pass, fail, partial, abstain, unsafe, or no-result according to canonical graders;
- `run_eligibility`: valid, invalid with owner/stage, inconclusive, or quarantined.

A correctly executed trial in which the candidate gives the wrong answer should normally have a successful root operation and `eval_outcome=fail`, not an OpenTelemetry error. Conversely, an evaluator timeout is an operation error and often a no-result, not evidence that the candidate failed.

The pinned OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions define inference, agent, tool/MCP, message, usage, and `gen_ai.evaluation.result` telemetry, but the inspected snapshot is Development; message content is opt-in and explicitly sensitive, the repository has no published release at that snapshot, and its schema URL remains unresolved [R17-7](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/tree/94f432d7126f5884d30a2cdde6f4e89908ebb6fd/docs/gen-ai). Treat those conventions as a versioned export profile. Put Headlamp-only fields under a documented `headlamp.eval.*` namespace and do not rename the canonical fields whenever a development convention changes.

#### Adapter contract and conformance

Each adapter must implement a narrow interface over closed canonical bundles:

- `qualify(config)`: report supported canonical/profile versions, destination capabilities, plan/region prerequisites, size/rate/retention limits, and unsupported required fields;
- `project(bundle, policy)`: deterministically produce the destination-safe records plus a field-level loss/redaction manifest without network access;
- `validate(payload)`: enforce schema, type, cardinality, size, secret-canary, parent/reference, and destination-profile rules before enqueueing;
- `export(payload, idempotency)`: send with bounded retries and return a receipt without altering canonical outcome;
- `flush(deadline)` and `health()`: expose queue age, depth, drops, permanent rejection, credential/config errors, and last acknowledged watermark;
- `reverseExport(range)`: page through all relevant remote records, preserve raw response artifacts, normalize them to the adapter's comparison model, and return completeness evidence;
- `delete(range)` where supported: request deletion and retain a non-sensitive receipt and later verification result.

Do not put vendor SDK objects in the canonical schema. Adapters receive plain validated records and return plain receipts. Run vendor integrations out of process or behind a queue where practical so an SDK's global tracer, callback order, exceptions, network latency, or dependency upgrades cannot change candidate execution.

For source canonical bundle $C$, disclosure transform $D_p$, destination projection $P_v$, remote materialization/export $E_v$, normalization $N_v$, and the fields a profile promises to preserve $\pi_v$, require:

$$
\pi_v(D_p(C)) = \pi_v(N_v(E_v(P_v(D_p(C)))))
$$

and separately require that prohibited canaries are absent from serialized payloads, Collector output, destination queries, reverse exports, logs, errors, and attachments. Privacy-preserving loss is intentional: the test compares the approved disclosure view $D_p(C)$, never demands recovery of withheld raw content.

The conformance corpus must exercise more than a happy trace:

- null versus absent, `false`, zero, empty string/list/map, Unicode, long strings, decimal strings, maximum safe integers, timestamps and durations at supported precision;
- every stage, actor, terminal outcome, invalid owner, grader score/label/error, safety precedence, pair/link, tool approval, retry, cancellation, and cleanup residue;
- sibling concurrency, child-before-parent delivery, parent omission, a child ending after its parent, equal timestamps, and explicit canonical sequence;
- payloads just below and above SDK, Collector, and destination attribute/event/span/request limits;
- duplicates, updates, reconnect retries, pagination boundaries, late records, partial acceptance, `429`, permanent `4xx`, transient `5xx`, timeout, queue overflow, crash/restart, and flush deadline;
- redaction canaries in every nested string, key, URL, header, exception, model message, tool schema/argument/result, Kubernetes object, artifact, and vendor error path;
- an old canonical bundle, current bundle with unknown additive fields, migrated bundle, and unsupported major version;
- summary-only versus child-span exports, numeric and categorical feedback, deleted/expired records, and artifact references whose objects are unavailable.

Compare record counts, stable IDs, parent/link graph, sequence, values and types, absent/null distinctions, timestamp precision, outcomes, scores, artifact digests, disclosure classes, and destination receipts. A profile passes only if every promised field round-trips, every declared loss is observed and no undeclared loss occurs. Preserve the remote raw export because a normalizer can otherwise hide a vendor regression.

#### Platform profiles

OpenTelemetry compatibility means a platform can ingest or emit a common telemetry envelope; it does not imply a common evaluation dataset, scorer, artifact, retention, query, or export model.

| Profile                        | Useful capability                                                                                                                                               | Qualification and exit risk                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| No sink / repository only      | Complete offline execution, deterministic reports and release gates, no account or network                                                                      | Must still test crash-safe writes, bundle validation, retention, access control, and report regeneration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Local Collector + OTLP file    | Exercises OTLP encoding, processors, fan-out, and replay without a hosted service                                                                               | Collector file exporter is alpha for traces/logs/metrics and warns field names are unstable; use it as a test capture, not the sole archive [R17-23](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/exporter/fileexporter)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Braintrust                     | OTLP endpoint, GenAI/vendor attribute mapping, nested eval/task/LLM/tool/score views, experiments, feedback, and cloud/self-hosted data-plane options           | Mapping deletes/translates some source attributes; export must select spans rather than summary traces for children, page beyond endpoint limits, and deduplicate updates by stable ID plus transaction order [R17-9](https://www.braintrust.dev/docs/guides/traces/integrations/opentelemetry) [R17-10](https://braintrust.dev/docs/kb/export-missing-child-spans.md) [R17-11](https://braintrust.dev/docs/kb/use-xact-id-to-dedupe-exports-and-determine-update-time.md)                                                                                   |
| LangSmith                      | Native LangChain traces, OTLP ingestion/fan-out, run trees, threads, feedback, offline/online evaluation, datasets, and bulk Parquet exports                    | Vendor run UUIDs/dotted order and flattened trajectory are projections; missing parents can cause asynchronously accepted children to disappear; retention, run/trace limits, rates, and bulk export availability depend on plan/version [R17-12](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/trace-with-opentelemetry) [R17-13](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export) [R17-14](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/usage-and-billing)                                                                                                                 |
| MLflow                         | Open-source local server, GenAI datasets/evaluation, OTLP ingestion and export, dual export, pluggable metadata/artifact stores, and managed variants           | "Compatible" still needs conformance for Headlamp graders, attachments, IDs, redaction and versions; self-hosting transfers database, object-store, auth, backup, migration, and capacity work to the operator [R17-15](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/genai/tracing/opentelemetry/) [R17-16](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/)                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Foundry + Application Insights | Cloud evaluators, tracing, monitoring, alerts, OpenTelemetry integration, configurable Azure retention and query/export ecosystem                               | Evaluation and telemetry schemas, evaluator availability, region, preview state, sampling, retention, ingestion/egress, and pricing are Azure-specific; portal status is not a Headlamp gate [R17-17](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/observability) [R17-18](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/application-insights-faq)                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Vertex AI + Google Cloud Trace | Managed GenAI/agent evaluation, SDK/console workflows, OTLP trace ingestion, Cloud Trace/Observability Analytics, regional storage, quotas, and linked BigQuery | Eval and trace are separate services; interface generations and previews coexist; trace retention/limits are cloud-specific, and the older BigQuery trace-sink exit path is already deprecated, demonstrating why export drills must be recurrent [R17-19](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/evaluation-overview) [R17-20](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/quotas) [R17-21](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/storage-overview) [R17-22](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/trace-export-overview) |

Start with repository-only and local MLflow or an OTLP capture as reference profiles, then qualify one hosted collaboration sink. Do not select a platform from a feature checklist alone. Use the same golden bundles and compare:

- field/type/graph round-trip and undeclared-loss count;
- supported local, CI, air-gapped, private-network, hosted, and self-hosted modes;
- raw and derived artifact support, maximum sizes, multipart behavior, and export completeness;
- content controls before SDK, in Collector, at ingestion, at rest, in UI/query, in exports, and on deletion;
- retention minimum/maximum, per-object exceptions, legal hold, region, backup, purge latency, and metadata retained after content deletion;
- ingest/query/export/evaluator limits, asynchronous visibility delay, backpressure, pagination, late update and duplicate semantics;
- measured SDK CPU/RAM/startup and candidate-path latency, bytes/spans/events per valid trial, storage growth, evaluator/model charges, network egress, and operating labor;
- API/SDK/schema release state, changelog and deprecation policy, migration tools, IaC coverage, and support model;
- full exit time, export cost, normalized completeness, artifact recovery, dashboard/report replacement, and deletion verification.

Pricing and limits are configuration evidence, not constants in the canonical schema. Snapshot the quoted plan/region URLs and tested values in each qualification report, then probe behavior at safe boundaries. Documentation can lag deployed enforcement, and custom enterprise limits cannot be inferred from public tables.

#### Privacy, redaction, and retention

Define disclosure at field creation, not as a regex pass immediately before upload:

| Class                 | Examples                                                                                                            | Default handling                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Public synthetic      | Published scenario ID, synthetic resource names, public taxonomy, harness version                                   | Export to qualified sinks under normal retention                                                                                                      |
| Operational aggregate | Counts, buckets, coarse error/stage, provider/model version, cost/latency, sampled cohort                           | Export with low-cardinality dimensions and no reconstructable content                                                                                 |
| Pseudonymous          | Opaque run/session/pair IDs and stable subject IDs needed for joins                                                 | Scope per environment, rotate or tokenize where possible, restrict access/retention; hashing a small identifier space is not anonymization            |
| Confidential content  | Prompts, model output, tool arguments/results, logs, manifests, cluster names, object metadata, grader rationale    | Local encrypted artifact by default; export only through an approved destination-specific allowlist and retention policy                              |
| Secret/prohibited     | Credentials, Secret values, tokens, kubeconfigs, private keys, authentication headers, customer identifiers         | Do not collect or serialize; fail canary tests and invalidate the export pipeline if detected                                                         |
| Eval-confidential     | Holdout identity, hidden facts, contradictory evidence, grader prompts, reference trajectories, transformation seed | Separate grader-only store and identity; never include in candidate-visible traces or a sink the candidate, provider, or untrusted reviewer can query |

OpenTelemetry makes the implementer responsible for consent, minimization, and sensitive-data handling and recommends preventing collection before relying on processors [R17-4](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/security/handling-sensitive-data/). The GenAI conventions also mark messages, prompt variables, instructions, and tool definitions as sensitive opt-in content [R17-7](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/tree/94f432d7126f5884d30a2cdde6f4e89908ebb6fd/docs/gen-ai). Therefore:

- use a schema-aware allowlist over typed canonical fields and artifact classes; regex redaction is defense in depth;
- apply disclosure before invoking any vendor SDK so SDK debug logs, exceptions, queues, retries, and automatic instrumentation never receive prohibited raw data;
- use a second independently configured Collector allowlist/filter for hosted routes and test its post-transform output;
- scan destination payloads and reverse exports with synthetic canaries; include canaries in nested keys and values because models can repeat a secret in an otherwise innocent answer;
- keep destination credentials out of the browser plugin and candidate environment; use short-lived workload identity or secret stores in the runner/export service;
- separate synthetic eval projects from privacy-reviewed production projects, credentials, retention, access groups, and export destinations;
- record policy version and field-level action (`allow`, `tokenize`, `truncate`, `drop`, `artifact-ref`) without recording the prohibited value;
- treat a URL as content: query strings, object names, bucket paths, share tokens, signed URLs, and trace links can disclose identities or credentials;
- verify deletion by ID and time range after the documented propagation period, including datasets, feedback, attachments, exports, caches and backups where the contract permits verification.

The existing `redactSecrets()` utility is useful input to the canary corpus, but it is text-pattern based and is designed for content sent to an LLM or UI. It is not sufficient as the exporter policy engine for typed nested records, binary artifacts, URLs, vendor metadata, or future fields.

Retention is independent at every layer: canonical bundle, CI artifact, local queue/WAL, Collector file, hosted trace, platform dataset/experiment, cloud export, object storage, backup, and imported report. Set an owner and deletion policy for each. A platform may retain datasets longer than traces, keep billing metadata after user content deletion, or charge based on ingested data despite later deletion. Never promise deletion, lower cost, or legal compliance from a UI setting alone.

#### Durability, limits, and cost

Write canonical events before handing them to optional exporters. Use one bounded queue and acknowledgement watermark per destination so a slow sink does not block another. OTLP defines retryable and permanent failures, partial success, backpressure, and possible duplicates but explicitly does not guarantee delivery across a multi-hop pipeline [R17-3](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otlp/). The Collector's in-memory queue can overflow and loses data on crash; a file-backed WAL improves restart behavior but still loses data on disk failure, exhaustion, or retry expiry [R17-5](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/resiliency/).

Required exporter behavior:

- bounded exponential backoff with jitter and `Retry-After` support; never retry permanent schema/auth/size failures indefinitely;
- deterministic destination idempotency key from canonical run/event identity and projection profile, not trace ID;
- duplicate-tolerant reverse normalization and explicit update/version semantics;
- payload sizing before enqueue, configurable batches below tested destination limits, externalized large artifacts, and a permanent-rejection dead letter;
- flush on normal process exit with a deadline, plus startup recovery of a persistent queue where enabled;
- health metrics for queue depth/age/capacity, attempts, accepted/rejected/dropped records, partial success, last acknowledgement, dead letters, and reverse-export lag;
- no unbounded memory buffering, synchronous network call in the candidate critical path, silent drop, or conversion of export failure into model failure;
- an export-completeness record at run and experiment level so a report can distinguish `complete`, `pending`, `partial`, `failed`, `expired`, and `not_configured`.

Measure total integration cost rather than only the platform subscription:

$$
C_{valid}=\frac{C_{model}+C_{judge}+C_{ingest}+C_{retention}+C_{query}+C_{export}+C_{egress}+C_{compute}+C_{ops}}{N_{valid}}
$$

Report also cost per successful safe task, per retained artifact byte-month, and per production sample. Record actual bytes before/after compression and redaction, spans/events/metrics, create/update/query/export calls, retries and duplicates, sampled/dropped units, storage duration, evaluator calls, and human operating time. A cheap sink with incomplete reverse export, high invalidity, or expensive maintenance is not cheap. Do not combine provider-reported estimates and invoiced charges without labels and uncertainty.

Apply backpressure to the optional export queue, not to candidate reasoning. If local durable capacity crosses a predeclared safety watermark, stop scheduling new evals or mark observability degraded rather than deleting the oldest failures. Sampling may be appropriate for production observability, but release eval trials and their canonical trajectories are census records; never sample away failed, unsafe, invalid, or cleanup-failed trials from the authoritative bundle.

#### Schema evolution and vendor exit

Version four contracts independently:

1. canonical scenario/trajectory/grader/result and bundle schemas;
2. disclosure policy and OpenTelemetry projection profile;
3. OpenTelemetry API/SDK/OTLP and pinned semantic-convention snapshot;
4. destination API/SDK, plan, region, storage/export format, and normalizer.

Every payload and receipt carries all four where applicable. Maintain forward readers for unknown additive canonical fields, explicit migrations for supported older versions, golden files for each retained version, and a hard refusal for an unsupported major version. A migration produces a new artifact with source digest and migration ID; it does not rewrite historical evidence in place.

OpenTelemetry schemas identify telemetry versions and reversible transformations, but they intentionally describe only a limited class of semantic-convention changes [R17-6](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/schemas/). They do not migrate Headlamp's scenario truth, grader rubric, safety precedence, artifacts, or vendor-native eval records. The current GenAI schema URL gap makes a separate pinned Headlamp projection version mandatory.

Treat destination changes as data migrations even when the OTLP endpoint remains stable. Re-run conformance on SDK/API upgrades, semantic-convention changes, destination release-stage changes, plan/region moves, retention changes, new processors, and normalizer changes. Compare old and new adapters against the same bundle before dual-writing production data.

A credible exit plan is an exercised restore, not a clause saying "supports export":

1. Export every required trace/span, dataset case, score/feedback, artifact, annotation, configuration and access-independent report over a fixed watermark.
2. Follow every cursor and partition, wait for late updates, deduplicate by stable record/version, and reconcile counts and IDs against canonical export receipts.
3. Normalize to an open repository-owned archive; record fields that cannot be exported, plan/API restrictions, and remote-only derived views.
4. Rebuild representative reports and investigations with exporters disabled and in a clean local environment.
5. Redirect new exports to another qualified sink without changing runner, grader, gate, or canonical schemas; compare a dual-write overlap.
6. Revoke credentials, stop automations, request deletion, and verify documented surfaces after the retention window while preserving non-sensitive receipts.

Classify a profile `portable` only when all required fields and artifacts round-trip and the clean restore works; `portable-with-declared-loss` when optional collaboration/UI data cannot be recovered but gates and investigations can; `blocked` when required evidence, scores, artifacts, configuration, export entitlement, or deletion cannot be obtained. Run a small reverse-export check continuously and a full exit drill on a scheduled cadence. Braintrust's trace-versus-span export modes and update duplicates [R17-10](https://braintrust.dev/docs/kb/export-missing-child-spans.md) [R17-11](https://braintrust.dev/docs/kb/use-xact-id-to-dedupe-exports-and-determine-update-time.md), LangSmith's plan-gated beta export format [R17-13](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/data-export), and Google's deprecated trace-sink path are concrete reasons not to postpone this test until an exit [R17-22](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/trace-export-overview).

#### Local implementation implications

The repository currently has product/runtime seams but no eval telemetry abstraction:

- [AssistantSession.ts](../packages/ai-common/src/assistant/AssistantSession.ts) owns framework-neutral conversation history and lifecycle but exposes no typed event observer.
- [LangChainAssistantSession.ts](../packages/ai-common/src/assistant/LangChainAssistantSession.ts) supports headless direct tool calling, making it usable by a future runner, but LangChain-native callbacks alone would omit fixture, verifier, cleanup, and some approval semantics.
- [ToolRuntime.ts](../packages/ai-common/src/tools/ToolRuntime.ts) is the nearest framework-neutral tool boundary and preserves tool call IDs and structured results, but it does not define eval event timing, attempts, disclosure, or artifact capture.
- [redactSecrets.ts](../packages/ai-common/src/security/redactSecrets.ts) provides tested text redaction but is not a typed export policy.
- The package manifests declare LangChain but no direct OpenTelemetry, Braintrust, LangSmith, or MLflow dependency. `langsmith` and `@opentelemetry/api` currently appear transitively in lockfiles or bundled dependencies; that is not a supported integration contract.

Add the canonical writer, validators, disclosure engine, OpenTelemetry projector, adapters, and gate reader to a future eval-runner package/CLI rather than the browser plugin or `AssistantSession` base class. If product sessions need observable hooks, define a small framework-neutral event sink injected by the runner and default it to no-op. Wrap the agent adapter, `ToolRuntime`, approval manager, fixture lifecycle, graders, verifier, and cleanup so the runner observes all stages without teaching product code about Braintrust or LangSmith.

Do not enable `LANGSMITH_TRACING`, global OpenTelemetry providers, or vendor auto-instrumentation merely because transitive packages support them. Initialization order and global providers can capture unrelated Headlamp/user traffic, duplicate spans, expose content, or change callback behavior. Qualification must use explicit dependency versions, an isolated provider where possible, destination-specific credentials held outside the candidate, and a shutdown/flush path owned by the runner.

#### Known-invalid controls

Reject designs or runs that:

- calculate a release gate from a hosted aggregate, dashboard query, sampled trace set, mutable playground, or vendor evaluator without a canonical row-level result;
- treat OpenTelemetry trace/span IDs, a LangSmith run UUID, Braintrust root span, MLflow trace ID, or cloud operation ID as the canonical run identity;
- upload the complete scenario manifest and thereby expose hidden root cause, prohibited actions, grader prompts, reference trajectory, or holdout identity;
- enable full prompt/output/tool capture by default because a GenAI integration offers it;
- run destination credentials or a privileged OTLP exporter in the browser, candidate container, or cluster service account being tested;
- apply regex redaction only after a vendor SDK, auto-instrumentor, logger, queue, or exception has already observed raw content;
- claim round-trip fidelity after checking only root spans, aggregate scores, row counts, or a few UI fields;
- omit pagination, child spans, feedback, late updates, duplicate/update resolution, expired records, or attachment retrieval from reverse export;
- assume HTTP `200`, OTLP full success, an empty exporter queue, or a visible root proves all remote children and fields materialized;
- count retries or duplicate exports as additional model trials, or let sink failures change candidate scores;
- block or slow candidate execution on an optional hosted exporter, silently discard old queue entries, or retry permanent failures forever;
- sample release-eval trajectories, unsafe actions, invalid runs, grader errors, cleanup failures, or export failures out of the authoritative store;
- put large logs, manifests, screenshots, archives, or base64 data in span attributes and rely on a destination not to truncate them;
- compare platform token or cost fields without preserving provider-native units, cache/reasoning subsets, price-map version, currency, and estimation source;
- assume self-hosted means offline, free, complete, or low-maintenance without testing licenses, image access, storage, auth, upgrades, backup and restore;
- hardcode current SaaS prices, quotas, retention, preview status, or export entitlements as stable schema semantics;
- use OpenTelemetry schema transforms as migrations for canonical eval data or depend long term on a Development GenAI field without a pinned adapter;
- accept an imported human/vendor score as a rewrite of historical gold or grader output rather than a new attributed annotation;
- declare vendor exit complete while reports, artifacts, annotations, permissions, deletion, or the release gate still require the old service.

#### Focused pilot

1. Freeze a minimal canonical bundle schema and reference reader before selecting a platform. Include one pass, semantic fail, unsafe action, abstention, grader error, fixture-invalid, cleanup-failed, multi-turn approval/tool run, paired run, and large-artifact case.
2. Implement crash-safe local JSON/JSONL writing, manifest validation, deterministic canonicalization/digests, a local report, and release-gate calculation with all network disabled. Prove the same gate after moving the bundle to a clean directory.
3. Implement the disclosure engine and canary corpus. Default to metadata-only export, then explicitly allow synthetic message/tool content in a separate profile. Prove prohibited values never reach serialized payloads or diagnostics.
4. Implement the OpenTelemetry projector and capture through a pinned local Collector. Decode the OTLP/file output and compare the promised projection with canonical input, including sequence, parents/links, score labels/values, absent/null values, timestamp precision, and artifact digests.
5. Add local MLflow as the first optional platform because it can run without a hosted account. Ingest OTLP, attach eval records through an adapter, reverse-query/export, normalize, and regenerate the local comparison report. Document every native field that has no lossless OpenTelemetry representation.
6. Add one hosted collaboration sink, Braintrust or LangSmith, using a synthetic project and least-privilege credential. Test native OTLP and vendor-native score/dataset projection separately; never assume one path subsumes the other.
7. Exercise payload/attribute/event/span boundaries, child-before-parent and missing-parent cases, 10-minute visibility lag, `429`, `413`, transient/permanent errors, partial success, duplicate replay, queue overflow, process crash, expired retention, pagination, and late score updates. Verify candidate results remain identical with the sink healthy, slow, and unavailable.
8. Measure bytes, calls, spans, storage, evaluator/model/network charges, queue resources, export time, restore time, and operator effort per valid and successful-safe trial. Record the exact plan, region, versions and pricing snapshot rather than extrapolating a universal cost.
9. Run a clean-room exit: export and reconcile the hosted project, restore its useful views locally or to the alternate sink, rotate routing without runner changes, revoke credentials, and test deletion verification.
10. Put repository-only conformance and redaction tests in PR CI; run real local-platform round trips on a scheduled job and hosted/cloud qualification only when credentials, budget and policy allow.

The pilot succeeds only if exporters can be disabled with no change to execution or gating; every release-critical projected field round-trips through the local profile; hosted losses are explicit; no prohibited canary crosses any tested boundary; retries are idempotent; destination outage cannot become candidate failure; reverse exports reconcile to acknowledged records; and a clean environment reproduces the gate and investigation without the hosted dashboard. It does not succeed because traces look attractive, a vendor SDK installs cleanly, or an OTLP endpoint accepts a batch.
