### Research 19: temporal and ecosystem robustness

#### Research method and scope

This research asks how a Kubernetes-agent evaluation remains interpretable while Kubernetes, operators, CRDs, Headlamp, plugins, MCP, provider models, dependencies, and observability systems evolve. It treats compatibility as a measured precondition for scoring, not as a property inferred from a version string. It does not define a universal support window for projects it does not own or claim that a semantically versioned update preserves agent behavior.

This is a targeted narrative review and design synthesis, not a systematic review or quantitative meta-analysis. It asks five prespecified questions:

1. Which exact versions, capabilities, schemas, defaults, artifacts, and support-policy facts are required to identify an evaluation environment reproducibly?
2. Which matched comparisons can distinguish a candidate reasoning regression from environment breakage, a candidate-environment interaction, or changed task semantics?
3. How should release gates sample supported, transition, historical, and unsupported combinations without attempting the full Cartesian product?
4. When can an old case be represented in a new environment without changing the construct it measures, and when must it be frozen or retired?
5. Which preflight and control results make a matrix cell scoreable, diagnostic-only, or invalid?

The source search was refreshed on September 5, 2026. Search families included `Kubernetes supported releases version skew`, `Kubernetes API deprecation removal migration`, `CRD served storage conversion storedVersions`, `operator Kubernetes compatibility upgrade graph`, `Helm chart CRD upgrade`, `Headlamp plugin version compatibility`, `MCP protocol version tool schema listChanged`, `model alias snapshot deprecation retirement`, `OpenTelemetry stability schema migration`, `Prometheus LTS migration PromQL`, `package lock reproducible install`, `factorial interaction design`, `combinatorial configuration testing`, `configuration constraints covering array`, `variability bugs configurable systems`, and `equivalence test smallest effect size`. Searches covered official Kubernetes, Helm, Operator Framework, Headlamp, MCP, provider, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, npm, Node.js, Playwright, and NIST sites plus Crossref and publisher records for peer-reviewed methods and empirical studies. Publication titles, venues, years, article types, and DOIs were verified from Crossref/publisher metadata rather than inferred from search snippets.

Sources were included when they supplied a normative lifecycle or compatibility rule, an inspectable product mechanism, a concrete migration failure mode, an experimental-design method, or direct evidence from the current repository. Secondary version aggregators, unsupported compatibility tables, mutable search summaries, and universal thresholds without an owning policy were excluded. Official support policy and observed compatibility are recorded separately: documentation establishes what an owner intends to support, while a passing preflight and reference control establish only what worked in the tested cell.

Evidence classes have different roles:

| Evidence class                    | Examples                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Appropriate use                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Peer-reviewed methods and studies | Combinatorial software testing [R19-33](https://doi.org/10.1109/MC.2009.253), constrained interaction testing [R19-34](https://doi.org/10.1145/1273463.1273482), real variability bugs [R19-35](https://doi.org/10.1145/3149119), and equivalence tests [R19-36](https://doi.org/10.1177/1948550617697177)                                                                                      | Supports matrix construction, empirical risk hypotheses, and equivalence inference under each study's assumptions; it does not validate this Kubernetes framework |
| Normative lifecycle authorities   | Kubernetes release/skew/deprecation/CRD rules [R19-1](https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/), [R19-2](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/), [R19-4](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definition-versioning/); MCP versioning [R19-11](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning) | Defines supported relationships, negotiation, deprecation, and migration invariants; does not prove a specific deployment conforms                                |
| Product and project documentation | Headlamp [R19-9](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/headlamp/releases), providers [R19-14](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations), [R19-15](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations), [R19-16](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models), observability [R19-20](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/migration/)                         | Supplies version-specific behavior, support windows, migration paths, and known breakages to test; may change after the research snapshot                         |
| Standards and test methodology    | SemVer [R19-23](https://semver.org/), NIST factorial design [R19-26](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pri/section3/pri3331.htm), and NIST combinatorial testing [R19-27](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/automated-combinatorial-testing-for-software)                                                                                                                                   | Structures identities and efficient interaction coverage; does not establish product compatibility or replace task-specific controls                              |
| Direct repository inspection      | Local files cited under implementation implications, at commit `41810531db9ce578d4dc76a9bb7bcf818dbbaf15`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Establishes only what the inspected snapshot contains; cited source files matched `HEAD`, while this research document was untracked                              |

This review did not exhaust every operator, Kubernetes distribution, model host, MCP implementation, browser, telemetry backend, architecture, or provider region. It used Strimzi and Argo CD as representative examples because they publish concrete multi-component or tested-version constraints; their policies must not be generalized to other operators. Provider documentation can change service behavior or retirement dates, and inaccessible retired model weights limit historical reproduction. No reviewed source validates the complete proposed matrix or supplies a universal migration-equivalence test, support horizon, cell count, or retirement threshold. The controls below are therefore falsifiable framework requirements.

Research 8 owns repeatability within an identified environment. Research 9 owns cross-provider and cross-runtime comparisons. Research 10 owns statistical uncertainty. Research 17 owns projections into external observability and eval platforms. Research 18 owns leakage and measurement integrity. Research 19 owns **environment identity, lifecycle eligibility, cross-version semantic comparability, and failure attribution under change**. Topic 20 should separately test concurrent workflow interference, and Topic 21 should separately test whether benchmark changes predict production changes.

The primary hypothesis is: **an undocumented or unresolved ecosystem change can be separated from a candidate reasoning regression by an immutable environment manifest, a compatibility preflight, reference/grader controls, and a matched old/new candidate by old/new environment comparison**. The cheapest falsification is to run setup, discovery, a known-good reference, a known-bad control, graders, verifier, and cleanup before assigning candidate quality. If the reference path fails, capabilities differ without an approved equivalence mapping, or the task/oracle changes, the cell is not evidence of a reasoning regression.

#### Counterevidence and validity threats

Version change is not itself evidence of breakage. Kubernetes requires round-trip compatibility within a served release and protects GA APIs from removal within a major version [R19-2](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/); OpenTelemetry and Prometheus publish substantial stable-surface guarantees [R19-18](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/versioning-and-stability/), [R19-32](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/stability/); and an unchanged immutable artifact can remain compatible across several supported environments. The matrix should therefore test specific boundary hypotheses, not assign prior blame to every dependency update or reward a permanently frozen stack.

The low-order interaction evidence is useful but bounded. A peer-reviewed IEEE Computer article motivates combinatorial coverage from observed software-failure interactions [R19-33](https://doi.org/10.1109/MC.2009.253), and constrained interaction research shows that valid configurations require constraint-aware generation [R19-34](https://doi.org/10.1145/1273463.1273482). A qualitative study of 98 real variability bugs across Linux, Apache, BusyBox, and Marlin shows that configuration-dependent bugs are diverse and difficult to understand [R19-35](https://doi.org/10.1145/3149119). None estimates the interaction-order distribution, effect size, or covering strength for Kubernetes AI agents. Pairwise coverage is a starting hypothesis, not a completeness claim.

The matched design has five important threats:

- **period and provider drift:** remote model aliases, quotas, safety systems, regional routing, and service load can change between cells even when the request manifest does not;
- **bundled changes:** an “environment upgrade” that simultaneously changes Kubernetes, operator, CRD, MCP server, Headlamp, browser, and telemetry cannot identify which component caused an effect;
- **invalid cross cells:** old candidates may be impossible to install in new environments, making candidate, environment, and interaction contrasts non-identifiable rather than zero;
- **non-independent cases:** transformed scenarios and repeated trials share family, fixture, model, and infrastructure effects, so treating rows as independent understates uncertainty;
- **selective escalation and survivorship:** expanding only surprising matrices biases attribution, while retired models and unavailable artifacts leave historical successes easier to preserve than historical failures to reproduce.

Mitigate these threats with prespecified escalation rules; one changed factor or an explicitly named indivisible bundle; randomized, time-blocked interleaving; stable negative-control scenarios; family-clustered uncertainty from Topic 10; complete invalid/unavailable-cell reporting; and sensitivity analyses that exclude unresolved moving aliases. Declare a bundle indivisible only when each omitted intermediate violates a captured owner support rule, cannot resolve required artifacts, or changes the task construct; retain that evidence in the manifest. If any valid intermediate exists, run a local disaggregation matrix before naming a component. If a provider cannot identify a stable snapshot and the four cells cannot be interleaved within an acceptable time block, report an observational epoch contrast, not a candidate-environment interaction.

#### Compatibility is not one boolean

Record four different claims for every matrix cell:

| Claim                   | Meaning                                                                                                                                                          | Authority                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy-supported        | Every owner whose policy applies lists the combination as supported, including component skew, platform, region, deployment type, runtime, and feature maturity  | Versioned owner policy captured at matrix-design time                            |
| Installation-compatible | Artifacts resolve, install, start, negotiate, discover required APIs/tools, and clean up under the exact manifest                                                | Automated setup and preflight evidence                                           |
| Task-compatible         | Candidate-visible facts, permitted actions, task intent, gold facts, safety constraints, and verifier semantics remain equivalent enough for the stated contrast | Versioned migration review plus round-trip, reference-agent, and oracle controls |
| Observed-compatible     | Repeated reference and known-bad controls behave as expected in this exact cell                                                                                  | Canonical control results; passing does not expand the vendor's support policy   |

Use states `supported-observed`, `supported-unverified`, `transition-canary`, `historical-frozen`, `unsupported-diagnostic`, and `invalid`. A cell cannot be promoted to `supported-observed` merely because installation succeeded. Conversely, an empirically passing but owner-unsupported cell remains `unsupported-diagnostic` and cannot block a supported release unless governance explicitly adopts it.

Compatibility has layers and owners:

1. **Artifact resolution:** exact source, package, image, chart, browser, model, and server artifacts still exist and their digests match.
2. **Static contract:** package peer ranges, Kubernetes discovery/OpenAPI, CRD schemas, MCP protocol/capabilities/tool schemas, provider request fields, telemetry schemas, and grader inputs are accepted.
3. **Lifecycle:** components start, authenticate, negotiate, reconcile, reach readiness, retain required data, and clean up in the prescribed order.
4. **Task semantics:** evidence availability, defaults, mutation effects, safety constraints, and accepted outcomes still measure the same capability.
5. **Measurement:** reference, known-bad, grader, verifier, and artifact controls still discriminate correctly.

Preserve the first failing layer. A failed tool call caused by a removed schema is not a reasoning error, while an agent that ignores a discoverable replacement API after compatibility has been established can be.

#### Immutable environment manifest

Close a versioned `environment_manifest` before candidate execution and bind its digest to every trajectory and result. Record requested configuration and runtime observation separately; a lockfile, chart version, model alias, or image tag is an input, not proof of what served.

| Domain                       | Required experiment identity                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Runner and host              | Runner source and build digest; operating system/image digest; architecture; kernel/container runtime; CPU/memory profile; locale/time zone/clock policy; Node/npm/Playwright versions; installed browser name, binary revision and digest; randomization block and declared seeds                                                                                                                                           |
| Candidate                    | Candidate source/artifact digest; Headlamp and AI Assistant plugin versions/build digests; production/developer feature flags; prompt, system policy, skill, tool adapter, grader and verifier versions; enabled capability profile                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Kubernetes                   | Distribution and image digests; server Git version/commit/platform; API server, controller, scheduler, kubelet, proxy and `kubectl` versions; HA skew; feature gates; admission plugins/webhooks; discovery and preferred resources; OpenAPI digest; runtime configuration; storage class/CNI/CSI; architecture                                                                                                              |
| Operators and extensions     | Installation method; operator, operand, chart, bundle/CSV/channel, controller and webhook image digests; supported Kubernetes declaration; feature gates; watched scope; owned/required APIs; upgrade-graph edge; reconciliation status/version; rendered manifests and values digest                                                                                                                                        |
| CRDs and custom resources    | CRD UID/generation/digest; served/deprecated/storage versions; `status.storedVersions`; per-version structural schemas, defaults, pruning and CEL rules; conversion strategy, review versions and webhook image/digest; SSA topology markers; custom-resource requested/served/storage representations and semantic round-trip result                                                                                        |
| MCP                          | Client/adapter/SDK and server artifact digests; transport; requested and negotiated protocol version; client/server implementation identity; capabilities; complete paginated tool/resource/prompt discovery; tool names, descriptions, annotations, input/output schemas and canonical digests; `listChanged` support/events; structured-result validation; confirmation policy                                             |
| Provider and model           | Provider, host, endpoint/deployment/region, API version, account availability class and request ID; requested alias/model, resolved or returned model identifier/version; lifecycle status and retirement date at run time; parameters including temperature/top-p/effort/reasoning/tool mode; supported context/output/tool/structured-output capabilities; tokenizer where observable; provider-side prompt/cache controls |
| Dependencies and artifacts   | Every `package.json` and lockfile digest; npm configuration and install command; resolved package inventory including source/integrity; mutable local/file/git dependencies; plugin package and shared-module versions; chart archive/rendered manifest/image digests; signature/provenance status                                                                                                                           |
| Observability and evaluation | Instrumentation, OpenTelemetry API/SDK/semantic-convention/schema URL, Collector distribution/component and backend versions; exporter/receiver/processor config digests; metric/span/log names and schema; Prometheus/Alertmanager/storage/query versions; recording rules/dashboards/query digests; retention, sampling, aggregation, clock and data-completeness policy; hosted-eval adapter/version/export receipt       |

Canonicalize structured schemas before hashing: resolve stable key ordering and representation-only differences while retaining descriptions, required fields, enum values, defaults, formats, annotations, and output contracts. Keep the original bytes as artifacts. A digest equality check proves byte or canonical-form identity only; semantic compatibility requires probes.

Reject a scoreable run when a required identity is mutable and unresolved, including `latest`, a moving branch, an unpinned container tag, an unrecorded regional deployment, an MCP tool name without schema, or a model alias without provider response/version evidence. When the service exposes no immutable model snapshot, label the run `provider-observed-at=<timestamp>` and do not promise future exact reproduction.

#### Matched attribution matrix

For a suspected regression, freeze one candidate baseline $C_0$, one candidate change $C_1$, one environment baseline $E_0$, and one environment change $E_1$. Run the complete matched matrix:

| Cell     | Candidate | Environment | Primary question                                                                 |
| -------- | --------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| $Y_{00}$ | $C_0$     | $E_0$       | Does the previously accepted system still reproduce its baseline?                |
| $Y_{01}$ | $C_0$     | $E_1$       | Does the environment change break or alter the old candidate?                    |
| $Y_{10}$ | $C_1$     | $E_0$       | Does the candidate change regress in the old environment?                        |
| $Y_{11}$ | $C_1$     | $E_1$       | Does the release candidate work in its intended environment, including coupling? |

For a metric whose direction is consistently “higher is better,” define descriptive contrasts:

$$
\Delta_C = Y_{10} - Y_{00}, \qquad
\Delta_E = Y_{01} - Y_{00}, \qquad
\Delta_{CE} = (Y_{11} - Y_{10}) - (Y_{01} - Y_{00}).
$$

$\Delta_C$ estimates the candidate change at the baseline environment, $\Delta_E$ estimates the environment change for the baseline candidate, and $\Delta_{CE}$ exposes interaction. NIST's two-level factorial design describes how full factorial cells permit separate main-effect and interaction estimates under a controlled design [R19-26](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pri/section3/pri3331.htm). These contrasts are not automatically causal: only claim attribution when the two candidate artifacts and two environment manifests differ solely in prespecified factors, cells are otherwise blocked/matched, task semantics remain invariant, and missing/invalid cells are not imputed. If $E_1-E_0$ is an indivisible upgrade bundle, $\Delta_E$ belongs to that bundle; it cannot be reassigned post hoc to one component.

Define a cell-eligibility indicator $A_{ce}$ from the preflight and controls before observing candidate quality:

$$
A_{ce}=1 \iff \text{policy, artifact, discovery, setup, contract, reference, grader, verifier, and cleanup controls pass}.
$$

$Y_{ce}$ is estimable only where $A_{ce}=1$. Report $A_{ce}=0$ with the first failing layer and owner; never encode it as a zero score. Candidate, environment, and interaction contrasts require all four eligible cells. A partial matrix can answer narrower operational questions, such as whether $C_1$ works in $E_1$, but cannot identify the missing factorial effect. The result-schema validator must reject a candidate, environment, or interaction attribution unless the claim references four eligible cell IDs, their control results, and a prespecified contrast; process review is not the enforcement mechanism.

Each $Y_{ce}$ is a distribution over repeated trials, not one pass/fail. Form contrasts within matched scenario-family and time blocks before aggregating; for binary outcomes, report paired risk differences or an appropriate hierarchical model rather than treating retries as independent Bernoulli trials. Use Topic 10's interval and practical-effect policy; randomize cell order within short blocks or use a balanced order such as $00,11,01,10$ followed by its reverse; hold scenario instance, capability profile, provider parameters, and measurement policy fixed; and use the same provider-supported seed only as one manifest field, never as a determinism claim. Include a scenario whose task-relevant surface should be unaffected by $E_1$ as a negative control. Report cell eligibility, period, control outcomes, exclusions, and family grouping before quality contrasts.

Classify common patterns conservatively:

| Valid-cell pattern                                                                                  | Attribution                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| $Y_{00}$ and $Y_{10}$ reproduce; $Y_{01}$ and $Y_{11}$ degrade; reference/control path also changes | Environment or measurement regression, not candidate reasoning                                   |
| $Y_{00}$ reproduces; $Y_{10}$ degrades in $E_0$; $C_0$ remains stable in both environments          | Candidate regression supported                                                                   |
| Marginal candidate and environment contrasts are small but $Y_{11}$ degrades                        | Candidate-environment interaction; both owners investigate                                       |
| Setup/discovery/reference/grader/verifier fails in any cell                                         | Cell invalid or compatibility failure; no reasoning score                                        |
| Required evidence/tool disappears or gold outcome changes                                           | Task semantics changed; migrate and requalify rather than compare scores                         |
| Only unsupported cells fail                                                                         | Unsupported diagnostic; no supported-release regression                                          |
| Mutable provider alias changes between cells or cannot be resolved                                  | Confounded provider drift; repeat with a resolvable snapshot or start a new observational series |

Do not average categories into “the model got worse.” Preserve hard outcome, semantic score, safety, latency/cost, invalidity owner, environment contrast, and interaction separately.

#### Staged compatibility preflight and attribution tree

Run these stages in order and stop scoring at the first invalidating failure:

1. **Policy gate:** confirm the matrix cell is in the declared lane and all owning support policies are captured. Unsupported combinations are tagged before execution.
2. **Artifact gate:** resolve and verify all digests, lockfiles, signatures, images, charts, model/deployment availability, browser binaries, and source revisions.
3. **Static discovery gate:** collect Kubernetes versions/discovery/OpenAPI/CRDs, operator APIs/status, MCP negotiation/capabilities/full paginated tool list and schemas, provider model capabilities, and telemetry schema/query contracts.
4. **Setup gate:** create the fixture, wait for explicit readiness and observed generation, and prove the intended fault and candidate-visible evidence through an independent identity.
5. **Contract probes:** validate one permitted and one denied operation per capability, CRD cross-version round trips where used, representative MCP calls and output-schema validation, telemetry ingestion/query fixtures, and cleanup feasibility.
6. **Measurement controls:** run reference, no-agent/known-bad, grader, verifier, and artifact controls under the exact candidate-visible interface.
7. **Candidate trials:** score only if the prior stages pass; retain all attempts and runtime rediscovery events.
8. **Postflight:** independently verify state, API deprecation warnings, schema/capability drift, residue, telemetry completeness, cleanup, and manifest closure.

Cache qualification only by a digest over the policy snapshot, complete resolved environment manifest, candidate-visible contract, scenario version, and control bundle. Any changed digest, support/deprecation event, runtime rediscovery, provider-resolved model change, or integrity incident expires the qualification immediately. Mutable external services also require a prespecified periodic control cadence; this research does not supply a universal time-to-live.

Use the following ownership decision tree:

- If artifacts cannot be resolved or policy rejects the combination, record `unsupported_or_unavailable`.
- Else if setup/readiness/discovery fails before candidate execution, record `environment_compatibility_failure` with the failing component owner.
- Else if a required tool/API exists but negotiation, schema, or representative invocation fails, record `protocol_or_contract_failure`.
- Else if the reference agent fails, record `task_interface_or_reference_failure`; inspect changed evidence, permissions, defaults, and accepted actions.
- Else if known-bad passes or verifier/grader disagrees with authoritative state, record `measurement_failure`.
- Else if $C_0$ fails only on $E_1$, investigate environment change before evaluating $C_1$.
- Else if $C_1$ fails on both valid environments while $C_0$ passes, candidate regression is supported.
- Else if failure appears only in $C_1,E_1$, record an interaction, not unilateral blame.
- Else if the migrated scenario cannot preserve task intent, observable facts, permitted action, safety rule, and oracle, start a new case version and do not compute a cross-version quality delta.

#### Kubernetes release, API, and feature matrix

Kubernetes maintains the latest three minor release branches and provides roughly one year of patch support for 1.19 and later [R19-1](https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/). That policy does not make every component combination valid. Current policy allows `kubectl` within one minor of the API server, kubelets and kube-proxy up to three minors older under constraints, HA API servers within one minor, and control-plane components with narrower rules. Upgrade order and admission-webhook ability to handle new versions/fields further constrain transition cells.

Build Kubernetes lanes from the owning policy at matrix-freeze time:

| Lane                      | Minimum cells                                                                                                                                                             | Gate role                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Maintained release        | Oldest, middle, and newest maintained minor at latest qualified patch; current production distribution/image; supported client skew boundaries                            | Blocking support lane                                          |
| Upgrade transition        | Old/current and current/next control-plane states that the distribution supports; valid HA/client skew; webhooks and operators at prescribed before/during/after versions | Canary until owner policy and observed controls pass           |
| API-removal canary        | Current scenario with deprecated APIs disabled using `--runtime-config`; deprecation warning/audit/metric checks                                                          | Detects upcoming compatibility breakage before removal         |
| Feature-maturity boundary | Required alpha/beta/default-on/GA feature gate combinations, including media type, validation, SSA, or admission behavior used by the scenario                            | Blocking only for explicitly supported capability profiles     |
| Historical                | Pinned retired Kubernetes image/toolchain when artifacts and isolation remain reproducible                                                                                | Frozen trend context; never blocks current releases by default |
| Unsupported               | Deliberate out-of-skew or EOL combinations with a known expected failure                                                                                                  | Diagnostic positive control for the compatibility classifier   |

GA APIs are not removed within a Kubernetes major version, beta APIs have minimum deprecation/removal windows, and alpha APIs may disappear without notice [R19-2](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-policy/). These are API-lifecycle guarantees, not semantic equality across versions. The migration guide documents changed defaults and representations, including an empty `PodDisruptionBudget` selector changing from selecting no pods in `policy/v1beta1` to all pods in `policy/v1` [R19-3](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/). Therefore, migration qualification must compare defaulted live objects, allowed operations, and verifier semantics, not only whether persisted objects remain readable.

Capture Warning headers, `k8s.io/deprecated` audit annotations, `apiserver_requested_deprecated_apis`, field-validation warnings/errors, and discovery changes as compatibility evidence. Treat `kubectl` client-side/server-side validation, apply mode/field manager, content type, and requested consistency semantics as manifest factors when scenarios depend on them. Server-Side Apply schema-topology changes can alter ownership and conflict behavior even without an API version increment [R19-5](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/server-side-apply/).

#### Operator, chart, and CRD matrix

An operator scenario is identified by a tuple, not an operator version:

`(Kubernetes, install method, chart/bundle/channel, operator image, operand version, CRD set, served/storage versions, conversion webhook, feature gates, values, upgrade path)`.

Apply these rules:

- use the operator's published Kubernetes/operand support table when one exists; Argo CD, for example, distinguishes supported-release policy from a concrete tested Kubernetes-version table [R19-8](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/installation/);
- represent upgrade edges, not only endpoints; OLM `replaces`, `skips`, `skipRange`, channel, approval mode, and catalog contents determine which paths are installable [R19-7](https://olm.operatorframework.io/docs/concepts/olm-architecture/operator-catalog/creating-an-update-graph/);
- capture chart `version`, informational `appVersion`, optional `kubeVersion`, rendered values/manifests, dependencies and archive digest separately; Helm explicitly states that `appVersion` does not drive chart version calculations [R19-6](https://helm.sh/docs/topics/charts/);
- never assume `helm upgrade` updates CRDs: CRDs in Helm's `crds/` directory are not upgraded or deleted automatically [R19-6](https://helm.sh/docs/topics/charts/);
- wait for operator status, `observedGeneration`, webhook readiness, and reported operand/operator versions, not only healthy pods;
- include one clean install, every supported direct upgrade edge used in production, and one known-invalid skipped or unsupported path for classifier qualification.

For each CRD, test create/read/update/watch through every served version used by the scenario, storage migration, and semantic round trip. Exactly one version is storage; changing it does not rewrite existing objects; old storage versions remain in `status.storedVersions` until migration; and removing an old version requires client and stored-object migration [R19-4](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definition-versioning/). `strategy: None` merely changes `apiVersion` and may prune fields, so it is invalid evidence of equivalence when schemas differ. Conversion failure can disrupt reads, writes, updates, and deletes.

Normalize round-trip checks by removing documented nondeterministic/server metadata, then require preservation of task-relevant information and behavior:

$$
N\left(C_{b\rightarrow a}(C_{a\rightarrow b}(x))\right) = N(x)
$$

for every accepted source object $x$, plus equivalent defaulted values, validation, SSA merge topology, status interpretation, and controller outcome. Equality of JSON is neither necessary nor sufficient when the new API intentionally changes representation; the migration record must name the semantic mapping and expert-approved tolerances.

Representative Strimzi documentation demonstrates why endpoint-only matrices are inadequate: a release can constrain Kubernetes and Kafka versions, require KRaft/API conversion and ordered upgrade steps, expose observed operator/Kafka/metadata versions in status, and require manual CRD updates for Helm upgrades [R19-28](https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/latest/deploying). Use this as an operator-specific test pattern, not a general policy for every controller.

#### Headlamp, plugin, and dependency matrix

Headlamp core, Helm chart, plugin-development tool, plugin package, shared frontend modules, browser, and AI Assistant artifact have independent versions. Headlamp releases add and alter plugin APIs and user-visible Kubernetes behavior, while the plugin tool is separately released [R19-9](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/headlamp/releases). Headlamp's plugin documentation also says shared modules are supplied by Headlamp and plugin-installed copies must match because the build excludes them in favor of `pluginLib` [R19-10](https://headlamp.dev/docs/latest/development/plugins/functionality/).

Define three Headlamp lanes:

1. oldest Headlamp/plugin-tool combination explicitly supported by the AI Assistant release;
2. current production combination with the exact plugin artifact and shared-module inventory;
3. next Headlamp release candidate or latest release as a non-blocking transition canary until qualified.

For each lane, probe plugin load, registry calls, route/sidebar/chat rendering, settings persistence/migration, Kubernetes API discovery, auth/token path, required browser behavior, production feature flags, and complete agent/tool flow. A compile success against `@kinvolk/headlamp-plugin` does not prove runtime compatibility with the Headlamp `pluginLib` loaded in the browser.

SemVer promises compatibility only relative to a declared public API; major zero permits anything to change, and prereleases may not satisfy the intended normal-version compatibility [R19-23](https://semver.org/). Package ranges therefore define candidate resolutions, not experiment identity. `package-lock.json` records the exact dependency tree, source and integrity needed for repeatable installation [R19-24](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-lock-json), while `npm ci` rejects manifest/lock disagreement and performs a frozen clean install [R19-25](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-ci). Preserve npm configuration because peer-dependency, link, script, platform and install-strategy settings can still change the installed/runtime result.

Record Playwright package and browser revisions together. Playwright release notes show bundled browser changes, operating-system support removals, and behavior/API changes across releases [R19-29](https://playwright.dev/docs/release-notes). A screenshot or navigation regression must first be reproduced against the same browser binary before it is attributed to Headlamp or the agent.

#### MCP protocol and tool-contract matrix

MCP protocol versions are date strings identifying the last backward-incompatible change. The current version observed in this review is `2026-07-28`; compatible edits can occur without changing that identifier, revisions can be draft/current/final, and the current revision negotiates per request while retaining a compatibility path for initialization-based revisions [R19-11](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning). The inspected `2025-06-18` revision instead performs protocol and capability negotiation during initialization and requires the parties to respect the negotiated result [R19-12](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/lifecycle).

Test MCP as a negotiated contract:

| Factor             | Required cells/probes                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Protocol           | Oldest supported handshake revision, current supported revision, and one unsupported-version error with advertised alternatives                               |
| Transport          | Every supported stdio/HTTP transport and auth profile; timeout/cancellation; reconnect and server restart                                                     |
| Capabilities       | Required capability present/absent; experimental capability isolated; only negotiated features used                                                           |
| Discovery          | Full pagination; empty/multi-page lists; `listChanged` notification followed by rediscovery; stale persisted schema after restart                             |
| Tool contract      | Name, title, description, annotations, input schema, output schema and canonical digest changes tested independently                                          |
| Results and errors | Structured and unstructured results, output-schema validation, protocol error versus `isError`, resource links, cancellation, timeout and malformed responses |
| Safety mediation   | Confirmation/approval and trusted-server annotations preserved across adapter versions; annotations treated as untrusted for unknown servers                  |

Tool names are not stable identities. The tools specification permits input and output schemas, annotations, paginated discovery, structured/unstructured content, and change notifications [R19-13](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools). Persist `(server identity, negotiated protocol, capability set, canonical tool contract digest)` with each call. If a server sends `listChanged`, close the prior contract epoch; do not merge calls made before and after rediscovery into one supposedly fixed trial.

Classify a candidate's use of a newly valid optional field as reasoning only after the client/adapter faithfully exposed it. A tool-schema diff that renames, requires, removes, retypes, redescribes, or changes the output of a task-relevant field requires an adapter qualification and potentially a scenario migration. Representation-only canonical equality can remain in the same case version.

#### Provider and model snapshot matrix

A model name is not necessarily a snapshot. Record provider, host, endpoint/deployment, region, API version, requested ID, returned/resolved ID where exposed, lifecycle state, parameters, capabilities, and request timestamp. Treat provider migration and model migration as separate factors because the same family can have different identifiers, schedules, regions, quotas, schemas, and behavior on first-party, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex, or other hosts.

Provider policies demonstrate several incompatible lifecycle models:

- OpenAI publishes model-specific shutdowns and minimum notice classes, with shorter possible notice for previews; aliases and snapshots can retire together or point to replacements [R19-14](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations).
- Anthropic distinguishes active, legacy, deprecated, and retired models, commits to notice for public models, and explicitly notes that partner-operated platforms set their own schedules [R19-15](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations). Current Claude documentation states which IDs are pinned snapshots and distinguishes older convenience aliases from newer dateless pinned IDs [R19-30](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview).
- Gemini distinguishes stable, preview, latest, and experimental names; `latest` is hot-swapped, while preview and experimental endpoints have weaker stability/availability expectations [R19-16](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models).
- Azure Foundry availability varies by region/deployment type; preview deployments can be force-upgraded; standard and provisioned deployments have different upgrade behavior; lifecycle fields are queryable programmatically [R19-17](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/concepts/model-retirements).

Use these lanes:

| Lane                 | Identity rule                                                                                                    | Release use                                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pinned current       | Provider-defined immutable/pinned model plus exact host/API/region and explicit parameters                       | Blocking, if available and supported                                                         |
| Moving observational | Alias or deployment whose backing snapshot cannot be proven; record returned identity/capabilities and timestamp | Trend monitoring only; a movement starts a new epoch                                         |
| Replacement canary   | Announced replacement evaluated side by side before retirement                                                   | Non-blocking until prompts/tools/graders and quality/cost/safety are requalified             |
| Preview/experimental | Explicit short-window capability profile                                                                         | Never silently substitutes for a GA blocking lane                                            |
| Retired historical   | Original service inaccessible but canonical outputs/environment manifest retained                                | Regrade-only history; do not fabricate reruns on the replacement and call them the old model |

Before comparing model quality, probe required input/output limits, tool calling, parallel calls, structured output, streaming, reasoning/effort controls, parameter acceptance, safety/refusal behavior needed by the scenario, and actual response model identifier. If a provider removes a parameter or changes an API enum while the old model remains named the same, classify the initial failure as contract drift. Requalify prompts and graders on the replacement, but preserve the old results and selection history.

#### Observability-stack matrix

Observability is both evidence presented to the candidate and instrumentation of the eval. Version both roles. A query that returns different samples, labels, retention, ordering, or partial data can change task difficulty even when the underlying workload is identical.

OpenTelemetry provides strong compatibility goals for stable APIs/SDKs, but Development signals may break or disappear, API/SDK/Semantic Conventions/Contrib have independent versions, and semantic-convention guarantees cover only specified fields [R19-18](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/versioning-and-stability/). Telemetry schemas identify versions and limited transformations, but intentionally do not describe the complete telemetry shape or every possible migration [R19-19](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/schemas/). They cannot migrate Headlamp's canonical evaluation truth.

The Collector combines components at different maturity levels and permits some minor-version changes in strings, OS/protocol support, dependencies, and experimental modules [R19-21](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/VERSIONING.md). GenAI conventions have moved to a separate repository whose schema URL was still marked TODO and which had no published releases at the reviewed snapshot [R19-22](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai). Treat those conventions as a versioned optional projection, not a stable gate contract.

Prometheus publishes LTS windows but ordinarily begins a new minor cycle every six weeks and non-LTS minors generally stop receiving fixes after that cycle [R19-31](https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/release-cycle/). Prometheus promises selected API stability within a major version while excluding experimental features, remote read, service discovery integrations, internal metrics, exact disk format, and logs [R19-32](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/stability/). Its 3.0 migration changed scrape strictness, query boundary semantics, labels, configuration, logs, and downgrade limits [R19-20](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/migration/). Therefore, “same PromQL text” does not prove equivalent evidence.

For each observability cell, replay a golden telemetry fixture and verify ingestion count, timestamps, resource/scope identity, schema URLs, sampling/drop decisions, metric type/unit/bounds, label normalization, query output, alert/recording rule output, retention boundary, dashboard/API adapter, and export receipt. Store raw canonical evidence before backend transformation. A backend query failure invalidates observability-dependent scoring but need not invalidate independent Kubernetes hard-state checks.

#### Matrix selection without combinatorial explosion

Do not execute every product of all versions. Use four complementary selections:

1. **Policy anchors:** oldest/current/newest supported values and exact production baselines.
2. **Transition edges:** every upgrade, deprecation, storage, protocol, model replacement, or schema edge the release actually crosses.
3. **Risk pairs and triples:** pairwise or higher-strength covering arrays over non-transition factors, respecting impossible/unsupported constraints. NIST reports that many software failures arise from low-order parameter interactions and provides combinatorial methods to reduce test-set size [R19-27](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/automated-combinatorial-testing-for-software); the peer-reviewed synthesis and constraint-aware study support the method while limiting the claim to their studied systems [R19-33](https://doi.org/10.1109/MC.2009.253), [R19-34](https://doi.org/10.1145/1273463.1273482).
4. **Matched escalation:** when a canary changes, run the full local $2 \times 2$ candidate/environment matrix and then add the smallest third factor that can discriminate the owner, such as CRD versus operator, MCP server versus adapter, model versus provider API, or instrumentation versus backend.

Covering arrays are for fault discovery and breadth; they do not substitute for the matched factorial cells needed to estimate a named interaction. Weight factors by support-boundary proximity, change magnitude, task dependence, usage share, security impact, irreversibility, prior failures, and observability. Keep at least one known-invalid constrained combination to prove that unsupported cells are rejected rather than silently coerced.

Generate the matrix from machine-readable policy records where available, but require review for semantic constraints such as upgrade order, region, webhook compatibility, CRD storage history, and model availability. Record all excluded combinations and reasons. A green matrix that silently omitted its hardest supported boundary is not complete.

#### Support-window release gates

Define gates by lane rather than “latest”:

| Lane                      | Entry rule                                                                                                                             | Gate behavior                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Current supported         | Owner-supported combination, immutable manifest, all preflight/reference/measurement controls pass                                     | Blocks release on practical candidate regression, compatibility regression, or unresolved interaction                |
| Transition/next           | Announced next Kubernetes/operator/Headlamp/MCP/model/telemetry version or deprecation edge; artifacts available                       | Canary warning first; becomes blocking only after support adoption, migration qualification, and stable baseline     |
| Historical frozen         | Formerly supported, reproducible or at least canonically archived, and retained for a named historical question                        | Does not block current release; prevents rewriting history and detects analysis-pipeline drift where regrading works |
| Unsupported diagnostic    | Outside one or more owner policies, deliberately malformed, or impossible in production                                                | Must classify correctly; no quality threshold and no denominator inflation                                           |
| Emergency security escape | Owning project/provider retires or disables a component early for security/compliance; replacement cannot preserve an ordinary overlap | Freeze affected series, open migration incident, qualify replacement, and document the discontinuity                 |

At release freeze, snapshot each owner's policy and calculate the required current cells. A later documentation edit must not retroactively change the denominator or verdict. Review policy at a fixed cadence and on release/deprecation events. Give each cell an owner, qualification expiry condition, and next action. Do not let an EOL cell block indefinitely, and do not remove an inconvenient supported cell without an append-only governance decision.

A current lane fails compatibility when any required supported cell cannot install/negotiate, reference controls fail, or the product no longer performs the task through its declared capability profile. It fails candidate quality only after compatibility is valid and Topic 10's practical/statistical gate is crossed. A transition warning becomes urgent when retirement occurs before the next planned release, a deprecated API is still observed, or no qualified replacement cell exists.

#### Scenario migration, freeze, and retirement

Never edit historical scenario/result artifacts in place. A scenario has immutable versions, lineage, representation mappings, and lifecycle events.

**Migrate** a case when the measured task remains the same but a supported representation, API, tool contract, or environment must change. Require:

- unchanged user intent, root-cause mechanism, required facts, safety constraints, and success/failure semantics;
- an explicit old-to-new field/evidence/action mapping and known losses;
- setup and cleanup success in both environments;
- CRD/API/tool conversion and semantic round-trip checks where applicable;
- reference agent pass and known-bad fail in both versions;
- expert review, blinded to candidate identity and desired release outcome where practical, that candidate-visible evidence does not become easier/harder in an unmodeled way;
- primary bridge estimands and symmetric or asymmetric equivalence bounds fixed before examining bridge results;
- a bridge run using the matched matrix. Hard semantic and safety invariants must pass exactly. Classify `equivalent` only when every required confidence interval lies wholly inside its prespecified equivalence bounds, `materially-different` when any required interval lies wholly beyond a bound, and `inconclusive` otherwise; a prespecified Bayesian rule may replace these interval rules. A non-significant difference is not evidence of equivalence; equivalence tests require bounds tied to the smallest practically important effect [R19-36](https://doi.org/10.1177/1948550617697177). Only `equivalent` joins a measurement series. The other states create a linked new series without rewriting old scores; `inconclusive` must not be described as evidence of difference.

**Freeze** a case when it is no longer in the current support gate but its historical result remains useful and the original artifacts, policy, and limitations can be preserved. Freeze when the environment is EOL, a provider model is no longer callable, an old storage/CRD state is unsafe to recreate, or exact reproduction is too costly, while the record still documents a meaningful former capability. Permit regrading only against retained canonical trajectories when the new grader's input contract is satisfied; label it reanalysis, not rerun.

**Retire** a case from active claims when any of the following holds:

- the task or gold is invalid under every supported environment;
- required evidence or action no longer exists and no construct-preserving migration is possible;
- a schema/default/behavior change makes the old and new tasks semantically different;
- safe isolation or legal artifact access cannot be maintained;
- fixtures or provider services are irrecoverably unavailable and retained evidence is insufficient;
- the case is redundant with stronger lineage coverage, chronically nondiscriminating, contaminated, or has unresolved expert disagreement;
- maintenance cost is disproportionate to a documented, low-risk coverage contribution.

Retirement removes the case only from future active denominators. Preserve its ID, versions, results, reason, decision owner/reviewer, replacement lineage, final supported environment, and last valid gate. Publish old aggregate recomputations only as new report versions with both original and current definitions.

Use status transitions:

`draft -> qualifying -> active -> migration-required -> active-new-version | frozen -> retired`.

Allow `quarantined` from any state for integrity or correctness incidents. Restoring a quarantined case requires a new immutable version and qualification; it does not erase the incident.

#### Known-invalid designs and interpretations

Reject designs or results that:

- record only Kubernetes minor, operator version, model name, or MCP tool name as experiment identity;
- call a package range, chart `appVersion`, container tag, `latest` alias, provider deployment name, or documentation sentence a resolved runtime;
- assume SemVer compatibility for major-zero, prerelease, behavior, transitive dependency, provider, schema, or model changes;
- infer support because a cell passed, or infer breakage because an owner never claimed support;
- compare candidate scores when setup, discovery, reference, grader, verifier, telemetry completeness, or cleanup failed;
- label a model reasoning regression from only $C_1,E_1$ without reproducing $C_0,E_0$ and testing the cross cells;
- treat a missing old/new cross cell as zero, carry-forward, or evidence of no interaction;
- compare scores after task evidence, permitted actions, defaults, safety policy, or gold semantics changed without migration qualification;
- use endpoint-only operator tests while ignoring upgrade path, channel, chart, operand, CRD storage history, webhook, and feature gates;
- assume changing CRD storage version migrates existing objects, that `strategy: None` converts differing schemas, or that readable old objects imply semantic equivalence;
- rely on Helm to upgrade/delete CRDs or use `appVersion` as the chart artifact identity;
- ignore Kubernetes component skew, admission webhooks, feature gates, client validation/apply mode, or deprecated-API warnings;
- cache an MCP tool schema across server/protocol/capability changes or ignore pagination and `listChanged`;
- treat provider aliases as immutable snapshots, merge runs from forced/rolling upgrades, or substitute a replacement model into historical rows;
- mix first-party and partner-hosted model lifecycle schedules or cloud regions/deployment types without explicit factors;
- use OpenTelemetry schema conversion, a hosted trace, or identical PromQL text as proof that candidate evidence was equivalent;
- let unsupported or historical failures block current releases by accident, or drop supported boundary cells to keep a gate green;
- rewrite a scenario or historical aggregate in place after migration or retirement;
- select covering-array cells and then report unidentifiable main effects/interactions as causal;
- name one component as the cause after changing an environment bundle without a rollback or local disaggregation matrix;
- run candidate/environment cells sequentially against a mutable provider without time blocks, balance, anchors, or a reported period effect;
- approve migration because a bridge difference is not statistically significant, choose equivalence bounds after seeing results, or use bounds wider than the release's minimum practical effect;
- expand the matrix indefinitely without risk ranking, ownership, expiry, or a decision each cell can affect.

#### Local implementation implications

The current repository already exposes several useful identities but does not close a compatibility manifest:

- [e2e/README.md](../e2e/README.md) says the E2E suite uses Headlamp `v0.43.0` and KWOK `v0.8.0`, but documentation is not enforcement.
- [run-ai-assistant-e2e.ts](../e2e/run-ai-assistant-e2e.ts) checks only that `docker`, `kwokctl`, `kubectl`, and `npm` exist. It does not compare actual versions, explicitly select the Kubernetes version passed to `kwokctl create cluster`, record server discovery/OpenAPI/CRD digests, or emit a canonical environment manifest.
- The runner builds the current working tree, installs the Chromium revision associated with the resolved Playwright package, builds a local Headlamp image tag, and deletes or optionally retains the cluster. Those resolved artifacts and `KEEP_E2E_CLUSTER` must become manifest fields.
- [package.json](../package.json) pins Playwright but uses ranges for the Headlamp plugin tool, LangChain, MCP adapters/SDK, provider SDKs, and other dependencies. The package itself is `0.4.0-alpha`. The root [package-lock.json](../package-lock.json) is therefore part of experiment identity, along with package-specific lockfiles and a runtime-resolved inventory.
- [catalog.ts](../packages/ai-common/src/providers/catalog.ts) curates mutable provider model names. [detectProvider.ts](../packages/ai-common/src/providers/detectProvider.ts) can receive Copilot model IDs, names, versions and capability type, but canonical eval results do not yet bind this metadata to requests and responses.
- [ToolStateStore.ts](../packages/ai-common/src/mcp/tools/ToolStateStore.ts) persists tool descriptions and input schemas and can replace them on rediscovery. [MCPClient.ts](../packages/ai-common/src/mcp/langchain/MCPClient.ts) delegates lifecycle/tool adaptation to `@langchain/mcp-adapters`; neither currently emits the complete negotiated protocol/capability/server/tool-contract epoch required by this research.
- No `outputSchema` match was found in the inspected MCP persistence/client surfaces, so a pilot must verify whether the adapter exposes and validates MCP structured output contracts before claiming compatibility.

Keep the present E2E suite as product wiring coverage. Add a release-eval preflight around it rather than pretending its current version prose is a matrix. The first local change should emit `environment-manifest.json` and stop before the build if declared versus observed tool versions disagree. After cluster creation, append server/component versions, discovery/OpenAPI/CRD digests, Headlamp/plugin/build/lockfile/browser identities, MCP contract epochs, and model observations. Use structured command/API output rather than scraping human version text where available.

#### Focused pilot

1. Define a versioned environment-manifest schema and canonical digest. Implement collectors for git/worktree state, host/runtime, npm/lockfile/resolved packages, Playwright browser, Docker/Headlamp image, KWOK/Kubernetes components/discovery/OpenAPI/CRDs, operator status, MCP negotiation/tool contracts, provider response metadata, and telemetry stack.
2. Add declared constraints for Headlamp `v0.43.0`, KWOK `v0.8.0`, Kubernetes, `kubectl`, Node/npm, architecture and browser. Run one known-wrong tool-version control and prove preflight rejects it before building or spending provider tokens.
3. Pin the Kubernetes image/version used by `kwokctl`; record actual API server version and feature gates. Run the current scenario on the oldest/current/newest supported Kubernetes lane selected at freeze time, plus a deprecated-API-disabled canary.
4. Select one representative CRD/operator scenario. Capture chart/operator/operand/CRD/conversion identities, create old-storage objects, exercise served versions, perform the documented migration, and verify semantic round trip, `storedVersions`, observed generation, reference pass and known-bad fail.
5. Qualify Headlamp baseline and next versions against the same production plugin artifact, then qualify baseline and candidate plugin artifacts against both Headlamp versions. This is the local $2 \times 2$ matched matrix.
6. Stand up two MCP contract epochs: unchanged tool behavior with representation-only schema ordering, and one task-relevant required-field/output-schema change. Prove canonical equality accepts the former, rediscovery records a new epoch, and the latter becomes adapter/scenario migration rather than model failure.
7. Run a pinned provider snapshot, an observed moving alias, and an announced replacement where available. Preserve requested/returned model, API/region/deployment, parameters and capabilities; prove alias movement starts a new series.
8. Replay a golden telemetry fixture through baseline and candidate OpenTelemetry Collector/Prometheus cells. Verify raw canonical evidence, transformed schema, PromQL output, alert/rule result and retention; inject one query-semantic incompatibility and prove only observability-dependent scoring becomes invalid.
9. Execute reference, known-bad and candidate repeats in randomized, balanced time blocks across the four matched cells. Trigger one environment-only break, one candidate-only break, one interaction, one secular provider-drift pattern, and one invalid cross cell in synthetic controls; require the classifier to assign the identifiable owner or refuse attribution without score imputation.
10. Exercise case lifecycle with one bridge whose prespecified equivalence interval passes, one whose ordinary difference test is non-significant but equivalence remains inconclusive, one inaccessible historical model freeze, and one semantically invalid API retirement. Require only the first bridge to join a measurement series, and reconstruct original and current denominators from append-only records.

The pilot succeeds only if every run has a closed resolvable manifest; unsupported and unresolved cells stop before candidate scoring; setup/reference/grader/verifier/cleanup controls separate compatibility from quality; synthetic candidate, environment, and interaction failures are attributed correctly while drift and invalid cells prevent overclaiming; CRD and MCP contract changes create explicit epochs; model alias movement cannot masquerade as a fixed snapshot; telemetry incompatibility is localized; equivalence and inconclusive bridges lead to different lifecycle decisions; and scenario migration/freeze/retirement preserve historical results. Passing one “latest” stack is not success.
